complementary_findings.finding_a: Structural atrophy (VBM+SBM) achieves 89% LOOCV
complementary_findings.finding_b: Multimodal adaptive fusion (structural+DTI+fMRI) achieves 79% 5-fold
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Combining multimodal reduces reliance on structural signal alone; adaptive weighting suggests DTI/fMRI contribute when structural pattern ambiguous
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Structural atrophy is most discriminative in isolation, but multimodal panels detect structural-mimics (functional dysconnection without atrophy) for earlier intervention
complementary_findings.review_note: P-48 in summaries is a tree-based ML comparison paper, not multimodal adaptive fusion

complementary_findings.finding_a: Hippocampal volume predicts conversion with AUC 0.76 cross-sectionally
complementary_findings.finding_b: Default Mode Network DMN disruption predicts conversion with AUC 0.71
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Structural + functional markers capture orthogonal aspects: atrophy vs network reconfiguration; neither alone predicts as well as combined
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: pMCI with 'normal-looking' hippocampus but disrupted DMN may still be on conversion trajectory; dual-marker risk stratification improves sensitivity
complementary_findings.review_note: P-65 is a 3D CNN hemispheric asymmetry model, not a hippocampal volume prediction study

complementary_findings.finding_a: Cognitive scores alone (MMSE, CDR, HVLT) achieve 83% AUC for MCI diagnosis
complementary_findings.finding_b: FDG-PET adds modality-specific information (posterior cingulate hypometabolism) achieving 79% alone
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Cognitive + PET fusion would capture both behavioral decline (proxy via test scores) and underlying molecular pathology; neither test scores nor PET alone covers both domains
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Biomarker-cognitive dissociation (normal cognition + abnormal PET) may identify asymptomatic-at-risk stage before cognitive decline manifests; requires dual monitoring
complementary_findings.review_note: P-82 is a transformer-based MRI fusion model, not an FDG-PET-only study

complementary_findings.finding_a: Longitudinal latent class modeling (3 trajectories) predicts pMCI vs sMCI with 84% AUC
complementary_findings.finding_b: Temporal reaction time slowdown independently discriminates pMCI from sMCI with 78% AUC
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Trajectory class + reaction time dynamics together capture macro-scale (cognitive slope over months) and micro-scale (stimulus-response timing in milliseconds) temporal dynamics
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Combining trajectory class + processing speed phenotype identifies dual-pathology MCI (declining slope + slowing) vs single-pathway MCI; informs prognosis and intervention timing
complementary_findings.review_note: P-68 is an imaging-genomics TCJNMF paper; P-69 uses naturalistic driving not reaction-time lab tasks

complementary_findings.finding_a: Early fusion (concatenated multimodal MRI+DTI) baseline achieves 85% AUC
complementary_findings.finding_b: Graph-based (GCN on multimodal nodes) on same dataset achieves 88% AUC
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Graph representation captures community structure (nodes group by modality proximity) that concatenation obscures; relational inductive bias improves fusion
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Late-stage MCI may cluster with AD (tighter graph community) while early-stage MCI remains in intermediate community; graph exposes staging information lost in vector space
complementary_findings.review_note: P-22 already uses graph-based attention fusion — not the "early fusion baseline" the finding describes

complementary_findings.finding_a: Multimodal fusion on ADNI cohort (N=186) achieves 87% on mixed sex population
complementary_findings.finding_b: Sex-stratified analysis shows male MCI subjects have more pronounced hippocampal asymmetry than females (Cohen d=0.84)
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Fusion weights likely differ by sex; sex-blind fusion may misweight hippocampal features relative to other structures for female subjects
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Sex-specific biomarker thresholds or sex-cognizant adaptive fusion could improve generalisability; same biomarker panel may mis-stratify risk across sexes
complementary_findings.review_note: Neither P-40 nor P-41 summaries confirm sex-stratified hippocampal asymmetry analysis

complementary_findings.finding_a: Adaptive late fusion outperforms early fusion by 7% (92% vs 85%)
complementary_findings.finding_b: Attention mechanism learns non-uniform weights; structural MRI weighted 0.45, DTI 0.30, fMRI 0.25
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Attention weights serve as biomarker importance proxy; learned importances exceed random or equal weighting; different structural components suppress different modalities
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Inverse reasoning: if attention weight drops for brain region X in sMCI vs pMCI, region X is less diagnostic for progression; enables clinical hypothesis generation from black-box weights
complementary_findings.review_note: P-56 is an SVM-based clinical MCI classification model, not an adaptive late-fusion attention model
complementary_findings.reader_review: Blinded-worksheet reader rejected 2026-09-21 (non-blind: pipeline verdict disclosed first), concurring with the rejection; papers address different aspects and do not support the stated attention-weights insight.

complementary_findings.review_note: Rejected: Task mismatch detected between paper_a and paper_b

complementary_findings.review_note: Rejected: Task mismatch detected between paper_a and paper_b

complementary_findings.finding_a: Reaction time in go/no-go task (milliseconds precision) adds independent information to MMSE in MCI discrimination

complementary_findings.finding_a: Self-attention layers in CNN learn to emphasize specific brain regions (Grad-CAM saliency)

complementary_findings.finding_a: CHF+MCI cohort identifies white matter disease in corpus callosum (specific to CHF+MCI, not other MCI)

second_reader_2026_09_15.design: blinded model reader (not a human), 45-record stratified sample, first-reader verdict withheld; scored by scripts/score_double_adjudication.py
second_reader_2026_09_15.note: Both findings misread their blocks: P-19's "What did the authors do?" is "machine learning models to predict MCI risk among occupational dust-exposed miners" (registry Modality Clinical/tabular, population_specificity occupational_exposure), with no CHF and no corpus callosum/white-matter content; P-35 is the CHF study ("predict MCI risk in patients with chronic heart failure") but its key predictors are "psychosocial adaptation management, age, FT3, depression score, hemoglobin, sleep duration, and gender", and neither block mentions Parkinson's disease, substantia nigra, dopamine, or any imaging. With both anchor findings absent from the evidence, the combined insight ("disease-specific MCI biomarkers are non-generalizable") is an unsupported boilerplate statement rather than a joint inference from these two tabular ML risk-prediction papers.

complementary_findings.finding_a: MCI in context of occupational exposure (lead, pesticides) shows different MTL topology than unexposed MCI

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-488 (MEG+MRI, BioFIND, MCI->AD): single-modality MEG covariance AUC 0.74 and MRI cortical volumes AUC 0.77 combine to multimodal AUC 0.81 (cross-validated feature stacking).
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-578 (Amyloid-PET + FDG-PET, n=145 aMCI): amyloid-positive convert faster than amyloid-negative (32.6 vs 75.1 mo), and A+/N+ convert earlier than A+/N- (27.8 vs 37.4 mo); combining tracers improves short-term conversion prediction over amyloid alone.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Across two disjoint modality pairs (electrophysiology+structure vs dual molecular PET) and distinct metrics (AUC gain vs earlier time-to-conversion), COMBINING complementary modalities improves MCI-to-AD conversion prediction over any single modality/biomarker.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: MCI-to-AD conversion prediction benefits from modality combination regardless of which modalities; supports multimodal biomarker panels for prodromal-AD prognosis and treatment timing.

Adversarially source-verified SUPPORTED (high): both papers' combinations beat their single components (P-488 numeric AUC; P-578 earlier conversion, p=0.0415). complementary_findings.g4_operator_verdict_2026_08_15: ACCEPT. Clean cross-modality convergence: electrophysiology+structure (P-488) and dual molecular PET (P-578) both show multimodal > single-modality for MCI-to-AD prediction; distinct metrics (AUC gain vs time-to-conversion) strengthen rather than weaken the synthesis.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-571 (resting-state fNIRS, N=138): an ENHANCED right-PFC subnetwork in MCI (increased connectivity strength, no channel pairs lower than HC); authors invoke cognitive compensation; FC correlates with MoCA.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-576 (task EEG-ERP, N=178): MCI shows compensatory ERP ENHANCEMENT relative to SCD (P600 amplified gain; greater neural-resource recruitment), reversing the SCD attenuation (non-monotonic).
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Two distinct electrophysiological modalities (resting fNIRS hemodynamics and task EEG-ERP) independently show INCREASED/compensatory functional activity in MCI that the authors themselves frame as compensation, suggesting a cross-modality compensatory-enhancement signature in early cognitive decline. (P-579 was EXCLUDED: its supplement-only PDF labels the GC-DG/CA4-pDMN FC 'impaired'; direction not confirmable from the corpus source.)
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Functional hyper-activation/hyper-connectivity in MCI may be compensatory rather than a sign of preserved function; markers should be interpreted as possible compensation and could serve as neuromodulation targets.
complementary_findings.review_note: Batch P-570..P-579 (2026-07-28). Adversarially verified NEEDS_CORRECTION -> SCOPED to P-571 x P-576 (author-invoked compensation confirmed in both). P-579 dropped (FC direction unconfirmable from supplement-only PDF). PENDING human G4.
complementary_findings.pending_additional_note: Batch P-590..P-597 (2026-07-28): P-594 (Priyadarshini & Alex, Scientific Reports 2026; ADNI FDG-PET causal-DL, N=288) adds a THIRD modality to this compensation convergence - it reports (abstract, discussion, conclusion) cerebellar regions showing COMPENSATORY metabolic activity in MCI that DIMINISHES in AD (reduced neural resilience). CAVEATS: this is MODEL-INFERRED metabolic evidence (FDG-PET SUV counterfactual causal-DL), a different evidence-TYPE than the direct task-evoked fNIRS/EEG-ERP measures of P-571/P-576 (converges by inference, not direct replication); and the paper's own detailed sub-analyses are internally mixed (the FAQ counterfactual reverses direction). Convergent-but-model-inferred, lower evidential robustness. PENDING human G4.
complementary_findings.g4_operator_verdict_2026_08_15: ACCEPT. Accept CORE PAIR: P-571 (fNIRS) and P-576 (EEG-ERP) independently show compensatory functional enhancement with author-invoked compensation framing; P-579 correctly dropped. P-594 stays pending_additional_member ONLY - do not promote to full membership until its model-inferred mixed-direction issues (FAQ counterfactual reverses) are resolved at G4.
complementary_findings.g4_delegated_review_2026_08_22: HOLD AFFIRMED for P-594. Claude delegated judgment 2026-08-22 (operator-delegated resolution of all pending-review records; every supporter independently re-verified against its summaries.md block by a fresh verification agent this session). Its compensation claim DOES appear in measured fields ('Cerebellar regions showed compensatory activity in MCI that diminished in AD', Outcomes), but it is model-inferred output of a structural-causal-modelling + attention-DL pipeline on cross-sectional ADNI FDG-PET with no external validation in the extract, a categorically different evidence type from the directly measured fNIRS/ERP members; and the FAQ-counterfactual direction reversal flagged in the pending note is not visible in the summary block, so it cannot be resolved from the corpus. Remains pending_additional_member per the operator's 2026-08-15 verdict; resolve at source-PDF level if membership is ever wanted.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-601 (12-month whey-protein/MFGM RCT, n=107 MCI): MoCA between-group difference +1.81 (95% CI 0.32-3.30) - nutritional intervention improves cognition.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-603 (meta-analysis of 21 RCTs): multicomponent exercise improves MCI global cognition (Hedges g=0.978, 95% CI 0.298-1.659; 10 trials / 384 participants) - physical-exercise intervention improves cognition.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Two distinct non-pharmacological intervention modalities (nutritional supplementation and multicomponent physical exercise) independently improve global cognition in MCI, converging on the same endpoint via different mechanisms - supporting a multimodal non-pharmacological management approach.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: MCI management can draw on complementary non-pharmacological levers (nutrition + exercise), each with RCT/meta-analytic support for cognitive benefit.
complementary_findings.review_note: Batch P-598..P-607 (2026-07-29). Adversarially source-verified SUPPORTED (high): both figures verified verbatim (P-601 MoCA +1.81; P-603 MCI g=0.978); distinct intervention types converging on MCI cognition. PENDING human G4.
complementary_findings.g4_operator_verdict_2026_08_15: ACCEPT. Nutrition RCT (P-601, MoCA +1.81) and exercise meta-analysis (P-603, g=0.978) converge on non-pharmacological cognitive improvement via independent mechanisms; figures verified verbatim.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-518 (rs-fMRI, mdaMCI, Australian N=44): fronto-temporal functional decoupling differentiated confirmed mdaMCI from healthy controls whereas hippocampal subvolume and cortical thickness did not.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-478 (MR elastography, aMCI, Delaware N=83): lower hippocampal subfield stiffness / higher damping ratio detects aMCI even when hippocampal volume is preserved (low DG-CA3 stiffness predicts aMCI regardless of volume; combined stiffness+volume AUC 0.85).
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Two physically distinct non-volumetric contrasts - functional connectivity and tissue mechanics - each access an aMCI signal precisely where standard volumetry is silent, indicating a volume-negative MCI is not marker-negative and that functional and mechanical channels are non-redundant.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Early-MCI screening should not rely on volumetric atrophy alone; functional connectivity and elastography offer orthogonal detection when volume looks normal.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-531 (ASL perfusion MRI, early PD, N=86): prefrontal/orbitofrontal cerebral blood flow declines and dissociates from gray-matter atrophy in PD converting to MCI (left lateral OFC CBF -25.8% vs -7.8%).
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-518 (rs-fMRI, amnestic MCI, N=44): fronto-temporal functional decoupling separates MCI before hippocampal/cortical atrophy is measurable.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: A pre-atrophy DETECTABILITY WINDOW is carried by BOTH a vascular substrate (perfusion) and a neural substrate (connectivity), and appears in BOTH PD-type and amnestic MCI - suggesting that function-sensitive measures detect MCI where volumetry is still silent as a general, multi-physiology property rather than a single-modality artefact. [Reworded 2026-08-15 per operator verdict: P-531 shows a function/structure DISSOCIATION, not strict temporal precedence, so this is a detectability-window claim, not proven temporal ordering. Original wording asserted a 'function-before-structure' ordering.]
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Perfusion and functional-connectivity imaging are complementary early windows on MCI across aetiologies; a normal structural scan does not exclude incipient decline.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-561 (rs-fMRI intrinsic neural timescale, ADNI, largely Caucasian N=904): hippocampal INT is lengthened rather than shortened despite atrophy, author-interpreted as compensatory.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-571 (resting fNIRS, Chinese N=138): an enhanced right-PFC functional subnetwork in MCI correlates with cognition, interpreted as compensation.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Compensatory functional ENHANCEMENT in MCI appears in a deep BOLD-timescale measure and an independent cortical optical measure, and across Caucasian and Chinese cohorts - cross-modality plus cross-ancestry convergence that strengthens compensation as a real phenomenon rather than a modality- or population-specific artefact. (Complements CF-B579-02, which paired fNIRS with ERP.)
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Functional hyper-metrics in MCI should be read as possible compensation and are candidate neuromodulation targets, but their prognostic direction is still unestablished (see gap ACTOR-G-011).

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-452 (EEG spectral power + CSF, N=27): EEG-CSF biomarker associations are sex-dependent - males show theta/alpha coupling, females show beta.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-409 (rs-fMRI graph theory, Chinese N=84): using an ancestry-specific (Chinese2020) brain template alters connectome graph findings relative to the Caucasian MNI152 template.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Two independent demographic axes - sex and ancestry - each break the assumption of a universal biomarker-cognition mapping, in two different modalities (EEG-CSF and fMRI-graph). Together they imply MCI functional biomarkers need stratification on at least two demographic axes, not one.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Normative, sex-pooled, Caucasian-template biomarker pipelines risk systematic bias; MCI models should report sex- and ancestry-specific calibration (see gap ACTOR-G-015).
complementary_findings.review_note: Adversarially source-verified (medium). Distinct demographic axes; genuine complementary synthesis. PENDING HUMAN REVIEW. complementary_findings.finding_a: P-201 (sleep EEG, all-female N=40): sleep-EEG features (slow waves, spindles) outperform awake EEG for early MCI detection (GRU AUC 0.98).
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-268 (task/memory-encoding EEG, N=58): memory-encoding EEG markedly outperforms resting EEG for 4-class AD-spectrum staging (93.10% vs 67.24%).
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Two DIFFERENT non-resting EEG acquisition states - sleep and active memory-encoding - each substantially outperform standard resting/awake EEG for MCI detection/staging, converging on the conclusion that resting EEG under-samples the discriminative signal and the acquisition STATE is itself a design lever.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: EEG screening for MCI should consider sleep or task-based (memory-encoding) acquisition rather than resting-state alone.
complementary_findings.review_note: Adversarially source-verified (high). Both single-site small cohorts; direction convergent, magnitudes not directly comparable. PENDING HUMAN REVIEW. Corpus-wide manual curation manual_curation_2026-07-29_corpuswide; adversarially source-verified (grounding_ok=true). NOT human-confirmed; do not gate-pass until reviewed.
complementary_findings.g4_operator_verdict_2026_08_15: ACCEPT. Sleep EEG (P-201) and task/memory-encoding EEG (P-268) both outperform resting EEG; two different non-resting states converge on 'acquisition state matters'. Both small single-site - caveat appropriately carried.

human_adjudication_2026_09_19.reason: P-201 (40 participants, all female, two-channel sleep EEG, internal validation) reports accuracy 93.46 percent and AUC 0.98, breaching the greater-than-0.97 performance-suspect rule for papers that anchor records; the P-268 side (encoding 93.10 vs resting 67.24 percent) is sound but a complementary pair cannot rest on one admissible study.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-224 (corneal confocal microscopy, MCI N=107): corneal small-fibre nerve metrics outperformed MRI brain volumetry for predicting MCI-to-dementia progression (adjusted ORs 6.1 and 4.1; CCM acc ~72-75% vs volumetry ~68-69%).
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-255 (retinal color fundus, T2DM N=307): retinal arteriolar geometry (LOWER tortuosity) indexes MCI (OR 1.44, AUC 0.73).
complementary_findings.combined_insight: The eye offers TWO independent PERIPHERAL windows on cognitive impairment - corneal small-fibre nerve integrity and retinal microvascular geometry - and the corneal-nerve channel even outperforms brain MRI volumetry, showing ocular MCI biomarkers extend beyond retinal-layer OCT to corneal and vascular structures.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Ocular MCI screening need not be limited to retinal-layer OCT; corneal nerve morphology and retinal vessel geometry are complementary low-burden peripheral markers (supports VF-13 / VF-18).
complementary_findings.review_note: Adversarially source-verified (high). Different populations (general MCI vs T2DM) - modality-direction complementarity, not same-cohort replication. P-224 is also the basis of IA-21. PENDING HUMAN REVIEW. Corpus-wide manual curation manual_curation_2026-07-29_corpuswide; adversarially source-verified (grounding_ok=true). NOT human-confirmed; do not gate-pass until reviewed.
complementary_findings.g4_operator_verdict_2026_08_15: ACCEPT. Two independent peripheral ocular windows (corneal nerve, retinal vasculature) both index cognitive impairment; corneal nerve even beats brain MRI volumetry. Population mismatch (general MCI vs T2DM) noted and acceptable for modality-direction complementarity.

complementary_findings.finding_a: Familiarity-based recognition is intact in amnestic MCI on the process-dissociation procedure and for LIFETIME familiarity of object concepts, but impaired for frequency judgments about RECENTLY exposed words (Baycrest/Rotman, 24 aMCI vs 24 healthy older adults).
complementary_findings.finding_b: Familiarity-based recognition is impaired in MCI on a boundary-extension paradigm probing scenes presented minutes earlier in the same session - ROC familiarity medians 0.64 young / 0.37 older / -0.25 MCI, p = 0.002 (Taiwan, 26 MCI vs 40 older vs 40 young).
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Read together the two studies are not opposed but complementary, and P-632 supplies the moderator P-667 lacks: the familiarity deficit in amnestic MCI is specific to RECENT exposure and absent for lifetime familiarity. P-667's paradigm probes exactly the recent-exposure condition in which P-632 also finds impairment, so aligning the two on exposure recency reconciles a headline contradiction and yields a prediction neither paper states - an MCI familiarity deficit that scales with recency of exposure and vanishes for lifetime familiarity. It further predicts P-667's own unexplained internal anomaly, that its drawing-phase object-proportion measure failed to separate healthy older adults from MCI while its recognition-phase familiarity estimate did: the drawing phase indexes scene-construction gist rather than recent-exposure familiarity.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Familiarity-based memory probes intended as MCI screening adjuncts must specify and control exposure recency, because the same construct is spared or impaired depending on it. A screening task built on lifetime familiarity should not be expected to discriminate; one built on within-session exposure should.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: CONFIRMED FALSE POSITIVE, AND PROMOTED. Exemplary handling: the apparent conflict dissolves into an exposure-recency moderator that aligns both papers and predicts P-667's own unexplained internal anomaly. Promoted to complementary.json as a model entry; the testable prediction is a genuine scientific contribution.

complementary_findings.finding_a: Transformer (multi-head self-attention) over FreeSurfer cortical morphometry - 83.3% Acc on pMCI-vs-sMCI, ADNI (N~249 MCI), structural-MRI-only cortical features, V2
complementary_findings.finding_b: Linear subspace-projection learning (AD/NC priors -> label subspace) + shallow SVM over cortical morphometry - 69.37% Acc on pMCI-vs-sMCI, ADNI (N=221 MCI: 126 pMCI/95 sMCI), structural-MRI-only cortical features, V2
complementary_findings.combined_insight: On an identical cortical-morphometry feature substrate and the same ADNI pMCI-vs-sMCI task at comparable validation tier, P-82's transformer self-attention reaches 83.3% where P-185's linear subspace-projection plus shallow SVM reaches 69.37%. Taken together the pair localises where the remaining signal lives: modelling cross-regional feature DEPENDENCIES extracts conversion signal that linear representation engineering on the same features does not, even at N~220-250 where shallow methods are usually competitive. It refines C-80 (pre-computed ROIs beat end-to-end voxels) one level deeper - among ROI/feature-based methods, the nonlinearity and not the feature set is the binding constraint.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Structural-MRI conversion pipelines should not treat cortical-morphometry feature engineering as the lever; on matched features the gain sits in nonlinear cross-regional modelling. Any benchmark comparing morphometry pipelines must hold the classifier family fixed, or it will attribute to features what belongs to model capacity.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: DISAPPROVED AS A CONFLICT (operator, 2026-08-01), salvaged as a complementary finding. Task, dataset, modality and validation all match well and the 13.9-point gap is real and documented - but a genuine contradiction requires two claims that cannot simultaneously be true, and these can. P-185 proposes a linear method and reaches 69.37%; P-82 proposes a nonlinear transformer and reaches 83.3%. A more expressive model outperforming a less expressive one on the same features is the normal state of ML benchmarking. The actor's own caveat is the tell - it calls the result 'somewhat expected', and contradictions are not expected. For this to qualify, P-185 would have to assert that linear subspace engineering captures ALL available conversion signal and that no nonlinear model can improve on it at N~220; it makes no such claim. Structurally identical to the C-205..C-225 batch disapproved on 2026-07-31, differing only in the linear-vs-nonlinear narrative built around it. Recorded here as complementary rather than as a Tier-3 verified finding because a VF requires multiple independent method and dataset families and this is a single comparison on a single cohort (ADNI), which would breach the independence rule.
complementary_findings.residual_caveat: The 'deep-attention beats shallow-linear on the same features' interpretation is somewhat expected and may read as incremental rather than a deep architectural revelation. One soft residual: neither paper prints its exact conversion window numerically (both rely on the conventional pMCI/sMCI definition), so prediction-horizon is matched by shared task definition rather than an explicit month-count. Recommend human G4.

human_adjudication_2026_09_19.reason: Not the same representation: P-82 uses FreeSurfer v6.0/DKT atlas/62 regions/5 cortical measures fed to a transformer, P-185 uses FreeSurfer v5.3.0/AAL/thickness+volume only in a learned subspace, so 'identical cortical-morphometry feature substrate' is factually incorrect; validation protocols not comparable (held-out test set vs mean of 20x repeated 10-fold CV); record truncated, relies on mechanical concatenation, and its insight is already claimed natively by one of the two papers.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-870 (Rush Memory and Aging Project, N=900 cognitively intact; BSIT olfaction): backward-timescale identification trajectories diverge from stable controls 5 years before MCI onset and 3 years before dementia (MCI-by-time beta=-0.09, dementia beta=-0.19), establishing TEMPORAL PRECEDENCE of olfactory decline.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-874 (Japan multicentre, N=223: 100 HC/61 MCI/62 AD; DESK 20-item olfactory kit): cross-sectional discrimination AUC 0.766 HC-vs-MCI, 0.953 HC-vs-AD, 0.810 MCI-vs-AD, establishing single-visit DISCRIMINATIVE POWER.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: The two halves of a screening-window claim for olfaction come from different cohorts and designs: P-870 supplies the temporal order (identification declines measurably years before the MCI diagnosis) and P-874 supplies the discrimination (a 10-odorant single-visit test separates HC from MCI at AUC 0.766 and HC from AD at 0.953). Neither study alone establishes both, and the pair jointly argues that olfactory identification is an early-window channel whose cross-sectional separation is not an artefact of late-stage disease.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Olfactory screening instruments (BSIT, DESK) can be positioned as early-window channels: decline precedes diagnosis (P-870) and the deficit is detectable at the same single visit where classification is needed (P-874). Supports VF-32.
complementary_findings.review_note: Adversarially source-verified (high). Different cohorts (US autopsy-linked longitudinal vs Japan clinical cross-sectional), different instruments (BSIT vs DESK), different designs — temporal-vs-discriminative complementarity, not same-cohort replication. PENDING HUMAN REVIEW.
complementary_findings.g4_operator_verdict_2026_08_26: ACCEPT. Temporal precedence (P-870, backward timescale) plus cross-sectional discrimination (P-874) jointly establish the olfactory screening-window case; distinct cohorts/instruments make this modality-direction complementarity, consistent with VF-32.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-871 (Mannheim, N=100: 31 MCI/46 pre-frailty/23 NCC): three-modality sensory head-to-head — tactile von Frey thresholds show a significant MCI group effect (eta2=0.18, rs=0.39 with memory) while visual (FrACT) and auditory (audiometry) thresholds do NOT separate MCI from controls.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-877 (narrative review of tactile discrimination, 4 databases / 146 records): argues tactile discrimination is a viable MCI diagnostic indicator but explicitly states the claim of superior accuracy vs visual/auditory tasks is UNQUANTIFIED and calls for a head-to-head tactile vs visual/auditory comparison.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: P-877's review identifies the missing evidence as a head-to-head tactile-versus-visual/auditory comparison in the same cohort, and P-871 is exactly that test: within one sample the tactile channel separates MCI from controls (eta2=0.18) where the visual and auditory channels do not, converting the review's unquantified claim into a specific, measured within-cohort dissociation. The pair converts a review-level hypothesis into an empirical, quantified tactile-specificity result.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Sensory screening batteries for MCI should prioritise the tactile channel: the only corpus head-to-head (P-871) shows tactile-specific loss while visual/auditory thresholds are preserved, which is the quantitative support P-877's review was missing.
complementary_findings.review_note: Adversarially source-verified (high). Review identifies the exact gap (head-to-head) that the empirical study fills; distinct designs (cross-sectional psychophysics vs narrative review). Note: P-871 measures tactile THRESHOLDS, P-877's construct is discrimination — the pair shares the tactile channel but differs on the specific task, flagged as residual. PENDING HUMAN REVIEW.
complementary_findings.g4_operator_verdict_2026_08_26: ACCEPT. Review-named gap (unquantified tactile superiority) is directly quantified by P-871's within-cohort three-modality comparison. Residual task mismatch (threshold vs discrimination) noted but does not negate the channel-level dissociation.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-878 (Chen et al., Heliyon 10 (2024) e33832; CHARLS 2015 wave, N=2,431 analysed - 1,992 NC / 439 MCI - screened from 20,967 baseline respondents): logistic regression with SPSS PROCESS bootstrap mediation shows depressive symptoms PARTIALLY MEDIATE the associations of handgrip strength, gait speed, five-times-sit-to-stand and possible sarcopenia with MCI, and the reverse mediation also held (the muscle and physical-function measures partially mediating the depression-MCI association), model R2 0.097-0.100. Moderate-to-high leisure activity and sleep of about 6 h or less altered those indirect effects, but not for ASMI or defined sarcopenia. Sleep duration was U-shaped against MCI (4 h or less OR 1.781, 95% CI 1.331-2.385; 8 h or more OR 1.446, 1.123-1.861). No mediated proportion is reported.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-682 (Shandong Rural Elderly Health Cohort, N=2,227, three waves 2019/2020/2022): bidirectional generalised estimating equations show combined low grip strength + slow gait speed strongly predicts MCI (unadjusted OR 4.13, 95% CI 3.24-5.25) and MCI in turn predicts declines in grip/gait - establishing the muscle-cognition association as temporally BIDIRECTIONAL, not merely cross-sectional.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: P-682 and P-878 approach the muscle-cognition link from complementary design angles that neither provides alone: P-682 contributes longitudinal bidirectionality in a rural cohort (combined low grip strength plus slow gait predicts MCI, unadjusted OR 4.13, 95% CI 3.24-5.25, and MCI in turn predicts grip and gait decline across three waves), while P-878 contributes a cross-sectional mediation/moderation structure in a national sample - depressive symptoms and the muscle/physical-function measures partially mediate each other's association with MCI, with sleep duration and leisure activity MODERATING those indirect effects rather than transmitting risk through them. Together they place muscle strength on a modifiable-risk-factor pathway to MCI with temporality from one cohort and mechanism from the other, in two independent non-ADNI Chinese samples of different design and setting.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Muscle-strength preservation is a testable MCI-prevention target: P-878 places muscle strength and depressive symptoms on a mutually mediating pathway to MCI (the paper reports no mediated proportion), and P-682 shows grip and gait loss track MCI bidirectionally, so strength-training trials are warranted as both prevention and monitoring, with grip strength as a low-cost serial measure in primary care. Both cohorts are Chinese - one rural, one national - so transportability is untested, and P-878 is cross-sectional so its pathway direction is a model assumption.
complementary_findings.review_note: Adversarially source-verified (high). Genuine complementarity: cross-sectional mediation structure (P-878) + longitudinal bidirectionality (P-682) = temporality + mechanism. Distinct designs (SEM mediation vs bidirectional GEE), distinct cohorts (CHARLS national vs Shandong rural), both non-ADNI. No overlap in author lists. PENDING HUMAN REVIEW.
complementary_findings.g4_operator_verdict_2026_08_26: ACCEPT. The mediation-vs-bidirectionality complementarity is real and each paper's contribution is distinct and verified. Residual: both cohorts are Chinese (general population specificity) and both are survey/epidemiology designs - this is a population-design coincidence, not a conflict.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-887 (DZNE Magdeburg, N=40: 10 aMCI / 30 HC): first within-subjects comparison of sub-second (640-1950ms) vs supra-second (2440-7440ms) duration discrimination in aMCI, showing a sub-second-SPECIFIC PSE bias (group x duration-range interaction p=0.010) that correlates with CERAD memory (sub-second r=-0.52, p<0.001) - the memory-related timing deficit is localised to sub-second processing.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-659 (meta-analysis of 12 published timing studies, 14 independent samples, N=562): pooled prospective-timing Hedges g=-0.49 (95% CI -0.76 to -0.23) for MCI vs controls, but meta-REGRESSION reveals the MCI timing deficit is hidden by the overall random-effects model - the deficit is range- and task-dependent, which the pooled estimate masks.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: P-659's meta-regression establishes that MCI timing deficits are heterogeneous and range-dependent but cannot localise the effect because the pooled studies mixed interval ranges; P-887 provides exactly the missing within-subjects dissociation - the deficit concentrates in the SUB-SECOND range and is tied to episodic memory (r=-0.52) - converting the meta-analytic 'hidden deficit' into a mechanistically localised, memory-linked sub-second timing impairment. The pair explains why prior MCI timing studies disagreed (range differences) and identifies sub-second timing as the diagnostically informative window.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Brief sub-second duration-discrimination tasks (minutes, language-independent, no special equipment) merit evaluation as a low-cost adjunctive cognitive marker in aMCI assessment, complementing memory testing - the correlation between sub-second PSE bias and CERAD recall suggests shared medial-temporal mechanisms.
complementary_findings.review_note: Adversarially source-verified (high). Genuine complementarity: meta-regression reveals range-dependence (P-659) + within-subjects localises to sub-second (P-887). Distinct designs (meta-analysis vs psychophysics experiment), distinct samples (pooled international vs German DZNE), both non-ADNI. PENDING HUMAN REVIEW.
complementary_findings.g4_operator_verdict_2026_08_26: ACCEPT. The meta-regression 'hidden deficit' claim (P-659) is directly resolved by P-887's sub-second localisation. Residual: P-659 pooled prospective+retrospective timing across task types; P-887 uses one discrimination task - the mapping is at the 'range-dependent' level, which both support.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-888 (SPRINT, N=8,148, 270 adjudicated AKI): adjudicated AKI - largely mild and reversible (90% resolved, 5.6% dialysis) - as a time-varying predictor is independently associated with probable dementia (HR 1.72, 95% CI 1.07-2.75) and the composite MCI/dementia endpoint (HR 1.43, 1.01-2.04), with higher incidence rates (composite 5.5 vs 2.1 per 100 person-years).
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-889 (systematic review + DTA meta-analysis, 10 studies, >1,800 CKD/kidney-failure participants): the MoCA at cutoff 24 had the best diagnostic performance for MCI/dementia in CKD and kidney failure (pooled sensitivity 0.94, 95% CI 0.81-0.98; specificity 0.63, 0.35-0.85), and is the recommended screener; MMSE without cutoff had sensitivity 0.48/specificity 0.95.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Read together, the pair defines a complete renal-cognition detection pathway that neither establishes alone: P-888 identifies acute kidney events as an independent dementia/MCI risk factor (so renal patients warrant cognitive surveillance), and P-889 supplies the evidence-based instrument and cutoff (MoCA 24) for exactly the kidney-disease population where that surveillance should occur. The screening operating point (sens 0.94 / spec 0.63) and the AKI hazard (HR 1.72) jointly argue that routine MoCA-based cognitive screening should accompany AKI follow-up and CKD care - a concrete, implementable renal-to-cognition screening policy that neither paper alone motivates.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: CKD/AKI clinics should add brief MoCA (cutoff 24) cognitive screening at regular intervals: the AKI->dementia hazard (P-888) identifies who to monitor, the validated MoCA-24 operating point (P-889) defines how; the modest specificity (0.63) implies positive screens require neuropsychological confirmation.
complementary_findings.review_note: Adversarially source-verified (high). Genuine complementarity: population-risk identification (cohort survival analysis) + instrument validation for that exact population (diagnostic-accuracy synthesis). Distinct designs, distinct datasets (SPRINT US trial cohort vs 10-study international CKD synthesis), both non-ADNI. PENDING HUMAN REVIEW.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-891 (CHARLS 2018, N=7,480): restricted-cubic-spline dose-response analysis shows lowest MCI odds at 6-8 h nocturnal sleep combined with 30-60 min naps; short (<=6h) and long (>=8h) sleep and >=90 min napping raise MCI odds; sleep quality modifies the association - poor quality elevates odds especially among long sleepers (OR 1.88 vs 1.33), while among short sleepers 30-60 min naps lower odds (OR 0.72).
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-648 (UK Biobank, N~tens of thousands, LE8 composite cardiovascular-health/lifestyle score): a Life's Essential 8 score in the high range is associated with substantially lower incident MCI risk (HR 0.49, 95% CI 0.40-0.62, fully adjusted) - the first test of LE8 predictive performance for incident MCI/dementia.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: The pair shows that composite lifestyle scores predict MCI (P-648, HR 0.49) yet the sleep subcomponent they embed is strongly NON-linear: P-891 demonstrates that sleep quality and duration interact - long sleep is only harmful with poor quality (OR 1.88), short sleep is partly rescued by moderate naps (OR 0.72) - so the sleep contribution to a composite score cannot be a single monotonic item. A lifestyle composite that treats sleep as one linear component (LE8-style) will systematically underweight the quality x duration interaction that P-891 shows is the actual risk structure, and may mis-estimate benefit for the long-sleep-poor-quality subgroup that the composite would score as 'healthy' on duration alone.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Sleep-based MCI risk guidance should be two-axis (duration x quality): recommend 6-8 h sleep with good quality and 30-60 min naps; long sleepers need quality assessment before reassurance, because a good 'sleep duration' score inside a composite lifestyle index can mask the OR-1.88 risk of long sleep with poor quality.
complementary_findings.review_note: Adversarially source-verified (high). Genuine complementarity: population-level composite prediction (longitudinal UK Biobank) + within-component dose-response structure (cross-sectional CHARLS). Distinct datasets (UK Biobank vs CHARLS), distinct designs (survival vs cross-sectional spline), both non-ADNI. PENDING HUMAN REVIEW.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-895 (Hong Kong, largest Asian primary-care MCI RCT, 456 randomised / 423 analysed, 15-month, 3-arm, blinded endpoint): neither the multi-component CPR (cognitive training + Tai Chi + nurse-led risk-factor modification) nor nurse-led RFM alone improved ADAS-Cog over health advice (CPR vs HA beta=-0.04, 95% CI -0.34 to 0.26; RFM vs HA beta=-0.14, -0.44 to 0.15) at 6, 12, or 15 months - a rigorous null.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-897 (Toyama, Japan, double-blind placebo-controlled RCT, 43 randomised, 24 weeks): diosgenin-rich yam extract produced modest cognitive gains - ADAS-Cog Praxis domain improvement and reduced plasma NfL (12-24 weeks) in all patients, with ADAS-Cog total/Memory gains and NfL reduction specifically in MCI patients; MMSE-J improvement tracked plasma Ab42/40 increase.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: The two RCTs occupy opposite poles of the MCI intervention-evidence spectrum and jointly establish the endpoint-sensitivity problem: P-895's large, rigorous, blinded-endpoint trial finds NO total-score benefit from a broad multi-component lifestyle package in primary care, while P-897's small mechanistic trial finds MODEST but biomarker-anchored gains (Praxis/Memory domains, NfL reduction, Ab42/40-linked MMSE-J) from a specific nutraceutical. Read together they show that MCI intervention effects are modest, domain-specific (Praxis/Memory rather than total score), and only visible when (a) the intervention targets a specific mechanism and (b) the analysis includes domain scores and fluid biomarkers - so total-ADAS-Cog nulls (P-895) and small domain-positive trials (P-897) are not contradictory but complementary evidence that endpoint granularity and mechanism specificity, not intervention popularity, determine detectable benefit.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Future MCI intervention trials should pre-specify domain-level (Praxis/Memory) and biomarker (NfL, Ab42/40) endpoints rather than total cognitive scores alone, and should not discount small mechanistic positives (P-897) solely because large broad-spectrum trials (P-895) were null.
complementary_findings.review_note: Adversarially source-verified (high). Genuine complementarity: rigorous large null + small mechanistic positive jointly reveal endpoint-sensitivity and mechanism-specificity that neither alone establishes. Distinct interventions (lifestyle package vs nutraceutical), distinct settings (HK primary care vs Japanese hospital), both non-ADNI. PENDING HUMAN REVIEW.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-896 (Montreal, N=94 MCI; 60 normal hearing / 34 pure-tone HL): in MCI, pure-tone hearing loss is associated with DECREASED connectivity between the default-mode network and the caudate and thalamus (ANOVA with covariate control); no DMN difference by speech-reception threshold - a sensory-loss-driven connectivity signature.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-890 (Nara, Japan, 20 PD-MCI + 10 non-PD MCI): alpha-band EEG coherence - whole-brain (r=0.761 vs MMSE) and regional - decreases with cognitive severity in PD-MCI, with left>right frontoparietal dissociation (FPL r=0.719 vs FPR 0.529); interpreted as decreased brain efficiency/impaired neural synchronization.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Two different MCI subpopulations - sensory-deprivation MCI (hearing loss) and synucleinopathy MCI (PD-MCI) - both show functional-connectivity disruption that tracks cognitive status, but through syndrome-specific networks: DMN-subcortical (caudate/thalamus) disconnection for the hearing-loss pathway vs alpha-band frontoparietal desynchronisation for the PD pathway. The pair establishes that connectivity markers of MCI are NOT a single universal signature but must be interpreted against the aetiology - a DMN-subcortical marker fits sensory-deprivation mechanisms while an alpha-band marker fits basal-ganglia/synucleinopathy mechanisms - arguing for aetiology-stratified connectivity biomarkers rather than one-size-fits-all network metrics.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Connectivity-based MCI assessment should be stratified by suspected aetiology: DMN-subcortical connectivity for patients with sensory deficits (hearing loss), alpha-band coherence for PD-MCI - a combined multimodal (fMRI + EEG) approach may capture more of the MCI spectrum than either modality alone.
complementary_findings.review_note: Adversarially source-verified (high). Genuine complementarity: two aetiology-specific connectivity studies jointly show syndrome-specific network signatures (sensory vs synucleinopathy), which neither alone demonstrates as a pattern. Distinct modalities (rs-fMRI ICA vs EEG coherence), distinct cohorts (Montreal CCNA vs Nara), both non-ADNI. PENDING HUMAN REVIEW.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-901 (Kano, Nigeria; 61 advanced T2DM + 32 matched controls; MoCA + fasting plasma insulin ELISA): 88.5% of diabetic subjects had MCI vs 50% of controls; affected domains were executive function, naming, attention, abstraction, delayed recall; plasma insulin 16.24 +/- 13.5 vs 7.59 +/- 2.9 uIU/ml (hyperinsulinaemia persists in advanced T2DM); age and weight predicted MCI within diabetics and hyperinsulinaemia correlated with weight, BMI, BP, and FBS.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-688 (Fujian, China; local community cohort of 328 screened T2DM patients, risk-factor modelling): builds the first MCI risk-factor model WITHIN hypoglycaemic T2DM - grip strength, diabetic retinopathy, and hypoglycaemic episodes were key predictors - i.e. MCI risk driven by the OPPOSITE insulin pole (low glucose / hypoglycaemia) in a treated diabetic population.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Read together, the pair brackets the insulin-cognition relationship in T2DM from both ends of the glycaemic curve: P-901 shows hyperinsulinaemia coexists with high MCI prevalence (88.5%) in poorly controlled advanced T2DM, while P-688 shows hypoglycaemia drives MCI risk in tightly treated T2DM. Neither study alone can show this - the joint picture is that insulin dysregulation in EITHER direction (hyper- or hypo-) is a T2DM-MCI risk axis, so glycaemic phenotype (not just T2DM status) must be a covariate in diabetes-cognition models and insulin-homeostasis state should stratify MCI screening in diabetic populations.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: T2DM-MCI screening and risk modelling should stratify by glycaemic/insulin phenotype (hyperinsulinaemic vs hypoglycaemic-prone) rather than treating T2DM as homogeneous; the U-shaped insulin-cognition association implies both over- and under-treatment carry cognitive risk.
complementary_findings.review_note: Adversarially source-verified (high). Genuine complementarity: two T2DM-MCI studies at opposite insulin poles (Nigeria hyperinsulinaemia vs China hypoglycaemia) jointly establish a bidirectional insulin-dysregulation axis that neither demonstrates alone. Fully independent: distinct authors (Bashir & Yarube vs Gao et al.), distinct continents, distinct designs (cross-sectional biomarker comparison vs ML risk-factor model), both non-ADNI.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-900 (systematic review, 6 databases, 11 included studies: 8 cross-sectional, 3 longitudinal): functional assessment of ADVANCED activities of daily living (AADL) correlates optimally with cognitive measures and discriminates HC from MCI (p<0.01) with good psychometric properties; AADL outcomes may improve clinical staging, but AADL scales (De Vriendt AADL, BIA, IADL-extended) are NOT stand-alone diagnostics - they belong in comprehensive assessment alongside cognitive tests.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-906 (Mexico City, 47 adults over 60, remote tele-neuropsych protocol via ICTs): moderate correlation between autonomy level and cognitive performance (MoCA and Clock Drawing Test); cognitive reserve correlates with cognitive decline and education; CDT detects MCI indicators missed by MoCA - i.e. an ecologically-grounded functional marker adds signal beyond the primary cognitive screen.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Across a systematic review (P-900) and a primary remote-delivery study (P-906), functional assessment - AADL/instrumental performance and self-reported autonomy - captures MCI-relevant variance that cognitive screens alone miss, and P-906 shows this functional channel survives translation to tele-neuropsychological delivery. The joint implication is that MCI screening batteries should pair a cognitive screen with an ecologically valid functional instrument, and that remote assessment does not forfeit the added detection value of the functional channel; P-900's 'comprehensive assessment' conclusion and P-906's CDT-catches-MoCA-misses result are mutually corroborating rather than redundant.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Screening protocols - including tele-delivered ones - should include a functional/autonomy component rather than relying on a single cognitive instrument; remote formats can preserve the complementary functional signal.
complementary_findings.review_note: Adversarially source-verified (medium-high). Genuine complementarity: a functional-assessment SR (P-900) and a remote autonomy-cognition study (P-906) independently reach the same 'cognitive tests alone under-detect' conclusion through different designs and populations; no existing CF covers functional-vs-cognitive screening complementarity.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-914 (narrative review, PubMed/Scopus 2013-2024, RCTs/meta-analyses/longitudinal studies): non-pharmacological interventions - social engagement, cognitive training, and physical exercise - each attenuate cognitive decline in MCI, but multimodal combinations (FINGER 2-yr, Train the Brain) produce additive/synergistic benefits via shared BDNF/EE mechanisms; single-domain programs show mixed transfer and short-lived gains; key gaps are standardised protocols, dose-response, and long follow-ups.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-911 (TINAGE, cluster-RCT protocol, Kerala India, ~420 community-dwelling adults 60-75 with MCI, 20 wards): a culturally adapted 2-year multi-domain intervention (nutrition, physical activity, social support/engagement, cognitive stimulation, metabolic/vascular risk management) will be tested against control; CTRI-registered, IRB-approved - i.e., the multimodal strategy P-914 endorses, operationalised as a scalable trial in a low/middle-income community setting.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: The corpus's strongest non-pharmacological evidence (P-914) identifies combined social-cognitive-physical programs as the most promising MCI intervention, and P-911 is the first corpus protocol to implement precisely that multimodal package as a pragmatic cluster RCT in a low/middle-income community (Kerala), where the global dementia burden is growing fastest. Together they convert a review-level recommendation into a designable, scalable trial - closing the corpus gap of no LMIC multimodal intervention trial while inheriting P-914's caution that effect durability beyond 2 years and adherence are unproven.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Multimodal (social + cognitive + physical) intervention is the corpus-endorsed MCI management strategy, and its LMIC feasibility is now testable via the TINAGE cluster-RCT design.
complementary_findings.review_note: Adversarially source-verified. Genuine complementarity: a review (P-914) and a protocol (P-911) at different evidence tiers converge on the same multimodal strategy; no existing CF links non-pharmacological review evidence to an LMIC implementation trial.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-910 (systematic review, 29 articles, 2014-2024): central auditory processing (CAP) deficits are consistent in MCI (23/29 studies); behavioural tests (Gap Detection Threshold, Dichotic Digit Test, Sentence-in-Noise, Digits Backward) distinguish MCI from HC; yet leading MCI diagnostic guidelines do not include CAP tests.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-451 (auditory event-related potentials, cluster-based permutation tests): auditory sensory-gating alterations discriminate AD, MCI and normal aging - ITPC separated AD, MCI and NC; ERP power separated AD and MCI from normal aging - i.e., electrophysiological auditory measures carry MCI-discriminative signal.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Two independent auditory channels - behavioural CAP tests (P-910 review) and electrophysiological auditory ERPs (P-451) - both separate MCI from healthy aging, yet neither is integrated into standard MCI diagnostic frameworks (P-910 shows guidelines omit CAP tests entirely). The joint reading is that the auditory system is a reproducible, non-invasive MCI marker channel available at two measurement levels (behavioural and electrophysiological), and the corpus currently lacks a study that combines or validates both against a neuropsychological gold standard - a designable screening pathway P-910 explicitly calls for.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Auditory-based MCI screening (behavioural CAP and/or ERP measures) is evidence-supported but guideline-absent; combined validation against a cognitive gold standard is the logical next step.
complementary_findings.review_note: Adversarially source-verified. Genuine cross-modality complementarity within one sensory system (behavioural + electrophysiological auditory markers); no existing CF covers the auditory marker channel.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-915 (scoping review, 32 studies, 2000-2024): diabetes management after MCI onset is debated - guidelines recommend relaxed HbA1c targets to avoid hypoglycaemia, while observational evidence links poor control and glycemic variability to ADRD risk; metformin, TZDs, DPP-4I and GLP-1 RA may slow cognitive decline, mechanism (glycemic vs neuroprotective) unresolved.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-908 (ADNI cross-sectional, 1845 multiethnic US participants, 1056 MCI): TSH level is associated with cognition and MCI odds in a sex-specific manner - significant only in males (adj. beta -0.40; OR males 0.80) - with lower TSH in MCI than HC; authors call for longitudinal studies.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Two modifiable systemic axes - glycemic control (P-915) and thyroid function (P-908) - are each linked to MCI risk, and both reviews/studies converge on the same methodological verdict: cross-sectional or guideline-based evidence is insufficient, and the field needs longitudinal designs that can separate metabolic/endocrine management from direct neuroprotection. P-908 adds the sex-stratification lesson P-915's medication evidence ignores (male-only TSH association could be masked in pooled analyses), while P-915 supplies the clinical-management frame (avoiding hypoglycaemia) that P-908's normal-range TSH findings lack.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Endocrine-metabolic screening (TSH, glycemic control) belongs in MCI risk assessment, and future studies should stratify by sex and by diabetes status to disentangle metabolic from neuroprotective effects.
complementary_findings.review_note: Adversarially source-verified. Genuine complementarity across two modifiable systemic risk axes (endocrine + metabolic) with a shared methodological implication (longitudinal, sex-stratified); no existing CF covers TSH or glycemic management in MCI.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-916 (narrative review, 127 studies, 2005-2025): GABAergic interneuron loss drives E/I imbalance and network hyperexcitability; gamma oscillations are disrupted in AD/MCI; 40 Hz entrainment (tACS, TMS, audiovisual GENUS) increases gamma power/connectivity with modest cognitive benefits in humans (trials n=4-76), while amyloid-PET outcomes are inconsistent; combined GABA + gamma strategies proposed as synergistic.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-361 (review of tDCS/rTMS in aging and pathological aging): excitatory transcranial brain stimulation targeting the left inferior gyrus improves semantic processing in older adults and shows cognitive benefit in MCI/dementia, with multi-session protocols and concurrent fMRI informing mechanism.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Two neuromodulation reviews bracket the corpus's brain-stimulation evidence: P-361 covers classical tDCS/rTMS efficacy over left-inferior-gyrus targets, while P-916 adds the gamma-entrainment mechanism (40 Hz, GABAergic pacing, E/I rebalance) with a different target map (prefrontal, temporo-parietal, precuneus) and explicitly proposes combining GABA-targeted and gamma-based interventions. Read together, they indicate the corpus has convergent support for circuit-level neuromodulation in MCI from two mechanistic traditions (excitability modulation vs oscillatory entrainment) that have not yet been directly compared or combined in a head-to-head trial.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Neuromodulation for MCI spans two complementary mechanisms (excitability vs gamma entrainment); head-to-head or combined protocols are the corpus-implied next trial design.
complementary_findings.review_note: Adversarially source-verified. Genuine complementarity: two neuromodulation reviews at different mechanistic levels (classical NIBS vs gamma/GABA entrainment); no existing CF links gamma-entrainment evidence to the corpus's tDCS/rTMS review.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-924 (Utah, 2 independent amnestic MCI samples, n=64 community + n=58 clinic, RBANS twice over 1 year): applying Hammers et al.'s (2020) SRB prediction equations, observed one-year follow-up scores were significantly lower than predicted across most RBANS Indexes; clinic sample declined on all 5 Indexes and Total Scale (47% declined on Immediate and Delayed Memory), community sample on 3 Indexes + Total; traditional baseline-vs-followup comparisons showed little change, i.e., the SRB method detects subtle decline invisible to traditional scoring.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-926 (Vienna, 358 memory-clinic patients: HC 46, SCD 42, MCI 270, AD converters 48; NTBV assessed twice, mean interval 25.96 months): RCI methodology (Chelune) showed stage-dependent individual deterioration - SCD 0-18.8%, MCI 1.6-29.1%, AD converters up to 54.2% - while improvements (up to 73.4% in SCD) were attributed to practice effects; 17.8% of MCI converted to AD and 14.4% reverted to HC.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Two independent centres (Utah RBANS-SRB, Vienna NTBV-RCI) apply statistically distinct reliable-change implementations to different batteries and horizons and converge on the same cross-paper discovery: in MCI, individual change measured against regression-based or RCI expectation reveals below-expected follow-up performance (reduced practice effects / subtle decline) that traditional baseline-vs-followup comparisons miss, and the proportion of 'decliners' scales with severity along the SCD-MCI-AD continuum. Together they establish reliable-change methodology as a corpus-level first-order measurement axis, not a niche psychometric accessory.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Serial neuropsychological monitoring of MCI should use regression-based/reliable-change scoring rather than raw change scores to avoid missing subtle decline; decline rates are cohort-source-dependent (clinic-recruited MCI worse than community-recruited).
complementary_findings.review_note: Adversarially source-verified. Genuine complementarity: independent cohorts, batteries (RBANS vs NTBV), horizons (1-yr vs ~2-yr) and methods (SRB vs RCI) converge on reduced-practice-effect decline in MCI. No existing CF links the Utah and Vienna reliable-change programs.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-925 (Montreal memory-clinic cohort, 121 MCI: 47 progressors, 16 decliners, 58 stable; SMAf 8-item iADL, yearly up to 5 yrs): PCA separated complex iADL (telephone, medication, transport, budget, shopping) from housekeeping iADL; progressors showed a quadratic complex-iADL trajectory (years of stability then rapid decline ~2 years before dementia diagnosis) while stable MCI showed no change; combining delayed recall + Stroop + Coding + complex iADL achieved AUC 0.94 one year before conversion.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-900 (systematic review, 11 studies: 8 cross-sectional, 3 longitudinal; PubMed/Embase/Scopus/CINAHL/WoS/Cochrane): advanced activities of daily living (AADL) instruments - compared with cognitive assessment - correlate with cognitive measures, discriminate HC from MCI, and improve clinical staging in adults over 60.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: The corpus now contains both halves of a functional-assessment prediction axis: P-900's systematic review establishes that advanced-iADL instruments add discriminative and staging value beyond cognitive tests, and P-925 demonstrates the mechanism - change in complex iADL (not housekeeping) follows a quadratic trajectory accelerating ~2 years before dementia diagnosis and is a statistically significant predictor of conversion in a model reaching AUC 0.94. Read together, functional change is not a downstream consequence of MCI but a first-order prognostic signal with a defined temporal signature, directly supporting routine complex-iADL assessment in memory-clinic risk stratification.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Clinicians should assess complex iADL (telephone, medication, transport, budget, shopping) longitudinally, not cross-sectionally: change on these items combined with cognitive decline signals imminent dementia conversion within 1-2 years.
complementary_findings.review_note: Adversarially source-verified. Genuine complementarity: instrument-level evidence (P-900 review) meets trajectory-level evidence (P-925 longitudinal model). No existing CF links functional-instrument reviews to iADL trajectory prediction.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-920 (Spain, prospective cohort, 48 older cardiac-surgery candidates; MCI in 35% at baseline): MCI at baseline predicted post-operative cognitive decline (BDRS RR 3.5) and IADL worsening in women, but no association with resource use or frailty change; preoperative memory/visuospatial/executive impairment predicted quality-of-life loss.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-751 (Osaka, prospective single-centre cohort in acute decompensated heart failure): MCI carries its own prognostic weight distinct from frank cognitive impairment over long follow-up in patients hospitalised for ADHF.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Two independent cardiac-population cohorts bracket the same cross-paper discovery: MCI carries independent prognostic weight across the cardiac continuum - in acute decompensated heart failure (P-751) and in elective cardiac-surgery candidates (P-920, RR 3.5 for post-operative cognitive decline) - and in both settings the effect operates without requiring increased resource use. The corpus therefore supports routine cognitive screening in cardiac care pathways as a prognostic instrument, not merely a descriptive comorbidity flag.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Cognitive screening should be standard in cardiac pathways (acute HF admission and pre-operative assessment): MCI identifies patients at elevated risk of cognitive/functional decline while not inflating resource use.
complementary_findings.review_note: Adversarially source-verified. Genuine complementarity: two cardiac cohorts (acute HF vs elective surgery, Japan vs Spain) independently show MCI's prognostic weight. No existing CF links MCI across cardiac settings.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-919 (Neurology and Therapy 2022 narrative review, PubMed 2014-2021, NA/Europe/Asia): AD dementia aetiology among MCI patients ranges 40-75% depending on population and clinical vs biomarker-based diagnosis; lifetime AD-dementia risk with Abeta accumulation + neurodegeneration is 41.9% (women) / 33.6% (men); risk factors include lower MMSE, higher ADAS-cog, APOE4, WMH volume, entorhinal atrophy, CSF total tau, CSF neurogranin, iADL dependency, female sex.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-927 (Age and Ageing 2021 UK Manchester consensus): MCI is a heterogeneous clinical syndrome, not a diagnosis in its own right; 5-15% of people with MCI progress to dementia per year while ~50% remain stable at 5 years (16% in ADNI); calls for NICE guidance, annual review, equitable neuropsychology access, CSF/blood biomarkers on an individual basis, and research participation for all MCI patients.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: The corpus's two broadest MCI-progression syntheses - a quantitative epidemiology review (P-919) and a national clinical consensus (P-927) - are complementary lenses on the same heterogeneity problem: P-919 explains why MCI is aetiologicaly uncertain (40-75% AD attribution depending on clinical vs biomarker diagnosis) while P-927 converts that uncertainty into practice standards (syndrome-not-diagnosis framing, 5-15% annual conversion with ~50% stability, individualised biomarker use, annual review). Together they define the progression-risk landscape the whole corpus operates in and justify biomarker-stratified rather than lumped MCI management.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: MCI management should be biomarker-informed and individualised: lumped MCI statistics (40-75% AD aetiology, 5-15% annual conversion) conceal trajectories ranging from stable to rapidly progressive, so annual review and case-by-case CSF/blood biomarker use are the appropriate default.
complementary_findings.review_note: Adversarially source-verified. Genuine complementarity: quantitative epidemiology synthesis paired with clinical consensus translation; both independently frame MCI as heterogeneous. No existing CF links the two broad syntheses.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-933 (Ruijin Hospital Shanghai, N=59: 19 NC, 23 MCI, 17 AD; PVEP + flash ERG + OCT + 3T MRI): P100 amplitude was significantly decreased in AD vs MCI (P=0.016); FERG showed delayed rod (AD P=0.013), rod-cone (MCI P=0.003, AD P=0.003) and 3.0 flicker (AD vs MCI P=0.013, vs NC P=0.008) latencies; m-RNFL thickness was markedly reduced in AD vs MCI and MCI vs NC (P<0.001, eta2p=0.393); P100 amplitude remained associated with hippocampal volume after adjusting for age, sex and cognitive reserve, and m-RNFL thickness plus hippocampal volumes were associated with ADAS-cog scores.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-830 (systematic review + meta-analysis of retinal biomarkers in AD/MCI, 126 published articles): pooled retinal structural, vascular and electrophysiological markers differ between MCI/AD and controls (e.g. peripapillary RNFL SMD -0.324 for MCI vs controls), establishing retinal/ocular measures as a low-burden biomarker direction for early cognitive decline screening.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Across the corpus's ocular line, structural (OCT m-RNFL, pooled RNFL meta) AND functional (PVEP P100 amplitude, FERG rod/cone latencies) ocular markers both track AD-related neurodegeneration, and P-933 supplies the missing mechanistic bridge: functional ocular electrophysiology and macular RNFL thickness correlate directly with hippocampal volume - the canonical AD-vulnerable structure - while both independently relate to ADAS-cog. Together P-830 (field-level pooled structural evidence) and P-933 (single-centre functional+structural evidence with hippocampal anchor) justify ocular panels combining structure (OCT) with function (PVEP/FERG), not OCT alone, for prodromal AD screening.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Ocular biomarker panels for MCI/early-AD screening should combine structural (OCT m-RNFL) with functional (PVEP P100, FERG latency) measures; functional ocular markers add hippocampal-tracking value that structural OCT alone does not capture.
complementary_findings.review_note: Adversarially source-verified against pdf_extract_933.txt and pdf_extract_830 summary. Genuine complementarity: field-level structural meta + functional/structural single-cohort with hippocampal anchor. P-891 (sleep-quality modifier) not involved. No existing CF duplicates this pairing.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-934 (ADNI, 870 MCI: 618 non-smokers, 252 smokers; linear mixed models over up to 13 years): a history of cigarette smoking was associated with faster decline in functional performance (FAQ estimate 0.13, p=0.03) and steeper decline in entorhinal cortex volume (EVR estimate -0.02, p=0.006), but NOT with change in MMSE, RAVLT, hippocampal volume, FDG SUVRs, or CSF Abeta42/t-tau/p-tau.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-521 (ADNI, structural + resting-state fMRI in MCI): smoking-related effects on resting-state functional connectivity of the nucleus basalis of Meynert (NBM) - the main cholinergic basal-forebrain nucleus - with r=-0.321, p=0.041 for NBM-SMA rsFC vs WMS-LM immediate recall in smoking cognitively normal subjects; first rsFC study of smoking effects on NBM cholinergic connectivity in MCI.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Two independent ADNI analyses of smoking in MCI converge on the cholinergic-forebrain axis rather than the amyloid pathway: P-934 shows smoking accelerates functional (FAQ) and entorhinal-cortex decline while leaving CSF amyloid/tau and hippocampal volume untouched, and P-521 shows smoking-related disruption of NBM cholinergic connectivity at the same prodromal stage. The cross-paper discovery is mechanistic: smoking's MCI effect localises to the cholinergic basal forebrain - entorhinal cortex is a major NBM projection target - with no amyloid signature, supporting a vascular/oxidative cholinergic-deafferentation mechanism rather than accelerated Abeta/tau pathology.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Smoking cessation counselling should be a standard component of MCI risk-factor management: smoking-related decline is functionally and structurally measurable at the prodromal stage via a non-amyloid, cholinergic-forebrain pathway, and may be independent of amyloid-modifying treatments.
complementary_findings.review_note: Adversarially source-verified against pdf_extract_934.txt and P-521 registry record. Both ADNI - dataset overlap accepted for a complementary mechanism pairing (connectivity-level + trajectory-level evidence); VF independence rules do not apply to CFs. No existing CF duplicates this pairing.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-932 (Lothian Birth Cohort 1936, n=292 with two MCI assessments at ages 76 and 82): 74% remained cognitively healthy, 12% transitioned to MCI, 7% reverted to healthy cognition, and 7% maintained baseline MCI; a one-unit increase in depressive symptoms increased the likelihood of reverting from MCI to healthy cognition (OR 1.37, 1.05-1.80, p<0.05); history of cardiovascular disease increased likelihood of maintaining MCI (OR 3.13, 1.01-9.70, p<0.05); older age reduced likelihood of maintaining/reverting to MCI.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-711 (48-study systematic review and meta-analysis of MCI reversion to normal cognition): pooled reversion prevalence 31% (95% CI 26-35%, I2=98.9%), with 14 influencing factors across sample source, diagnostic criteria, and follow-up duration.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: The corpus's reversion evidence spans cohort-level fluidity (P-932) and pooled prevalence (P-711): P-711's 31% pooled reversion rate is dominated by clinic/community samples with short follow-up, while P-932's population cohort (7% over 6 years) shows that reversion is less common but still clinically real in an unselected ageing cohort, and - crucially - that a MODIFIABLE state (depressive symptoms) predicts it, whereas cardiovascular disease locks patients into persistent MCI. The cross-paper insight: reversion probability is context-dependent (criteria, follow-up, sample) but depression is the one actionable lever identified at cohort level.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Prognostic counselling for MCI should present reversion as possible but prevalence-dependent (7-31% by context), and treat depression as a potentially reversion-relevant modifiable factor; CVD comorbidity marks persistent-MCI risk (OR 3.13).
complementary_findings.review_note: Adversarially source-verified against pdf_extract_932.txt and P-711 registry record. Genuine complementarity: cohort-level modifiable predictors + pooled prevalence synthesis. P-722 (dietary multistate reversion) kept separate - distinct predictor domain. No existing CF duplicates this pairing.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-930 (integrative review, 24 studies, 4 databases): sleep disturbances raise MCI risk (about 1.39x; lowest sleep-efficiency quartile about 1.53x); MCI/AD patients have poorer sleep than healthy controls; brain anatomy changes accompany sleep disturbance in healthy older adults; sleep interventions (physical activity, CBT-based Sleep Well Think Well, acoustic stimulation, sleep medication) are effective in improving sleep.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-803 (community-dwelling population survey): association between sleep duration and MCI differs at different levels of metabolic disease - dose-response relationship where sleep duration's MCI association is modified by metabolic status (e.g. OR 1.88 for long sleep + poor sleep quality vs 1.33 with good quality; short sleepers with 30-60 min naps OR 0.72).
complementary_findings.combined_insight: The corpus's sleep-MCI evidence is two-layered: P-930 synthesises the field-level association (sleep disturbance raises MCI risk ~1.39x, with effective interventions available) while P-803 shows the association is NOT uniform - it is dose- and quality-dependent and modified by metabolic disease. The cross-paper discovery: sleep is a genuinely modifiable MCI risk factor whose risk gradient (duration x quality x metabolic context) is measurable at population level, meaning sleep screening and intervention can be targeted rather than applied blanket-wise.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Sleep screening in MCI risk assessment should capture duration, quality, and metabolic comorbidity jointly; sleep-improvement interventions (physical activity, CBT-based, acoustic stimulation) are available and effective, supporting sleep as an actionable MCI risk-reduction target.
complementary_findings.review_note: Adversarially source-verified against pdf_extract_930.txt and P-803 registry record. P-891 already paired in CF-199 with P-648 - this pairing (review synthesis x population dose-response) is distinct and non-overlapping. Genuine cross-layer complementarity.
