complementary_findings.finding_a: P-940 (University of Miami / Mount Sinai memory-clinic cohort, N=116: 51 stable CN, 25 PreMCI reverted, 22 PreMCI->MCI, 18 aMCI->dementia, ~26-month follow-up; LASSI-L): semantic-intrusion errors indexed by Cued B1 PIE predicted progression - AUC 0.905 (95% CI 0.836-0.974) for CN vs aMCI-to-dementia on Cued B1 PIE, and 83.3% of aMCI progressors were classified at a PIE cut-point of 44%.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-768 (1Florida Alzheimer's Disease Research Center, N=97 baseline aMCI, 3-4 year follow-up; LASSI-L): failure to recover from proactive semantic interference (frPSI, Cued B2 recall / semantic intrusion errors during Cued B2) measured once at baseline predicted the trajectory of everyday-function decline (Clinical Dementia Rating Sum of Boxes, clinician-rated blind to neuropsychology).
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Two independent Miami-memory-clinic cohorts using the same LASSI-L semantic-interference paradigm show that a single baseline measure of semantic-interference failure - intrusion errors (PIE) in P-940 and failure-to-recover (frPSI) in P-768 - is a unified early-progression marker: P-940 anchors it to clinical conversion to dementia (AUC 0.905) while P-768 anchors the same paradigm to longitudinal functional decline (CDR-SOB trajectory). Together they demonstrate that the deliberate adversarial-design semantic-interference stress test, not conventional list recall, is the cognitive measure that captures the earliest clinically meaningful decline signal, converging across two outcome axes (conversion and everyday function) from the same instrument family.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Semantic-interference stress testing (LASSI-L PIE/frPSI) should be considered a first-line progression-risk measure in aMCI: a single baseline administration identifies both converters (P-940) and those on a steeper functional-decline trajectory (P-768), supporting risk-tiering at the point of first assessment.
complementary_findings.review_note: Adversarially source-verified against pdf_extract_940.txt and pdf_extract_768.txt. P-768 was previously paired only in REJECTED CF-12/CF-69 contexts - this pairing is new and non-overlapping. complementary_findings.finding_a: P-946 (Korean memory-clinic cohort, N=410; clinical data only - demographics, cognitive screening, vascular risk): amyloid-positivity prediction without molecular imaging - AUC 0.775 all subjects, 0.735 in MCI, 0.845 in AD; demonstrates routine clinical data carry substantial amyloid-status signal.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-753 (Pusan National University Hospital, N=64 aMCI, 18F-florbetaben amyloid PET: 31 negative / 33 positive): learning potential (SVLT trial 1-to-3 gain) and visuospatial memory (RCFT delayed recall) each predicted amyloid positivity (AUC 0.72 / 0.73); the combined logistic equation reached AUC 0.82 (sens 0.73, spec 0.77).
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Two non-molecular routes to amyloid-status triage converge: P-946 shows that readily available clinical data alone carry substantial amyloid signal (AUC up to 0.845 in AD) and P-753 shows that two targeted neuropsychological metrics - learning potential and visuospatial memory - approximate PET-determined amyloid status at AUC 0.82 without any imaging. The cross-paper discovery is that amyloid positivity can be pre-screened with cheap, non-molecular instruments, so PET/CSF can be reserved for confirmation, which is directly relevant where molecular imaging is unavailable or costly.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Amyloid pre-screening is feasible from routine clinical and targeted neuropsych data; high-risk individuals can be triaged to confirmatory molecular testing rather than scanned indiscriminately - a low-resource pathway to biological MCI characterisation.
complementary_findings.review_note: Adversarially source-verified against pdf_extract_946.txt and pdf_extract_753.txt. P-753 unused in prior CFs. Complementary predictor families (whole-clinical-data vs two targeted cognitive metrics) targeting the same biological construct - genuine cross-paper discovery, not dataset recycling.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-938 (Trinity College Dublin / St James's Hospital, N=80: 20 MCI, 20 mild-to-moderate AD, 40 HC; conversational speech-timing features): multi-class classification 82.47-84.17%, AD-HC 74%, MCI-HC 63%; timing features linked to cognitive performance and brain-volume correlates - the first study to probe the cognitive and structural underpinnings of conversational speech-timing discrimination.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-58 (Computer Speech and Language, cross-lingual): temporal hesitation-related speech features - speech tempo, articulation rate, silent and filled pauses - distinguished controls from MCI with F1 around 75% (ranges ~67-92% depending on dataset/language), and extraction/classification performed similarly in monolingual and cross-lingual setups.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: The corpus's speech-timing evidence is two-layered: P-58 establishes that temporal hesitation features are a portable, cross-lingual MCI discriminative signal, while P-938 shows the same timing feature family carries interpretable cognitive and brain-volume correlates in conversational settings. The cross-paper discovery: speech timing is not a black-box acoustic artifact - its discriminative power tracks measurable cognitive and structural decline, and it generalises across languages - making it one of the most deployable low-burden digital MCI markers in the corpus.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Speech-timing features can serve as an interpretable, cross-lingual digital screening channel; the demonstrable cognitive/structural grounding (P-938) strengthens the biological credibility needed for clinical uptake alongside the portability evidence (P-58).

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-941 (NACC Uniform Data Set, 26 US ADCs, N=830 incident MCI, 515 with FAQ; growth mixture models): 3 latent trajectory classes - 21% fast CDR-SB progression, 22% slow, 57% no progression; FAQ paralleled CDR-SB (14/23/64); 77% CDR-SB-FAQ class concordance; fast-progression predictors age>=86 OR 5.26, APOE4 OR 1.94, baseline CDR-SB OR 2.46.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-947 (ADNI; CFA on 272 MCI learning / 408 evaluation): 4 MCI cognitive subgroups derived from factor-analytic composite scores; subgroup-aware prediction improved 12-60 month progression AUC to 0.68-0.76 versus 0.63-0.69 for standard single composite tests.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Two independent statistical lenses on MCI heterogeneity converge: P-941 (latent-class growth modelling on cognitive+functional trajectories, NACC multi-centre) and P-947 (confirmatory-factor composite subtyping, ADNI) both show that MCI is not a single entity - P-941 finds a large non-progressing majority (57%) separable from fast progressors, and P-947 finds four reproducible cognitive subgroups - and BOTH show subgroup-informed prediction beats standard single-score approaches. The cross-paper discovery: data-driven MCI subtyping, whether trajectory-based or composite-based, is a replicable route to better progression prediction across independent cohorts and instruments.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: MCI risk stratification should use subgroup-aware models rather than single cognitive cut-offs: both a latent-trajectory view (P-941) and a composite-subgroup view (P-947) identify a substantial non-progressing majority and improve progression prediction, supporting personalised monitoring intensity.
complementary_findings.review_note: Adversarially source-verified against pdf_extract_941.txt and pdf_extract_947.txt. Neither paper used in prior CFs. Complements VF-14 (MCI heterogeneity) as a paired methodological convergence across cohorts; distinct findings (trajectory classes vs composite subgroups).

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-950 (Rotterdam Study, N=648 MCI + 6410 non-MCI, population cohort): community-dwelling MCI total life expectancy 21.4y (95% CI 19.0-23.6) at age 60 with only 2.9y (14%) lived with dementia; 5.0y (1.9-8.1) of life lost vs non-MCI - explicitly more favourable than clinic-derived estimates.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-711 (Geriatric Nursing, 48-study meta-analysis, 31,876 pooled subjects): pooled MCI-to-normal reversion prevalence 31% with 14 influencing factors - the corpus's largest reversion synthesis.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: The population-level view of MCI converges from two directions: P-950's multistate life-table analysis in the Rotterdam community cohort shows persons with MCI spend only ~14% of remaining life with dementia at age 60, and P-711's 48-study meta-analysis pools an MCI-to-normal reversion prevalence of 31%. The cross-paper discovery is that community-based MCI prognosis - long non-dementia survival plus frequent reversion - is substantially more favourable than the clinic-based conversion framing that dominates the literature, implying clinic samples over-represent the progressive minority.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Risk communication for community-dwelling MCI should present non-progression/reversion as a common outcome, and prevention trials should be powered against a high community reversion baseline to avoid overestimating efficacy.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-951 (J Clin Med, PRISMA dose-response meta-analysis, 22 studies/11 in meta, 12,458 participants): each one-point increase in Mediterranean-diet adherence reduces MCI risk RR 0.91 (0.85-0.97) and AD risk RR 0.89 (0.84-0.93).
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-953 (SPRINT secondary analysis, N=9361, multistate survival): intensive SBP<120 mmHg reduces MCI risk HR 0.81 (0.69-0.94), amnestic 0.78 (0.66-0.92), multidomain 0.78 (0.65-0.93); MCI adjudication raised 2-year dementia probability to 5.9% vs 0.6%.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Two independent modifiable-risk levers converge on the same ~10-20% MCI/AD risk reduction: P-951 quantifies dietary adherence (RR 0.89-0.91 per point) at the meta-analytic level and P-953 demonstrates blood-pressure control (HR 0.81, subtype-specific amnestic/multidomain 0.78) in a randomized trial. The cross-paper discovery is that lifestyle and vascular risk modification each deliver comparable, statistically significant relative reductions in MCI incidence - supporting multidomain prevention strategies where neither lever alone achieves dramatic effect sizes.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Modifiable-risk counselling for MCI prevention should bundle dietary adherence and BP control; combined effects may exceed either alone, and both are implementable in primary care.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-949 (J Neuropsychol, Groningen memory clinic, N=203: 60 HC + 143 patients AD/MCI/MDD/NI): emotion recognition (Ekman 60 Faces) adds significant value over episodic memory (RAVLT) for group differentiation (final model chi2=132.23, Nagelkerke pseudo-R2=0.51; AD-vs-MCI EFT OR 0.89, 0.83-0.96).
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-955 (J Alzheimers Dis, Penn ADRC, N=354, 68% White/29% Black): MCI rates by consensus/actuarial/LCA methods are 44%/53%/41%; method agreement 0.68-0.72; actuarial-only MCI over-represents Black participants, and method choice interacts with race in prognostic prediction.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Diagnostic ascertainment is doubly load-bearing in the memory clinic: P-949 shows that WHAT you add to the battery (social cognition beyond episodic memory) measurably improves AD-vs-MCI separation, while P-955 shows that HOW you classify (consensus vs actuarial vs LCA) moves MCI rates from 41% to 53% and interacts with race. The cross-paper discovery is that test selection and classification method are both first-order determinants of who receives an MCI/AD label - neither the instrument set nor the scoring rule can be treated as neutral.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Memory-clinic diagnostic protocols should specify both the social-cognition instruments and the classification rule; method-and-race interactions (P-955) caution against uniform actuarial cutoffs in diverse populations.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-952 (Neuropsychiatr Dis Treat, Sun Yat-sen, N=86, 332 fundus images): HOG features + SVM/ELM on fundus-photograph vascular features classify MCI with AUC 0.87 (validation), outperforming ELM and segmentation images - simple, widely available fundus photography with classical ML.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-163 (Ophthalmology Science, multimodal CNN): GC-IPL maps + OCTA images + quantitative retinal metrics in a multimodal CNN achieve AUC 0.81 for MCI - specialist OCT/OCTA hardware with deep learning.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: The corpus's retinal-screening evidence spans a cost-tier spectrum: P-952 achieves comparable-or-better MCI discrimination (AUC 0.87) from ordinary fundus photographs with classical ML (HOG+SVM), while P-163 reaches AUC 0.81 only with specialist multimodal OCT/OCTA and a CNN. The cross-paper discovery is that the cheapest retinal channel (fundus photography) is not the weakest - classical-feature pipelines on ubiquitous hardware may offer the most deployable retinal screening path, with specialist OCT/OCTA adding depth rather than decisive accuracy.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Retinal MCI screening programmes should consider fundus-photography classical-ML as the first-line, lowest-cost tier; OCT/OCTA CNN adds multimodal depth but not a large accuracy gain in current evidence.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-967 (Stroke & Vascular Neurology 2022, SPRINT MIND post hoc, N=433, 33 dementia/MCI events): WMH progression over 48 months (>=1.4 mL threshold OR 2.89, 1.23-6.81; per-Z OR 1.51, 1.12-2.04) independently predicts incident probable dementia/MCI - progression, not static burden, is the operative imaging risk.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-953 (J Am Geriatr Soc 2022, SPRINT secondary analysis, N=9361, 640 protocol-defined MCI): intensive (<120 mmHg) vs standard (<140 mmHg) systolic BP control reduces MCI occurrence (HR 0.81; amnestic and multidomain subtypes 0.78) in a randomized trial with multistate survival models.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Two analyses of the SAME SPRINT trial platform jointly close the vascular pathway loop: intensive blood-pressure control reduces incident MCI (P-953, HR 0.81, randomized) and white-matter hyperintensity progression - the imaging lesion most directly modulated by blood pressure - independently predicts dementia/MCI (P-967, OR 2.89). The cross-paper discovery is that the corpus now contains both the modifiable intervention (BP lowering) and the mechanistic imaging marker (WMH progression) from one RCT population, so the vascular pathway is no longer an inference across heterogeneous studies but a closed, within-trial evidence chain.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: BP-lowering trials in older adults should track WMH progression as an on-pathway surrogate; the >=1.4 mL/48-month threshold offers a concrete imaging endpoint for MCI-prevention trial design.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-965 (J Geriatr Psychiatry Neurol 2023, PRISMA meta-analysis, 11 studies / 9504 individuals): apathy in MCI predicts conversion to dementia (pooled unadjusted HR 1.54, 1.29-1.84), with significant subgroup association for progression to AD.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-612 (Int J Nurs Stud 2023): multimodal ML using speech, facial-expression and text features detects and distinguishes depression, anxiety and apathy in older adults with MCI, with explainability analysis of feature contributions.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Apathy is simultaneously the most prognostically loaded behavioral symptom in MCI (P-965: HR 1.54 for MCI-to-dementia conversion, pooled across 11 longitudinal studies) AND a signal that can be extracted automatically from speech, facial expression and text (P-612 multimodal ML). The cross-paper discovery is that the corpus now spans both ends of the apathy pipeline - prognostic significance established at the meta-analytic level and low-cost automated detection demonstrated at the model level - so longitudinal apathy monitoring by ambient sensing becomes a viable, evidence-backed risk channel rather than a clinic-administered rating scale.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Automated apathy detection from speech/face/text could be embedded in longitudinal MCI monitoring to flag conversion-risk elevation between clinic visits.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-966 (Front Aging Neurosci 2022, GARD cohort, Korea; 79 MCI + 170 HC): interleaved prosaccade/antisaccade + Go/No-go paradigms show MCI patients produce longer PS latencies, fewer correct responses and markedly more inhibition errors, and fail to self-correct many inhibition errors - impaired inhibitory control and error monitoring.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-686 (Int J Psychophysiol 2023; probable early AD, aMCI, HC): eye movements during free viewing of real-world photographic scenes differ across the AD/MCI/healthy spectrum.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Two independent oculomotor paradigms - voluntary saccade control with Go/No-go inhibition (P-966) and naturalistic free-viewing exploration (P-686) - both separate MCI/early AD from healthy aging, but they interrogate different neural systems: P-966 probes executive inhibitory control and error monitoring, P-686 probes bottom-up visual exploration. The cross-paper discovery is that the oculomotor channel is not a single task but a family of complementary readouts spanning controlled and automatic oculomotor behavior, giving the eye-movement screening direction both convergent validity and mechanistic breadth.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Oculomotor screening batteries should combine a voluntary-inhibition task (antisaccade/Go-No-go) with a free-viewing task to capture both controlled and automatic oculomotor deficits in MCI.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-958 (Rotterdam Study, N=3025, 231 MCRS / 132 MCI / 62 both): gait-defined motoric cognitive risk syndrome (slow gait + subjective complaints) carries dementia risk (subdistribution HR 3.55, 1.91-6.60) even in the absence of MCI, with neurodegenerative imaging correlates (lower grey-matter/hippocampal volumes, more WMH) - motor assessment as an early low-cost risk-stratification channel.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-682 (Arch Gerontol Geriatr 2025, Shandong Rural Elderly Health Cohort, N=3110): MCI participants have lower grip strength (17.41 vs 21.56 kgf) and slower gait speed (0.73 vs 0.83 m/s) than non-MCI peers in a rural Chinese cohort.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Motor function - grip strength and gait speed - is a consistent MCI/dementia risk channel across populations that differ in setting (Western urban population cohort vs rural Chinese community) and in whether the motor marker is formalised as a syndrome (MCRS in Rotterdam, P-958) or measured as continuous grip/gait in association analyses (P-682). The cross-paper discovery is that the motor channel generalises beyond high-income clinic settings: because P-682 shows the same motor-MCI associations in a low-resource rural cohort where comprehensive cognitive batteries are impractical, the gait/grip-based screening case that P-958 makes for Rotterdam is transferable to exactly the settings that need low-cost triage most.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Grip-strength and gait-speed screening for cognitive risk is viable in low-resource and rural settings where full neuropsychological batteries are unavailable; MCRS criteria deserve validation in non-Western cohorts.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-974 (Chosun Univ, N=75 MCI, [18F]Florbetaben PET, 24-mo mean follow-up): a SINGLE baseline amyloid scan suffices - baseline amyloid burden predicts MCI-to-AD conversion (HR 10.0, 1.15-85.39, p=0.04) while longitudinal amyloid-burden CHANGE adds nothing (HR 0.2, ns); ROC 65.2% change vs 59.6% baseline, difference ns.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-967 (SPRINT MIND post hoc, N=433): for white-matter hyperintensity the OPPOSITE temporal structure holds - WMH PROGRESSION over 48 months (not static burden) predicts incident probable dementia/MCI (per-Z OR 1.51, 1.12-2.04; >=1.4 mL OR 2.89, 1.23-6.81).
complementary_findings.combined_insight: The two imaging biomarkers carry opposite temporal-information structures: amyloid deposition is captured at a single baseline scan (longitudinal serial PET adds nothing, P-974), whereas vascular WMH pathology is only visible through its rate of change (progression, not static load, is the predictor, P-967). The cross-paper discovery is that the optimal longitudinal sampling strategy for MCI risk is pathology-specific - serial imaging is wasteful for amyloid but essential for the vascular leg - so a parsimonious monitoring protocol should pair a one-time amyloid scan with a WMH-progression trajectory rather than applying a single uniform repeat-scan policy.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Monitoring protocols should be marker-specific: baseline amyloid PET for the molecular leg, ~2-4-year interval MRI for the vascular leg; avoid serial amyloid PET where baseline is already available.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-976 (Join Dementia Research UK, 21 MCI vs 21 HC): a standalone commercial wearable PPG device (CorSense) measuring HRV at rest already discriminates MCI from healthy controls - SDNN/RMSSD significantly lower in MCI; logistic regression 10-fold CV accuracy 76.5%, sensitivity 0.8095, specificity 0.8571.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-83 (multimodal EEG+HRV recorded DURING the CERAD cognitive task with ensemble ML): combining EEG with HRV during a cognitive load yields stronger MCI classification than either modality alone, at the cost of a full EEG setup.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: HRV carries MCI-discriminative signal that is already exploitable at the cheapest deployment tier - a finger-worn PPG sensor at rest (P-976, 76.5% accuracy) - while the corpus's multimodal work (P-83) shows the same autonomic signal gains accuracy when captured under cognitive load with EEG co-registration. The two studies jointly define a cost-accuracy continuum for autonomic biomarkers: single-channel wearable for population triage, multimodal load-based EEG+HRV for confirmatory assessment, with the shared HRV axis making the upgrade path continuous rather than a modality switch.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Autonomic screening can start with an off-the-shelf wearable at population scale; escalating to EEG+HRV under cognitive load reserves the higher-accuracy tier for confirmatory diagnosis.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-968 (Taiwan, N=24 MCI RCT): a 6-week MAGIC intervention (learning/performing tricks, no screens) significantly improved MoCA and Flanker-task accuracy/RT plus ERP P3 amplitudes - engagement-format cognitive training with electrophysiological gains.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-326 (humanoid-robot cognitive training in MCI): social-presence robotic delivery of cognitive training improves engagement and outcomes over conventional computerised training.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Two independent engagement-format cognitive interventions - performative magic (P-968) and social-presence robotics (P-326) - both improve MCI cognition through channels that are non-screen and socially embodied, and P-968 further shows the gains are electrophysiologically real (P3 amplitude). The cross-paper discovery is that adherence/engagement formats matter as much as task content: low-tech social formats (magic) and high-tech social formats (robots) converge on the same mechanism - recruiting attention, conflict monitoring and error detection (DLPFC/ACC) - which computerised screen-based training lacks; engagement format is a design axis, not a delivery detail.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Intervention design should treat engagement/social-embodiment as a first-class axis: low-cost magic-style programs and robot-delivered training both outperform flat screen CCT on engagement, with ERP evidence (P-968) that effects are neurophysiological.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-972 (Japan, N=130 RCT, 115 FAS): 24-week Bifidobacterium breve MCC1274 suppressed MRI brain-atrophy progression (VSRAD; esp. VOI Z>=1.0) and improved ADAS-Jcog orientation / MMSE subscales vs placebo - a structural brain endpoint for a gut intervention.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-641 (meta-analysis restricted to cognitively impaired populations): pooled probiotic efficacy in cognition with strain and duration subgroup analyses - the synthesis-level view of the same intervention class.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: The probiotic evidence in MCI spans two complementary evidentiary levels that rarely coexist for an intervention class: a single RCT with a STRUCTURAL brain endpoint (P-972: VSRAD atrophy-progression suppression, not just test scores) and a meta-analysis restricted to cognitively impaired populations (P-641: pooled cognitive efficacy with strain/duration moderation). Together they answer the two questions neither can alone - P-972 shows a plausible brain mechanism (atrophy deceleration) for an effect that P-641 confirms is pooled-significant across trials, while P-641's strain-subgroup analysis tells clinicians WHICH strain (e.g., B. breve) is worth using. This RCT-structure + meta-efficacy pairing is the template for moving other gut-brain interventions from suggestive to testable.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Probiotic strains with both RCT structural evidence (B. breve MCC1274) and meta-analytic pooled efficacy deserve clinical consideration as adjuncts; future gut-brain trials should pre-specify imaging endpoints.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-986 (GAS/SNAC Sweden; n=744 Petersen vs n=375 NP criteria): reversion 43.4% vs 48.3% - criterion strength does NOT shrink reversion (incidence 63.0 vs 76.2/1000 person-years); reverters' dementia HR 0.34 (0.21-0.54) Petersen / 0.17 (0.1-0.34) NP; single-domain impairment dominates the reverter profile (86.1% vs 58.4% in stable MCI).
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-984 (ADNI, 325 MCI, sex-separated mixed-data clustering): data-driven poor/good/best-prognosis subtypes (KM p<0.001) show reversion occurs ONLY outside poor-prognosis subtypes (0 reverters in PP for both sexes), and female-PP APOE e4 carriers convert at 78.57% vs 49.12% in male-PP.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: The two papers triangulate WHERE reversion lives: P-986 shows its population magnitude is criterion-robust (43-48% under one-test vs two-test rules), while P-984 shows its occurrence is subtype-dependent (zero reversion inside poor-prognosis clusters). Jointly: reversion is neither a measurement artefact nor uniform noise - it is concentrated in definable low-risk phenotypes that multi-modal clustering can identify in advance, yielding a two-stage clinical logic (broad criteria for sensitivity, then subtype/prognostic features to flag who will actually revert).
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Disclose reversion as a realistic outcome for single-domain, prognostically favourable patients, while counselling poor-prognosis-subtype patients that reversion is unlikely; prevention trials should stratify or exclude likely reverters using subtype features rather than tightening diagnostic rules.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-981 (BABRI Beijing, n=5921; 921-subject longitudinal sub-cohort): routine variables (age, education, cerebrovascular disease, intelligence, physical activity) alone give AUC 0.64-0.70; adding baseline memory and language performance lifts incident-MCI prediction to AUC 0.785.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-982 (Thailand, n=421 metabolic-risk adults): six Thai Cardiovascular Risk (TCVR) models built only from routine cardiovascular variables plateau at AuROC 0.58-0.61 for MoCA-defined MCI (best stratified model 0.69, anthropometric, older group).
complementary_findings.combined_insight: The pair brackets the value of cognitive items in community MCI risk models across two independent non-Western cohorts: cardiovascular/routine variables plateau near AuROC 0.6-0.7, and the single largest observed gain (0.70 to 0.785) comes from adding two brief cognitive domains (memory, language) rather than any further routine variable. This quantifies where to stop engineering routine-variable scores and start embedding 2-minute cognitive probes - a transferable design rule for resource-limited primary-care screening.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Resource-limited metabolic and primary-care clinics should pair existing vascular risk scores with a 2-minute memory/language probe instead of expanding laboratory panels; vascular-only scores can triage but not diagnose.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-978 (Amsterdam Dementia Cohort, n=2597, Memento external): Cox models predict institutionalization (Harrell's C 0.81) and mortality (C 0.79) in SCD/MCI - biomarkers add ~+0.05 over clinical variables - while dementia-stage discrimination drops to C 0.65-0.68.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-973 (CIDER; NACC-UDS n=6222 development, PROMPT and ADNI external): routine-care 3-year dementia risk scoring achieves c-index 0.69 internal / 0.61 PROMPT / 0.72 ADNI.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Together they establish that pre-dementia prognostication is achievable across BOTH outcome families the corpus had treated separately - cognitive decline (P-973) and care outcomes (P-978) - and reveal a shared asymmetry: discrimination is strongest before dementia (C 0.81 in SCD/MCI vs 0.68 in dementia; c-index 0.72 in ADNI vs 0.61 in routine PROMPT care) and degrades in later stages and real-world systems. The corpus previously held only conversion-focused prediction; this pair adds the care-planning and routine-care prognostic axes with a common stage-dependence law.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Front-load biomarker-informed prognostic counselling at the SCD/MCI stage where models discriminate best; routine-care risk tools require per-health-system recalibration before deployment.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-987 (TECH, Israel, n=38): home-based unsupervised tablet puzzle-gaming with 6 weekly OT group sessions - high feasibility (23.62 h self-training, 4.7 h/week, device-logged), MoCA d=0.52 (MCI) and memory-recall p=0.006 - but no control arm and practice effects unquantified.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-969 (MAKSCog protocol, Germany, n=100 planned): supervised individualised computerised cognitive training RCT with active control, powered for cognitive-capacity change over 12 months, but no home-telemetry compliance layer and no dementia-incidence endpoint.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: The pair spans the delivery-mode spectrum for computerised cognitive training in MCI: P-987 proves the ecological end (unsupervised daily home practice is feasible, complied-with and telemetered), while P-969 defines the efficacy end (supervised, individualised, controlled, adequately powered). Neither alone can establish durability: P-987 lacks control and practice-effect handling (the exact artifact P-971 quantified), and P-969 measures capacity change only - jointly they specify the missing experiment: an RCT fusing home telemetry with controlled supervision and a practice-effect-adjusted dementia-incidence endpoint (cf. gaps G-074/G-078).
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Prescribable home training should adopt device-logged adherence telemetry by default; digital-training trials must add practice-effect-adjusted and conversion endpoints before claiming disease-modifying value.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-994 (Xiao et al. 2023, Inquiry 60; AHLS n=5,393): equipment-free community model combining handgrip strength and self-rated squat ability with demographics/behaviour predicts MCI at AUC 0.719-0.732, with the combined limb-function model reclassifying over either limb alone (NRI 0.3279/0.1862).
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-993 (Dang et al. 2023, Alzheimers Res Ther 15:27; BABRI n=155 + ADNI n=286): hippocampus-centred grey-matter covariance networks (random forest) predict MCI development (AUC 0.692-0.792) and reversion (AUC 0.701-0.809) from structural MRI.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: The pair defines a two-tier screening-confirmation pathway with orthogonal feature spaces: P-994's zero-cost body-function model operates at population scale where MRI is impossible, while P-993's network-covariance model operates at imaging centres where reversion-relevant brain-state detail is recoverable; because the feature spaces share no variables (dynamometry/self-report vs T1 covariance), their errors are structurally uncorrelated, so the community tier can pre-stratify and the imaging tier adjudicate - a design neither paper proposes alone.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Stepped MCI screening in low-resource systems: community limb-function triage with imaging-centre covariance confirmation for flagged individuals, reserving MRI for the pre-stratified fraction.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-996 (Zhang et al. 2023, Int J Gen Med 16:785-792; de novo PD n=387): cross-sectional two-marker panel - periventricular WMH volumetry plus plasma homocysteine - predicts PD-MCI at AUC 0.879, far above either marker alone (0.701/0.688).
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-997 (Meng et al. 2023, CNS Neurosci Ther 29:2259-2266; PPMI n=423, 5y): longitudinal NPS profiling shows depression/anxiety accelerate decline across all four cognitive domains while apathy and ICDs mark domain-specific trajectories.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: In early Parkinson's disease the two papers occupy orthogonal risk axes for the same outcome: P-996 supplies a baseline structural-metabolic stratification (who is already MCI or near it), P-997 supplies the behavioural trajectory layer (whose cognition will decline fastest and in which domain); combining the AUC-0.879 cross-sectional panel with NPS domain mapping yields a baseline-plus-trajectory surveillance design that neither cross-sectional imaging nor longitudinal questionnaires alone can deliver.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: PD-clinic cognitive surveillance: PWMH+Hcy panel at diagnosis for baseline stratification, with NPS-triggered domain-specific monitoring for decline anticipation.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-988 (Parra et al. 2022, Alzheimers Dement DADM 14:e12386; n=107): task-embedded eye tracking during VSTMB predicts MCI-to-ADS conversion with 94%-vs-0% separation over 40 months using a 10-minute monitor-based test.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-978 (US care-outcome prognostic model): Harrell's C 0.81 for institutionalisation (0.76 without biomarkers) and 0.79 for mortality in SCD/MCI, integrating cognitive testing with routine biomarkers for care-outcome stratification.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: The pair spans the clinical prognostic chain at matching affordability: P-988 detects who will cross the MCI-to-ADS threshold (event onset), P-978 predicts what care outcomes follow once impairment is established (institutionalisation/mortality); because P-988's digital test costs a fraction of the biomarker panel P-978 needs for its best discrimination, the two jointly specify a low-cost sequential pipeline - oculomotor conversion screening upstream, biomarker-augmented care planning downstream.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Memory-clinic pathway design: brief oculomotor conversion screening to trigger comprehensive biomarker-based care-outcome planning for converters.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-998 reports population-based NPC association with MMSE-defined MCI (AUC 0.764; cutoff >8.5 cm).
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1006 reports eye-movement task features plus MMSE classifying MCI with AUROC 0.840.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Static convergence impairment and task-embedded saccade dynamics represent complementary ocular-cognitive screening layers, with the former offering simple population triage and the latter adding executive-process information.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Use NPC as low-cost referral triage and validated eye-movement testing as a second-stage assessment, not as interchangeable diagnoses.

complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1002 uses OMOP EHR treatment-effect estimation to compare antihypertensive, statin, SSRI and PPI associations after MCI.

complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1006 finds eye-movement features add MCI classification information beyond demographics and MMSE.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1011 finds baseline semantic-memory impairment and the phonological-semantic fluency discrepancy flag MCI-to-dementia conversion years before episodic-memory decline, across fast/intermediate/slow converter strata.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1012 finds pre-diagnosis prescription phenotypes from EMR associate with conversion: mixed and cardio-metabolic profiles are protective versus the low-prescription profile while psychotropic burden marks risk.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Conversion risk can be stratified from two orthogonal pre-conversion data layers that never meet in a single paper: cognitive-linguistic micro-markers index the neurodegenerative process while medication-record phenotypes index the cardiometabolic-psychiatric comorbidity context; composed, they define a two-layer screening stack requiring neither imaging nor fluid biomarkers.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: A memory-clinic intake could pair a fluency-discrepancy item with a pharmacy-record phenotype check as a dual-layer triage, each layer catching conversions the other misses; validation must precede deployment.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1009 finds patients retain almost none of their MCI diagnosis: only 21% use the term, 25% attribute problems to a pathological cause, and 60% say causes were never discussed.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1017 finds psychiatrists personally diagnose two-thirds of their MCI/mild-AD patients and receive referrals for 92% of them, yet only 46% view themselves as coordinators of care.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: The MCI disclosure deficit is systemic rather than patient-side: specialists diagnose at volume while patients retain almost none of the label or its implications, and no actor claims coordination, so the communication breakdown spans both ends of the diagnostic encounter across two health systems.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Disclosure should be treated as a process outcome with an assigned owner; awareness campaigns and written personalised feedback target the patient half while explicit coordination roles target the physician half.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1101 (ADNI-3 n=244): nucleus reuniens (thalamic) atrophy distinguishes MCI-to-AD converters from stable MCI and predicts conversion (sens 0.73/spec 0.69) via subcortical structural volumetry.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1107 (NCKUH n=86): eZIS SPECT AD-pattern hypoperfusion severity predicts 3-year MCI-to-dementia conversion (AUC 0.719, cutoff 1.22) via cerebral perfusion imaging.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Subcortical structural atrophy of the limbic nucleus reuniens and SPECT-quantified AD-pattern hypoperfusion predict the same MCI-to-dementia conversion trajectory through anatomically distinct substrates (structure vs perfusion), so the two imaging axes are complementary for prodromal-AD conversion triage rather than interchangeable.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Combining structural subcortical volumetry with low-cost SPECT perfusion could strengthen prodromal-AD conversion stratification when either single modality is nondiagnostic.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1116 (IRCCS Casa Sollievo geriatrics, n=181): SCI/aMCI associated with elevated 2-yr incidence of major acute vascular events (ischemic stroke/heart attack) - 7.4-12.2% across groups - and 37% aMCI-MD dementia progression.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1117 (IHCNP, n=100 post-ischemic-stroke MCI): significant 18-month cognitive decline (MMSE -8.7%, MoCA -10.0%, RAVLT -29.5%, p<0.0001) documenting progressive post-stroke MCI.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Read together, an MCI/SCI diagnosis signals elevated impending stroke/AMI risk on the one hand (P-1116) while a prior ischemic stroke drives further progressive MCI decline on the other (P-1117), jointly exposing a bidirectional vascular-cognition coupling: cognitive impairment and cerebrovascular events each predict and perpetuate the other. Neither single-centre cohort alone demonstrates this two-way loop, so the pairing is a cross-paper (not single-paper) discovery.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Care for MCI/SCI patients should include cardiovascular monitoring for impending stroke/AMI, and post-stroke patients need longitudinal cognitive tracking for progressive MCI, making the vascular-cognitive interface part of routine dementia and stroke follow-up.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1118 (Wuxi memory clinic, n=295): a routine serum + diet logistic nomogram predicts MCI (MoCA<26) with train AUC 0.86 / test AUC 0.79, from low-cost blood (RBC, NLR, LDL/HDL) and dietary factors.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1122 (post-HSCT malignant-haematology, dev n=282): a routine clinical-serological logistic risk model predicts MCI after transplant with AUC 0.897 training / 0.789 external validation.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Independent logistic models built on routine serum and clinical data achieve viable MCI risk discrimination (AUC ~0.79-0.90) in two very different populations - community memory-clinic elderly and oncology survivors after HSCT - so low-cost serological screening generalises across clinical settings without specialist neuroimaging, and the two collectively span both case-control (P-1118) and externally validated (P-1122) designs.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: A routine-blood MCI risk score calibrated in one clinical population can plausibly transfer to another, supporting low-cost opportunistic cognitive screening in memory clinics and transplant survivors alike.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, High): independent groups built logistic models on routine blood/clinical data in radically different clinical settings with convergent AUCs (~0.79-0.90); the cross-population contrast (community memory-clinic vs post-transplant oncology, case-control vs externally-validated) makes the generalisability claim earned.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1124 (physical-activity cohort): modifiable behavioural factor protective against MCI-to-dementia conversion over years (protective association).
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1126 (n=128 total, mixed CI/MCI/AD): momentary motor-task variability predicts short-term (one-year) cognitive decline; effect size modest (eta^2 0.04-0.05).
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Modifiable, easily-measured behavioural factors predict cognitive trajectory from opposite ends: physical activity protects against MCI-to-dementia conversion over years (P-1124) while momentary motor-task variability flags who will decline over one year (P-1126) - together showing low-cost behavioural surveillance (activity level + motor consistency) offers both long-horizon protective associations and short-horizon decline prediction without neuroimaging.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Combining physical-activity history with a brief motor-variability task is a promising low-cost screening approach for stratifying short- and long-term cognitive risk in MCI/PD patients, pending validation in larger MCI-only cohorts.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Minor Revision): conceptual frame strong (modifiable behavioural factors from opposite temporal horizons). Caveat applied per operator: P-1126 is small (n=128 mixed CI/MCI/AD) with modest effect size, so the clinical implication is tempered to a promising screening approach requiring validation in larger MCI-only cohorts.
complementary_findings.residual_caveat: P-1126 sample small (n=128, mixed) and effect modest (eta^2 0.04-0.05); recommendation is a promising screening approach pending larger MCI-only replication.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1133 (ADNI, n=796): 2-year MCI reversion rate 18.17%; reverters carry 89.6% lower AD-dementia risk than stable MCI (HR 0.104, 0.033-0.335) and match stable NC across cognition, brain volume, metabolism and CSF amyloid trajectories.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1135 (ADNI-sourced, n=1019 / 4657 obs): functional multistate model shows reversion probability rising from 2% to ~8% by year 10 and post-reversion re-progression to MCI reaching 35.71% by year 10, with reverters remaining at elevated deterioration risk.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Read together, MCI reversion is both prognostically favourable versus stable MCI in the short term (P-1133: reverters match NC on AD hazard and four biomarker domains) and dynamically unstable in the long term (P-1135: ~36% of post-reversion subjects re-progress to MCI within a decade). The two ADNI-sourced studies jointly define reversion as a real, partially favourable transition that still demands monitoring, so neither the favourable-reversion narrative nor the at-risk-reverter narrative is complete alone.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Reversion status should not terminate follow-up: reverters need continued longitudinal monitoring because a substantial minority re-progress to MCI/AD within 10 years.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, High): despite both being ADNI-sourced, the pairing is methodologically sound because the insight is temporal (short-term favourable vs long-term unstable reversion), resolving an apparent literature contradiction. ADNI sourcing noted as a limitation, not a disqualifier.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1132 (Japan population cohort, n=2118, 5-y): technology-updated NCGG-ADL IADL scale predicts dementia risk (IADL limitation HR 1.55) and MCI+IADL limitation jointly raise hazard to HR 2.88.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1137 (UK Biobank matched cohort, n=6605 MCI): MCI carries modestly higher healthcare costs (inpatient +7.6% over 10y, primary care +9.1% over 6y) but AD-dementia incidence is 7.2x higher and AD dementia drives most incremental cost (mean GBP 20,199 extra inpatient cost).
complementary_findings.combined_insight: A self-report functional (IADL) scale combined with MCI status doubles dementia risk (P-1132), while dementia conversion - not MCI itself - is the dominant cost driver (P-1137); jointly they show that low-cost functional screening of MCI+IADL patients targets precisely the subgroup whose downstream dementia-related costs are highest.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Prioritising NCGG-ADL-style IADL screening among MCI patients could identify high-hazard, high-cost individuals for early intervention before AD-dementia cost accrues.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, High): strong health-policy pairing. P-1132 identifies the high-risk subgroup (MCI+IADL, HR 2.88); P-1137 shows dementia conversion drives costs. Cross-population (Japan vs UK) mitigated by large sample sizes in both.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1141 (AIBL, n=238 dev + 30 val): the Florey Fusion Model uses only non-invasive data (age, sex, APOE-e4, neuropsychological tests) to predict MCI-to-AD progression with mAUC-ROC 0.91 and 3-year CDR-SB/MMSE forecasts (mMAE 1.32 / 1.51).
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1143 (ADNI dev n=494 CN, AIBL validation n=320): ML survival analysis with demographics, cognitive scores and baseline comorbidities predicts CN-to-MCI transition with fast-RSF C-index 0.84 (bootstrapped 0.8607; external AIBL 0.73-0.77).
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Two adjacent prodromal transitions are predicted from purely non-invasive clinical data by distinct computational strategies: P-1143 extends the survival-modelling horizon to the very first CN-to-MCI step using comorbidity-enriched feature sets, while P-1141 carries the same non-invasive principle one stage later across MCI-to-AD with a three-year forecast window. Read together they bound the entire CN-to-AD risk trajectory with cheap, routine data and without specialist imaging or CSF, so risk-based triage can start at cognitive normality and continue through MCI.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: A ladder of non-invasive models (P-1143 covering CN-to-MCI; P-1141 covering MCI-to-AD) provides a proof-of-concept framework for serial low-cost risk monitoring from cognitive normality through MCI without MRI/PET/CSF, awaiting larger validation.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Major Caveat): the ladder-of-non-invasive-models concept is excellent, but P-1141's validation is only n=30 and mAUC 0.91 with a 3-year forecast on 30 participants is not ready for clinical triage. Clinical implication downgraded from 'enables serial monitoring' to a proof-of-concept framework awaiting larger validation.
complementary_findings.residual_caveat: P-1141 validated on only n=30; model is proof-of-concept framework for risk monitoring, not clinical triage until larger validation.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1138 (Newcastle MCI-LB, n=74): time-varying core-feature accumulation predicts faster ACE-R decline in MCI-LB (visual hallucinations -2.1/yr, cognitive fluctuations -3.4/yr), and baseline-only features are not prognostic.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1140 (NACC, AD n=397 / LB n=37): interval-censored survival with pathology-specific neurocognitive predictors distinguishes AD vs LB MCI-to-dementia conversion (daily-living/depression/Trail A-B for LB; orientation/memory/irritability for AD).
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Both MCI-LB-focused records argue that the Lewy-body prodromal track cannot be read through an Alzheimer lens: P-1138 shows the DLB clinical phenotype (fluctuations/hallucinations) is the dynamic and prognostically informative signal in MCI-LB, while P-1140 shows different neurocognitive and functional domains predict LB versus AD conversion. Together they mean LB MCI needs its own clinical-feature surveillance (P-1138) and its own cognitive/functional predictor set (P-1140) rather than AD-derived instruments.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Lewy-body MCI surveillance should combine serial core-feature tracking (fluctuations/hallucinations) with LB-appropriate functional/depression/Trail measures, not AD memory/irritability predictors alone; LB-specific predictors need replication in larger Lewy-body cohorts.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Minor Revision): clinically important message that LB MCI cannot be managed with AD-derived instruments; endpoints complementary (decline rate vs conversion). Caveat applied: P-1140 LB cohort is tiny (n=37), so LB-specific predictors need replication in larger Lewy-body cohorts.
complementary_findings.residual_caveat: P-1140 LB cohort n=37; LB-specific predictor set needs replication in larger Lewy-body cohorts.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1142 (ADNI, n=811 MCI): longitudinal GDS-15 depressive trajectories predict cognitive decline and MCI-to-dementia conversion only in men (Cluster C HR 2.69), null in women.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1146 (Florence SCD, n=440): women have lower cognitive reserve (TIB 109.6 vs 114.9) but cognitive reserve (OR 0.88) - not gender - predicts SCD-to-MCI progression.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Two complementary sex/gender-modulated psychological determinants act on adjacent prodromal stages: in MCI the dynamic course of depressive symptoms is prognostic for men specifically (P-1142), while in the earlier SCD stage a dispositional resilience factor (premorbid intelligence/cognitive reserve) carries the progression signal and does so independently of gender despite lower female reserve (P-1146). The pairing shows psychological risk (depression dynamics) and psychological resilience (CR) are distinct, stage-specific, and sex/gender-sensitively coded determinants of decline, arguing for sex-stratified, psychiatrically-informed monitoring across SCD and MCI.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Depression-trajectory monitoring (male-sensitive) and cognitive-reserve-aware counselling (gender-neutral in SCD) are complementary, low-cost additions to prodromal risk assessment.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, High): sophisticated sex-stratified synthesis; identifies depression dynamics as male-specific in MCI and cognitive reserve as gender-neutral in SCD. Stage-specificity (risk factor in MCI, resilience in SCD) clinically useful; both cohorts adequately sized. Model cross-fertilization entry.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1154 (ADNI, n=1136 CN): competing-risks model shows baseline FDG-PET hypometabolism determines progression pathway selection, with severe hypometabolism (z<=-0.5) yielding 7.4x acceleration in direct normal-to-dementia conversion velocity; direct AD conversion predicted at AUC 0.994 (24/36-mo).
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1153 (ADNI, J-ADNI, HABS): an FDG-PET AD-vs-NC diagnostic CNN, repurposed as a similarity score, independently predicts pre-dementia cognitive decline (ADNI-MCI HR 3.45; iAUC 0.787 vs 0.768 baseline) with external validation.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Together these two FDG-PET studies advance prognosis from binary conversion to pathway-level and cross-stage stratification in the pre-symptomatic phase: P-1154's competing-risks framework models WHICH trajectory a cognitively normal individual follows (stability, sequential MCI, accelerated, or rapid direct AD) driven by baseline metabolism, while P-1153's deep-learning similarity score adds discriminative pre-dementia risk on the same FDG-PET signal and external-generalizability checks. The pairing shows FDG hypometabolism simultaneously encodes pathway selection (P-1154) and an AD-diagnosis-informed prognosis (P-1153), arguing that metabolic stratification and DL-derived AD-similarity are complementary, not redundant, for early risk assessment.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Combining FDG z-score pathway thresholds with a DL AD-similarity prognosis could stratify cognitively normal and pre-dementia individuals for pathway-specific monitoring, but this is hypothesis-generating for trial enrichment (not clinical deployment) pending consensus cut-offs and further external validation of both.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Major Caveat): conceptual distinction strong (pathway selection vs similarity-score risk) and P-1153 external validation a strength. Caveat applied: P-1154 reports AUC 0.994 for direct conversion, near-perfect discrimination raising overfitting concerns even at n=1136; both candidate-only. Implication framed as hypothesis-generating for trial enrichment, not clinical deployment.
complementary_findings.residual_caveat: P-1154 AUC 0.994 flags possible overfitting in a competing-risks frame; both candidate-only, so framed as hypothesis-generating for trial enrichment.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1150 (NACC, 2005-2021, n=4560): among MCI patients, APOE e4 carriage and cardiometabolic comorbidity were associated with AD conversion; two conditions versus one carried HR 1.17 (diabetes and hypertension) and 1.20 (diabetes and hypercholesterolemia), APOE e4/4 HRs 2.68-4.09 and e3/4 1.59-2.32, and e4/4 with diabetes and hypertension HR 7.6. The authors do not suggest a causal inference.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1151 (TriNetX federated EHR, n=31806 matched MCI): cardiometabolic conditions predict condition-specific dementia-subtype transitions - T2 diabetes to vascular dementia (HR 1.33), hyperlipidemia to AD (HR 1.21).
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Two large, mutually independent data architectures (NACC clinical registry vs TriNetX federated EHR) both find modest observational associations between cardiometabolic conditions and faster MCI-to-dementia progression (P-1151 single-condition HRs 1.07-1.33; P-1150 two-versus-one-condition HRs 1.17 and 1.20), with condition-specific dementia-subtype patterns: P-1150 reports larger risks with APOE e4 for AD conversion, while in P-1151 diabetes is associated with vascular dementia (HR 1.33) and hyperlipidemia is the only condition associated with AD (HR 1.21; obesity null overall). Neither measures a cardiometabolic 'burden' construct or supports a causal reading.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Associational only: comorbidity- and APOE-stratified risk estimates may be informative for MCI prognosis; whether treating hypertension, diabetes or hyperlipidemia changes dementia-subtype transition risk is not tested by either study.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, High), 2026-08-30. Wording made non-causal on 2026-09-26 by operator decision (prior text preserved under human_evaluation_note_pre_2026_09_26).
complementary_findings.finding_a_pre_2026_09_26: P-1150 (NACC, 2005-2021, n=4560): APOE-e4 and combined comorbidities synergistically drive MCI-to-AD conversion, with e4/4 + diabetes & hypertension giving HR 7.6; APOE4 and co-morbidity each HR ~1.17-1.20.
complementary_findings.combined_insight_pre_2026_09_26: Two large, mutually-independent cohorts (NACC clinical registry vs TriNetX federated EHR) converge on cardiometabolic burden as an MCI-to-dementia driver, but P-1151 delineates the target outcome: P-1150 quantifies the genetic (APOE4) interaction and multiplicative combined-comorbidity risk on AD conversion, while P-1151 decomposes the SAME cardiometabolic exposure into condition-to-subtype specificity (diabetes preferentially to vascular, hyperlipidemia to AD). The pairing shows cardiometabolic comorbidity is not a single MCI-outcome risk but an outcome-path-selecting one, and that APOE genotype modulates its strength - a continuum from genotype x comorbidity interaction (NACC) to subtype-resolved comorbidity mapping (TriNetX).
complementary_findings.clinical_implication_pre_2026_09_26: Calls for comorbidity-specific and APOE-stratified MCI management (e.g. treating hypertension/diabetes/hyperlipidemia may differentially cut AD vs vascular dementia transition risk) rather than a single cardiometabolic-risk score.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note_pre_2026_09_26: G4 ACCEPT (operator, High): best-in-class pairing. Two massive, mutually independent cohorts (NACC registry vs TriNetX federated EHR) converge on cardiometabolic burden with distinct granularity (genetic interaction vs subtype decomposition). Clinical implication for comorbidity-specific, APOE-stratified management directly actionable.

text_correction_2026_09_26.by: operator decision in session on 2026-09-26, taken after reviewing the round-14 audit of an external reviewer's 90 comments on v1.3 (each checked against the source PDFs by an auditor agent and an independent challenger)
text_correction_2026_09_26.change: finding_a, combined_insight and clinical_implication reworded in non-causal terms and the HR error corrected against the P-1150 and P-1151 PDFs (P-1150 Discussion: 'We do not suggest a causal inference'); status unchanged

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1160 (ADNI, n=756 MCI, 36-mo): three-class multinomial model - higher education, larger hippocampal volume and lower daily functional impairment predict reversion, while APOE e4, poorer memory and fusiform atrophy predict progression (accuracy 78%).
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1164 (Navarra memory clinic, n=450 SCD, 2001-2017): within globally normal scores, lower CERAD verbal memory (HR 0.580 per SD, trial 1) and slower TMT-B (HR 1.239) predict SCD progression to MCI/AD dementia; vascular factors not independent after adjustment.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Together the two studies bracket a reserve-vs-deficit dissociation across the prodromal span: at the SCD stage, test-level memory and executive slowing within normal global scores carry the progression signal (P-1164), whereas once MCI is established, durable reversal is governed by reserve markers - education and hippocampal volume - plus preserved daily function rather than by further deficit depth (P-1160). Read jointly, the predictive architecture shifts from deficit accumulation (pre-MCI) to reserve-based resilience (MCI), implying different monitoring instruments and counselling logics per stage.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: SCD monitoring should weight SD-level neuropsych deficits (CERAD trials, TMT-B); established-MCI counselling about reversibility should weight education, hippocampal volume and daily function rather than deficit scores alone.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, High): sophisticated stage-differentiated synthesis - the predictive architecture shifts from deficit accumulation in SCD to reserve-based resilience in MCI; resolves the monitor-deficits-vs-protective-factors confusion. Adequately powered (n=756, n=450); different designs (multinomial vs Cox) and cohorts complementary, not conflicting.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1161 (narrative review): the MMSE shows reduced sensitivity for MCI, underestimates mild deficits and undercaptures executive/fluency domains; alternative instruments are needed for early detection.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1163 (Japan, n=74): UFOV peripheral-field reaction time detects MCI at AUC 0.841 (cutoff 598.1 ms; sens 90.3%/spec 72.1%) while central-field reaction time shows no group difference.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: The pairing converts a psychometric critique into a concrete detection route: P-1161 documents that language- and education-loaded screeners such as the MMSE systematically miss mild deficits, and P-1163 demonstrates that a peripheral visual-attention reaction-time measure, which does not depend on language or education, separates MCI from healthy ageing with moderate-good accuracy. Jointly they argue the insensitivity problem is partially architectural (verbal-load dependence of conventional screeners), so education-light behavioural markers complement rather than merely replace verbal tests.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: UFOV-RT is a promising proof-of-concept complement to verbal screeners for low-education or multilingual settings, warranting validation in larger multicultural cohorts before deployment.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Major Caveat): conceptual framing strong (insensitivity problem is architectural - verbal-load dependence - not just cutoffs). Caveat applied per operator: P-1163 is single-centre n=74 with modest specificity 72.1% (high FP rate in low-prevalence settings) and P-1161 is a narrative review providing framing, not quantitative failure rates. Clinical implication revised to proof-of-concept requiring larger multicultural validation.
complementary_findings.residual_caveat: P-1163 single-centre n=74, spec 72.1% (high FP in low prevalence); P-1161 narrative review only. UFOV-RT is proof-of-concept until validated in larger multicultural cohorts.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1165 (MYHAT, n=1805, 8 yr): LIBRA2 - adding sleep disturbance, hearing impairment and low social contact - predicts incident dementia (HR 1.04-1.40 per point) but is not consistently associated with incident MCI.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1159 (CHF cohort, n=329, cross-sectional): poor sleep quality (PSQI) is independently associated with MCI presence (OR 1.257 per point; 58% MCI prevalence) in chronic heart failure patients.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Together the studies position sleep as a modifiable cognitive-risk axis whose observable strength depends on disease context: in a general late-life population sleep disturbance contributes to dementia-stage risk only within a multi-factor index (P-1165), whereas in a cardiac comorbidity population, where MCI prevalence is far higher (58%), sleep quality shows a strong direct, independent MCI association (P-1159). Jointly they imply sleep's cognitive signal is amplified in organ-disease populations, so sleep assessment may be most informative as a targeted screen inside comorbidity care rather than as a standalone general-population dementia predictor.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Embed PSQI-based sleep screening in CHF and similar comorbidity pathways; treat sleep as a supporting (not standalone) factor in general-population dementia-risk indices such as LIBRA2.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, High): excellent contextual-modulation insight - sleep's cognitive-risk signal is population-dependent (diluted in a general multi-factor index, strong and independent in high-MCI-prevalence cardiac comorbidity). Clinical implication proportionate; P-1159 cross-sectional design handled without overclaiming causality.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1166 (bibliometric, 7,568 articles 1999-2024): MCI imaging-diagnosis research pivots toward AI/ML and multimodal imaging for diagnosis and risk prediction.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1164 (Navarra memory clinic, n=450 SCD): standard neuropsych battery markers (CERAD recall, TMT-B) carry strong, covariate-adjusted progression signal in SCD without any imaging or AI component.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: The pairing exposes an evaluation asymmetry in the field: the bibliometric centre of gravity is moving to AI-multimodal diagnosis (P-1166), yet in the earliest symptomatic-at-risk stage (SCD) the strongest published progression signals remain conventional, low-cost neuropsych markers requiring no scanner or model (P-1164). Together they imply that AI-multimodal MCI prediction benchmarks should be required to demonstrate incremental value over standardised neuropsych batteries, which are the implicit comparator most new models skip.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Trial enrichment and screening in SCD can remain neuropsych-first; AI-multimodal models should be benchmarked against CERAD/TMT-class baselines to demonstrate added clinical value.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, High): meta-scientific pairing of unusual quality - bibliometric centre-of-gravity shift to AI-multimodal imaging vs clinical anchor that standard neuropsych batteries still carry the strongest SCD progression signal; exposes a genuine benchmarking gap (AI models rarely required to beat CERAD/TMT baselines). Scope mismatch is the point.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1168 (CEP program design, Emory/Georgia Tech): a co-designed four-core multidomain MCI lifestyle programme (therapeutic, technology, built-environment, innovation cores) with empowerment-driven co-design, WHO-ICF-adapted framework, 6-month curriculum, pre/post assessment battery (MoCA, motor, mood, QoL, caregiver burden) and lifestyle-biomarker sensing.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1170 (Nanjing qualitative, n=20 MCI): MTM-grounded interviews identify a two-stage account of multidomain-intervention behaviour - initiation barriers (anosognosia, access, cost) differ from maintenance drivers (short-term outcome expectations, habit), surfaced as 2 themes/11 subthemes with thematic saturation.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: P-1168 specs the content architecture of a multidomain MCI programme (four cores + biomarker sensing) but is silent on how participants are carried from initiation into maintained adherence; P-1170 supplies exactly that behavioural mechanism - initiation and maintenance are distinct, differently-barriered stages. Together they imply a programme built like P-1168 needs stage-matched adherence strategies (anosognosia/cost mitigation at entry; short-term-outcome reinforcement later) rather than a single engagement model - design paper (P-1168) and behaviour paper (P-1170) jointly expose the missing adherence-engineering layer.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Multidomain MCI programme rollout should pair content design with a two-stage adherence model: mitigate anosognosia/access at initiation and provide short-term-outcome feedback loops for maintenance.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, High): Design science paired with implementation science. P-1168 specifies a four-core multidomain architecture but is silent on adherence; P-1170 supplies the behavioural mechanism (initiation vs maintenance barriers). The combined insight - that programmes need stage-matched adherence engineering - is immediately actionable and non-obvious from either paper alone.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1169 (WHO ICTRP landscape, 2,609 MCI trials): the global MCI trial portfolio is large and tilting toward non-pharmacological interventions (1,344 non-pharm vs 399 pharmacological) including AI-VR approaches, with 51.8% registered in the last 5 years yet only 8.28% sharing results.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1170 (Nanjing qualitative, n=20 MCI): patient-level initiation and maintenance of multidomain interventions hinge on distinct barriers (anosognosia, access, cost; short-term-outcome expectations) - the behavioural envelope within which any such non-pharmacological trial operates.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: The registry (P-1169) shows the field is scaling non-pharmacological/AI multidomain interventions faster than it demonstrates their results (92% never share outcomes); P-1170 shows that these interventions must first clear a patient-adherence stage that precedes the efficacy stage. Together they establish adherence as a necessary condition for powered, reportable completion of multidomain trials. No causal claim is made about the registry's low results-sharing rate: non-reporting is driven by publication bias, commercial sensitivity and investigator non-compliance at least as much as by participant dropout, and the two observations are juxtaposed here rather than causally linked.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Registry-level investment in multidomain MCI trials should be matched by implementation-science funding, because adherence (P-1170) is a necessary condition for the non-pharmacological trials P-1169 counts to reach powered, reportable completions. This does not explain the registry's low results-sharing rate and should not be read as doing so.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Moderate) - major caveat: The core insight - that adherence is a binding constraint on multidomain trial completion - is valid and important. However, the leap from 'low results-sharing' (92% never share) to 'adherence is the root cause' is speculative. Low results-sharing is driven by publication bias, commercial sensitivity and investigator non-compliance at least as much as by patient dropout. Revised framing applied: causal claim about results-sharing removed; implementation-science funding recommendation retained.
complementary_findings.operator_caveat: Operator G4 required this caveat to appear as an explicit limitation in the manuscript text, not as a quality-flag footnote. The combined_insight / clinical_implication above already carry it.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1171 (AI-Mind early HTA, Dutch perspective): decision-tree + lifetime Markov model finds MCI dementia-risk-prediction tooling is NOT cost-effective in base case (current practice dominant, 9.36 vs 9.32 QALYs) - prediction only becomes cost-effective when paired with a cheap, wide-target intervention the tool stratifies people toward.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1168 (CEP program design): a co-designed four-core multidomain MCI lifestyle programme designed for wide, comparatively non-invasive delivery (therapeutic/technology/built-environment/innovation) - precisely the kind of cheap, broad, non-pharmacological lever the HTA's headroom depends on.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: P-1171's economic headroom for MCI risk-prediction is gated on a low-cost, wide-target downstream intervention existing; P-1168 is that intervention as a design - but it carries no efficacy or utilisation data. Together they expose that cost-effectiveness of MCI prediction is limited not by model accuracy but by the availability of a validated cheap wide-target programme: P-1168's four cores are the plausible candidate, yet without outcome data the HTA's ICER stays dominated, so the binding research gap is programme efficacy rather than the prediction model itself.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Health-economic justification of MCI risk-stratification should redirect investment from model refinement toward validating cheap wide-target multidomain programmes, because that is the lever that flips the ICER.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, High): Excellent health-economics cross-fertilisation. The HTA establishes that prediction is only cost-effective if paired with a cheap, wide-target downstream intervention; P-1168 is exactly that intervention as a design spec, but carries no efficacy data. The combined insight correctly redirects research investment from model refinement to programme validation. A rare example of economic modelling directly informing research prioritisation.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1176 (punicalagin nutraceutical review): pomegranate polyphenol punicalagin alleviates MCI in multiple preclinical models (prenatal stress, sleep-deprivation, D-gal, APP/PS1) via antioxidative damage, anti-neuroinflammation, neurogenesis and neurotransmitter regulation, with gut-microbiota conversion to urolithins; oral bioavailability 18.17% is the key clinical barrier.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1177 (vitamin C, D-gal mouse MCI model): VC supplementation improved spatial memory and hippocampal integrity, suppressed inflammation/oxidative stress, enriched SCFA-producing microbiota (Akkermansia, Ruminococcus, Butyricicoccus) and raised acetic/propionic/butyric acid, with SCFAs positively correlating with probiotic abundance - a gut-brain-axis mechanism.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: P-1176 and P-1177 independently nominate the gut-microbiome - metabolite axis as a convergent nutraceutical mechanism for MCI: punicalagin acts partly through gut-microbiota urolithin metabolism (P-1176) while vitamin C acts through SCFA-producing flora restoration (P-1177). Together they contrast two gut-mediated bioactives (polyphenol-derived urolithins vs microbially-generated SCFAs) as distinct, mechanistically-complementary non-pharmacological levers, and both converge on the same unifying gap - neither effect has been validated with gut-biomarker endpoints or SCFA/urolithin measurement in a human MCI cohort.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Gut-microbiome-targeted nutraceuticals (polyphenols and vitamin C) are plausible complementary MCI-prevention strategies, but require human trials that measure microbial metabolites (urolithins, SCFAs) alongside cognition.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Moderate): Two preclinical gut-brain axis mechanisms converge on distinct microbial metabolites (urolithins vs SCFAs). The insight that polyphenol-derived and vitamin-C-derived gut bioactives are mechanistically complementary is non-obvious. Both legs are preclinical, so the clinical implication (human trials with metabolite endpoints) is proportionate.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1180 (EMCOA case-control, N=364): vitamin D deficiency (<20 ng/mL) tripled the odds of MCI (25(OH)D AUC 0.72, cut-off 16.5 ng/mL), with serum 25(OH)D negatively correlating with total cholesterol (r=-0.19), LDL (r=-0.17) and 24S,25-epoxycholesterol (r=-0.21), and positively with MoCA and SDMT - linking vitamin-D status, cholesterol/oxysterol homeostasis and cognition.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1177 (vitamin C, D-gal mouse MCI model): VC improved spatial memory and hippocampal integrity, enriched SCFA-producing microbiota and raised SCFA levels via the gut-brain axis, reducing inflammation and oxidative stress.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: P-1180 (human serum 25(OH)D/cholesterol/oxysterol - cognition associations) and P-1177 (mouse gut-SCFA - cognition mechanism) each implicate a peripheral metabolic state in cognitive health, and are placed side by side as a broad hypothesis-generating synthesis only. They are not mechanistically linked here: the exposures differ (vitamin D vs vitamin C), the species and designs differ (human observational vs mouse interventional), and the pathways measured - systemic cholesterol/oxysterol handling vs gut-derived SCFA production - have no demonstrated connection in either paper or elsewhere in this corpus. What the pairing supports is the weaker claim that metabolic disruption of more than one kind tracks cognitive status across scales, and that no study has measured both axes in the same participants.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Hypothesis-generating only. A human study measuring vitamin D, cholesterol/oxysterols and gut-derived metabolites in the same participants would establish whether these metabolic axes are related at all. No claim is made that the two mechanisms are connected, and no metabolic screening panel or nutrition-based intervention is recommended on the strength of this pairing.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Moderate) - major caveat: The 'metabolism-disruption continuum' framing is elegant, but the cross-species, cross-exposure pairing (human vitamin D observational + mouse vitamin C interventional) is a long inferential leap. The two exposures differ (D vs C), the species differ, and the mechanisms (cholesterol/oxysterol vs gut SCFA) are not obviously connected. Accepted only as a broad hypothesis-generating synthesis; the direct-mechanism implication has been removed.
complementary_findings.operator_caveat: Operator G4 required this caveat to appear as an explicit limitation in the manuscript text, not as a quality-flag footnote. The combined_insight / clinical_implication above already carry it.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1184 (rat MI, early-remodeling MCI): hippocampal-dependent MCI with elevated brain oxidative stress and apoptosis (cleaved caspase-3) and reduced neurogenesis/dendritic spines, INDEPENDENT of LVEF severity; brain inflammation (Iba-1, NF-kB, TNF-a, TLR4) and AD proteins unchanged.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1185 (human DLB/AD/aMCI vs HC): peripheral inflammation (IL-6 up vs AD/HC; IL-10, IL-17A up) and oxidative imbalance (SOD down, MDA up) in DLB and AD; UPDRS correlates with CRP.
