complementary_findings.combined_insight: Two independent origins of MCI (cardiac-brain in a rat MI model vs peripheral-immune/oxidative in human DLB/AD/aMCI) converge on OXIDATIVE STRESS as the common thread while diverging on inflammation: P-1184 finds brain inflammation is NOT elevated in early cardiac-driven MCI, whereas P-1185 finds peripheral inflammation IS elevated in neurodegenerative MCI. Together they imply oxidative stress is a shared early driver across MCI aetiologies, whereas an inflammatory signature may be disease-context-dependent (neurodegenerative vs cardiac) - a cross-model, cross-compartment dissociation neither paper shows alone.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Oxidative stress is a candidate common early target across MCI aetiologies, so redox-focused biomarkers and antioxidant interventions merit evaluation in both cardiac- and neurodegenerative-driven MCI populations, with the inflammatory signature used as a differential (peripheral-inflammatory) rather than universal axis. Because the pairing bridges a rat cardiac model and a human neurodegenerative cohort, it is a hypothesis-generating bridge: the redox biomarkers require validation in human cardiac-cognitive cohorts before the cross-aetiology generalisation is asserted.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Moderate) - minor caveat: The oxidative-stress-commonality / inflammation-dissociation insight is genuinely interesting. However, the cross-species comparison (rat cardiac model vs human neurodegenerative cohort) limits inferential strength. Accepted as a hypothesis-generating bridge, with the clinical implication now stating explicitly that redox biomarkers need validation in human cardiac-cognitive cohorts before generalisation.
complementary_findings.operator_caveat: Operator G4 required this caveat to appear as an explicit limitation in the manuscript text, not as a quality-flag footnote. The combined_insight / clinical_implication above already carry it.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1186 (BZYQD, reserpine rat MCI + PC12): BZYQD improves MCI by repairing mitochondrial oxidative DNA damage (reduced 8-OH-dG) via the SIRT3/MnSOD/OGG1 pathway - a demonstrable, interventionally-modulated repair axis.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1190 (Mitochondrion review): synaptic mitochondrial dysfunction (oxidative mtDNA damage, impaired trafficking, mPTP/fission, reduced complex I/IV ATP) is a core, early driver of MCI/AD synaptic loss, and antioxidant phytochemicals restoring synaptic mitochondria confer neuroprotection.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: P-1190 establishes mitochondrial oxidative DNA repair as a mechanistically central and targetable axis in MCI/AD synaptic loss; P-1186 is the direct interventional demonstration that a natural product up-regulating exactly that repair pathway (SIRT3/MnSOD/OGG1) rescues MCI in an animal model. Together they triangulate a mechanism-to-intervention bridge: the review frames the pathological rationale and the drug study shows a concrete, assay-verified repair mechanism, converting a review-level claim into an interventionally-testable hypothesis.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Mitochondrial oxidative-DNA-repair (SIRT3/MnSOD/OGG1-axis) targeted interventions are supported as candidates for human MCI trials, grounded in both the mechanistic-review rationale (P-1190) and a demonstrable preclinical pathway (P-1186).
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Moderate): Classic review-to-intervention bridge. P-1190 frames mitochondrial oxidative DNA repair as a core, early, targetable axis; P-1186 demonstrates that a natural product upregulates exactly that pathway (SIRT3/MnSOD/OGG1) and rescues MCI phenotypes. The triangulation is tight and the clinical implication (human trial candidate) is appropriately scoped.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1201 (Japanese clinic, N=69: 29 MCI / 40 controls; 16S rRNA gut-microbiota profiling): sex-stratified SEM + logistic MCI risk models reach AUC 0.75 (males) / 0.87 (females), the only sex-stratified gut-microbiome MCI risk model in the corpus (internal 10-fold CV + SMOTE only).
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1198 (mini-review, Scopus search, 9 human probiotic clinical studies, ~576 participants): preliminary cognition gains in MCI but 'not yet convincing' - small confounded evidence base, no pooled estimates, no gut or biomarker endpoints.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: The gut-brain axis in MCI is supported at two evidentiary levels that never meet inside any single study: P-1201 shows gut-microbiota composition carries a sex-specific cross-sectional MCI risk signal (AUC 0.75/0.87) while P-1198 shows probiotic interventions yield only fragile, unconvincing cognitive gains across 9 clinical trials. Together they expose the missing link: no corpus study uses gut-microbiota composition to stratify or predict response to a probiotic/SCFA-targeted intervention, so the risk signal (P-1201) and the intervention evidence (P-1198) cannot be bridged - a two-sided gut-brain axis with no connecting study, and a clear template for the next trial.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Stool-based gut-microbiota profiling should be tested as a response-stratifier inside probiotic MCI trials rather than as a stand-alone risk screen; the sex divergence (AUC 0.87 female vs 0.75 male) argues for sex-stratified probiotic trial analysis.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, High): Strong gap-identification pairing. P-1201 shows gut composition carries a sex-specific MCI risk signal; P-1198 shows probiotic trials yield only fragile cognitive gains. The combined insight - that no corpus study uses gut composition to stratify probiotic response - is precisely the missing link the field needs. The sex-divergence observation (AUC 0.87 female vs 0.75 male) adds value.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1200 (FRAMINGO, open-label 24-week Kampo Ninjin'yoeito, N=14 MCI/mild AD; 11 frail/3 prefrail): significant improvement on NPI anorexia (primary), J-CHS frailty score and fatigue VAS - preliminary evidence that frailty and its feeding correlate are modifiable in MCI.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-644 (Tianjin/Shanghai community, N=1394, fully adjusted logistic regression): sarcopenia OR 1.67 (1.04-2.68), handgrip OR 0.97 (0.94-0.99), gait speed OR 0.16 (0.07-0.35) each associated with MCI, whereas the static mass component (skeletal muscle index) is NOT (OR 0.86, ns).
complementary_findings.combined_insight: The corpus's cross-sectional evidence that functional frailty components (gait, grip, sarcopenia) associate with MCI where static muscle mass does not (P-644) gains its only interventional counterpoint in this batch (P-1200): frailty, anorexia and fatigue can be improved in MCI/mild AD with a nutraceutical Kampo formula. The pairing converts frailty from a static risk marker into a modifiable axis, while P-1200's open-label single-arm design (N=14, no control, no cognitive primary) leaves whether frailty improvement alters cognitive trajectory entirely untested - precisely the placebo-controlled trial the association literature (P-644) calls for.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Frailty deserves evaluation as an interventional target in MCI, not only as a prognostic marker; the open-label gains justify a placebo-controlled trial with frailty and cognition co-endpoints. P-1200 is an open-label single-arm study of N=14 with no control arm and no cognitive primary endpoint: it establishes feasibility only, and the modifiability claim rests on P-644's association evidence plus this pilot, not on demonstrated efficacy.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Moderate) - minor caveat: Converts frailty from static risk marker to modifiable axis. The pairing is conceptually sound, but P-1200 is a tiny (N=14) open-label single-arm study. The clinical implication correctly calls for a placebo-controlled trial, which saves it; the final text has been checked so it does not overstate P-1200's evidence quality.
complementary_findings.operator_caveat: Operator G4 required this caveat to appear as an explicit limitation in the manuscript text, not as a quality-flag footnote. The combined_insight / clinical_implication above already carry it.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1195 (random-effects meta-analysis, 79 1H-MRS + 9 31P-MRS studies): NAA down and mI up progress from MCI to AD, and the brain's principal antioxidant glutathione (GSH) is decreased in MCI - an in-vivo chemical change present before frank neuronal-integrity loss.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1199 (redox proteomics review of aMCI post-mortem brain): oxidative protein/lipid damage (protein carbonyls, 4-HNE, 3-nitrotyrosine) is an early event in aMCI hippocampus/IPL, preceding AD neuropathology.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Two independent chemical-biology channels converge on oxidative stress as the earliest molecular event in the MCI cascade: in-vivo MRS meta-analysis finds GSH (the brain's main antioxidant) already reduced in MCI while NAA loss only progresses MCI-to-AD (P-1195), and ex-vivo redox proteomics localises oxidative protein/lipid damage to early aMCI hippocampus/IPL (P-1199). The meta-analysis supplies the temporal ordering (antioxidant depletion before neuronal-integrity loss); the proteomics supplies the molecular target inventory. Together they argue oxidative stress is upstream of neurodegeneration rather than secondary to it - a claim neither source can make alone, and one that repositions redox capacity as a first-window biomarker.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Antioxidant-capacity monitoring (GSH by MRS, plasma oxidative markers) deserves testing as an early-window biomarker preceding conventional NAA/atrophy-based staging of MCI.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, High): Outstanding cross-modal synthesis. In-vivo MRS meta-analysis (GSH reduced before NAA loss) plus ex-vivo hippocampal redox proteomics (oxidative damage precedes frank AD neuropathology) jointly argue that oxidative stress is upstream of neurodegeneration. Neither modality alone can make the temporal-upstream claim; together they can. Clinical implication is proportionate.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1203 (AlzBiom longitudinal cohort, N=49 MCI: 27 converters / 22 stable, 3.7 yr follow-up; shotgun metagenomics): ensemble model (24 genera + 25 GO + 33 KO + clinical/ApoE) predicts MCI-to-AD conversion with AUROC 0.96 (BL) / 0.96 (1y) / 0.97 (4y), best single 24-genus model 0.95 - the corpus's only gut-metagenomics MCI-to-AD conversion model; internal validation only, pilot N=49, no CSF biomarkers.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1211 (narrative review of gut-derived TMAO in MCI): TMAO is reviewed as an MCI risk factor acting via oxidative stress, blood-brain-barrier disruption and impaired synaptic plasticity, and as a treatment target (dietary/faecal-microbiota modulation); evidence is mostly preclinical and causality is unresolved.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: The corpus's gut-brain axis is now two-sided at the CONVERSION level, not just the risk level: P-1203 reports a longitudinal MCI-to-AD conversion signal from gut-microbiome composition (AUROC 0.96-0.97) while P-1211 supplies the metabolite-level mechanism (TMAO) through which gut signals are hypothesised to reach the brain, yet no corpus study links gut composition or TMAO levels to conversion outcomes or tests a TMAO-lowering intervention in an MCI cohort. Distinct from CF-cand-269 (P-1201 16S cross-sectional risk x P-1198 probiotic trials): this pairing spans conversion prognosis + metabolite mechanism, not risk screening + intervention trials. P-1203's discrimination is derived from n=49 with 27 converters against 24 genera, 25 GO terms and 33 KO terms plus clinical variables - a feature-to-event ratio that is a classic overfitting signature - so the reported AUROC must be treated as unreplicated rather than as a performance benchmark.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: P-1203 requires independent replication in a cohort of N>200 before any clinical workflow is proposed on it. Conditional on that replication, gut-metagenomic conversion models should be re-tested with TMAO/SCFA metabolite quantitation and conversion endpoints, and TMAO-lowering interventions (diet, DMB, faecal-microbiota modulation per P-1211) would then merit randomised MCI trials stratified by baseline gut composition. Neither step is warranted on the present evidence.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Moderate) - major caveat: The conversion-prognosis + metabolite-mechanism pairing is conceptually sound, but P-1203's N=49 with AUROC 0.96-0.97 is a classic overfitting signature. A 24-genera + 25 GO + 33 KO + clinical model on 27 converters is not credible for clinical deployment, and the original clinical implication (TMAO-lowering trials stratified by gut composition) was premature. Accepted for the conceptual bridge with the replication requirement (N>200) stated in the record text.
complementary_findings.operator_caveat: Operator G4 required this caveat to appear as an explicit limitation in the manuscript text, not as a quality-flag footnote. The combined_insight / clinical_implication above already carry it.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1206 (hospitalised T2DM, N=329: 231 train / 98 validation; plasma galectin-3): galectin-3 nomogram predicts T2DM MCI with AUC 0.813 (train) / 0.775 (validation); miR-128-3p identified as a regulator of LGALS3 - an inflammatory/glycoprotein axis for T2DM MCI.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1212 (T2DM, N=140: 65 normal cognitive function / 75 MCI; plasma BVR-A + HOMA-IR): BVR-A + HOMA-IR nomogram predicts T2DM MCI with C-index 0.863; BVR-A (bilirubin redox enzyme) is the strongest single marker - a redox/insulin-resistance axis for T2DM MCI.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Two independent T2DM-MCI plasma biomarker axes - galectin-3 (inflammation, miR-regulated) and BVR-A/HOMA-IR (bilirubin redox + insulin resistance) - each nomogram-discriminate T2DM MCI in separate single-centre cohorts, but no corpus study measures both axes in one cohort, so the marginal value of combining inflammatory and redox-metabolic plasma channels for T2DM MCI screening is unknown. Both are cross-sectional, single-centre and internally-split validated only, so the pairing also exposes a shared methodological ceiling neither paper alone discloses: no external validation and no MCI conversion endpoints for either nomogram.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: A combined T2DM-MCI plasma panel (galectin-3 + BVR-A + HOMA-IR) should be tested in an independent multi-centre cohort with conversion follow-up; until then neither single-centre nomogram can be assumed to generalise beyond its training hospital.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Moderate): Two independent T2DM-MCI plasma axes (inflammatory vs redox-metabolic) are presented in parallel single-centre cohorts. The combined insight - that their marginal value in combination is unknown and both share a methodological ceiling (no external validation, no conversion endpoints) - is a valid cross-paper critique. Clinical implication is precise.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1209 (ADNI, N=495: 54 CN / 345 MCI / 96 AD, 1-yr follow-up; plasma GST-alpha): plasma GST-alpha and its 1-year change predict MCI (AUC 0.76) and AD (0.75); a peripheral phase-II antioxidant/redox enzyme.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1210 (ADNI retrospective, N=250: 70 CN / 119 MCI / 61 AD; 82 MCI with conversion follow-up, 48 (58.5%) developed AD; CSF alpha-synuclein aggregation states): Syn1 aggregation state carries MCI-to-AD HR 2.89, while Syn0-AD shows faster decline/atrophy - a central proteinopathy aggregation-state marker.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Two ADNI fluid compartments give orthogonal MCI information: plasma GST-alpha stratifies MCI cross-sectionally (peripheral oxidative-defence enzyme, AUC 0.76) while CSF alpha-synuclein aggregation states stratify MCI prognostically (central proteinopathy seeding, HR 2.89), so a dual plasma+CSF panel could separate 'who has MCI' (peripheral redox) from 'who will convert' (central aggregation). Caveat recorded: BOTH analyses draw on the ADNI single-source cohort, so this is a same-source complementary observation, not independent replication; the cross-compartment claim requires validation in a non-ADNI cohort before any combined-panel inference.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Combined peripheral (GST-alpha) + central (alpha-synuclein aggregation) fluid biomarkers should be evaluated in a non-ADNI cohort to test whether cross-compartment stratification adds conversion-prediction value beyond either biomarker alone.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, High): Elegant orthogonal-fluid pairing. Peripheral redox enzyme (GST-alpha) stratifies MCI cross-sectionally; central proteinopathy aggregation state stratifies conversion prognostically. The dual-panel concept ('who has MCI' vs 'who will convert') is clinically intuitive. Same-source caveat is correctly noted and handled.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1204 (AIBL, N=2136: 1297 CU / 217 MCI / 369 AD / 253 PRO; 546 with cancer history): cancer history lowers adjusted AD odds by ~37% and halves MCI-to-AD progression risk - an inverse cancer-neurodegeneration association in a longitudinal Australian cohort; self-reported cancer, type/therapy unrecorded, Caucasian-only.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1208 (aged-MCI rat model, 22-mo SD + bilateral CCA stenosis, plus independent in-vitro neurons): RUVBL2 knockdown accelerates hnRNPA2/B1 stress-granule disassembly and blunts perioperative neurocognitive disorder (PND) - stress-granule dynamics / RUVBL2 as a proteostasis mechanism in MCI-type cognitive impairment.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: The corpus's only cancer-MCI epidemiology study (P-1204) and its only stress-granule/RUVBL2 mechanism study (P-1208) jointly point at the cancer-neurodegeneration interface: RUVBL2 is a cancer-associated AAA+ ATPase and stress-granule biology is shared between oncogenic stress responses and neuronal proteostasis failure, so the inverse cancer-MCI association P-1204 observes in 2136 AIBL participants and the RUVBL2/stress-granule pathway P-1208 manipulates in aged-rat MCI may be two faces of one stress-response/proteostasis axis. Neither paper alone can state this: P-1204 is epidemiological without molecular data, P-1208 is rat-only with no human disease association - the pairing converts a population-level inverse association into a testable molecular-bridge hypothesis.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Hypothesis only, and the inferential chain is long: a population-level inverse association in 2136 AIBL participants is bridged to rat stress-granule biology solely through RUVBL2's shared role in oncogenic stress responses and neuronal proteostasis. The proposal is to measure stress-granule/RUVBL2 proteostasis markers in cohorts with cancer-history data (e.g. AIBL) to test whether cancer history modulates MCI risk through shared stress-response biology - the first molecular-bridge hypothesis proposed in this corpus for the inverse cancer-MCI association. No therapeutic recommendation follows from this pairing.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Low-Moderate) - major caveat: Highly speculative but intellectually generative. The epidemiological inverse association (P-1204) and the rat stress-granule mechanism (P-1208) are bridged by the shared RUVBL2/cancer biology, but this is a very long inferential chain. Accepted only because it proposes a genuinely testable hypothesis (measure stress-granule markers in AIBL); framed as a first molecular-bridge hypothesis with no therapeutic recommendation.
complementary_findings.operator_caveat: Operator G4 required this caveat to appear as an explicit limitation in the manuscript text, not as a quality-flag footnote. The combined_insight / clinical_implication above already carry it.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1214 (ADNI, N=180 MCI: 104 nonconverters / 76 converters, 6-yr follow-up): composite 'shape feature' integrating amyloid PET BASS (amyloid smoothing) x MRI BAI (atrophy index) predicts MCI-to-AD conversion with AUC 0.891 (baseline) / 0.898 (2-yr), outperforming single-modality biomarkers; no adjustment for cholinesterase-inhibitor (ChEI) or other medication use.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1216 (ADNI 1/2/3/4/GO, N=558 amnestic MCI: 168 ChEI users / 390 non-users, up to 10-yr): ChEI use is associated with ACCELERATED MCI-to-AD progression (time-varying Cox HR 1.77, 95% CI 1.15-2.73) and continued cognitive decline, independent of amyloid status (no interaction HR=0.27, p=0.06); Abeta+ ChEI users highest risk (HR 2.18).
complementary_findings.combined_insight: P-1214's imaging conversion model has no medication-use covariate, while P-1216, a separate observational ADNI study, finds cholinesterase-inhibitor use (168 of 558 amnestic MCI participants in its analytic sample) associated with higher risk of the conversion outcome being predicted (HR 1.77), with its authors unable to establish whether decline prompted treatment or resulted from it. Read together, they raise the possibility that imaging conversion AUCs partly reflect treatment-status differences; models should adjust or stratify for treatment before their performance is read as biomarker performance.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Imaging conversion models should stratify or adjust for ChEI use before their AUCs are interpreted as pure biomarker performance; amyloid-confirmed trials should report imaging conversion metrics separately for treated vs untreated arms.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, High): Methodologically critical confound exposure. P-1214 reports high AUCs without medication covariates; P-1216 shows ChEI is common (30%) and independently accelerates progression. The combined insight - that imaging AUCs may partly encode treatment-status differences rather than pure biology - is a genuine, field-relevant warning. Same-source limitation appropriately flagged.
complementary_findings.combined_insight_pre_2026_09_24: P-1214's imaging conversion model predicts the exact outcome P-1216 shows ChEI treatment independently accelerates, yet P-1214 contains no medication-use covariate while P-1216 shows the treatment is common (30% of amnestic MCI) and an independent progression driver. Together they expose a systematic confound in imaging-only MCI conversion prediction: a shape-feature AUC of 0.89-0.90 measured on a mixed treated/untreated ADNI cohort may partly encode treatment-status differences rather than pure amyloid-atrophy biology - a claim neither paper alone can make, since P-1214 never measures treatment and P-1216 never measures the composite imaging feature.
complementary_findings.correction_note_2026_09_24: Causal wording ('independently accelerates', 'independent progression driver', 'systematic confound') removed against the P-1216 PDF, whose authors restrict themselves to association; consistent with the operator revision of C-253 (2026-09-14).

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1218 (Inha University Hospital, N=60: 20 AD / 20 MCI / 20 HC; plasma): first label-free electrochemical impedance biosensor for plasma p-tau181 (LOD 0.92 fg/mL, KD 0.533 pM), discriminating AD vs HC (AUC 0.94, sens 95%/spec 85%) and MCI vs HC (AUC 0.75), outperforming MMSE/CDR/CDR-SB; single-analyte, deployable, point-of-care-oriented.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1221 (EMIF-AD MBD, 11 European cohorts, N=800: 230 NC / 386 MCI / 184 AD; 194 MCI with paired omics + follow-up): 4-algorithm paired plasma proteomics (SOMAscan 3630 proteins) + metabolomics (540 metabolites) pipeline; 14-feature MCI-conversion model AUC 0.872 including tTau, alpha-synuclein (SNCA), junctophilin-3 (JPH3), properdin (CFP), PI15; multiclass metabolite model validated at 0.726 balanced accuracy with oleamide released by disease-associated microglia.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: P-1218 demonstrates a single plasma analyte (p-tau181) can be measured at femtogram sensitivity on a label-free, deployable biosensor, while P-1221 shows the conversion-relevant plasma signal in MCI is a 14-feature multi-omic panel (tTau + SNCA + JPH3 + CFP + PI15) with AUC 0.872 - yet no corpus study combines a deployable p-tau181 biosensor readout with the omics-derived conversion feature set in one MCI cohort. The pairing maps the path from P-1221's discovery-grade multi-analyte signature to P-1218's single-analyte clinical deployability: tTau is shared, but the marginal conversion value of adding biosensor p-tau181 to the remaining 13 omics features (SNCA/JPH3/CFP/PI15) is completely untested.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Evaluate whether a low-cost p-tau181 biosensor adds conversion-prediction value on top of multi-omics plasma panels in MCI cohorts with follow-up; if yes, the omics signature can be triaged to a two-tier (biosensor screen + omics confirm) plasma workflow.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, High): Technology-to-discovery pairing. P-1218 demonstrates deployable single-analyte measurement; P-1221 shows a 14-feature conversion signature. The combined insight maps a plausible two-tier workflow (biosensor screen -> omics confirm) and correctly identifies that the marginal value of adding p-tau181 to the omics panel is untested.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1217 (UK Biobank, N=125,594; median 11.8-yr follow-up): moderate dietary choline intake (2nd quartile vs lowest) lowers incident dementia (HR 0.80) and AD (HR 0.76) risk with U-shaped dose-response (protective range 332.89-353.93 mg/d); free choline, phosphatidylcholine, sphingomyelin and glycerophosphocholine intakes associated with 17-23% lower dementia odds; moderate choline improves visual attention, fluid intelligence and complex processing speed.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1215 (narrative review, Frontiers in Aging Neuroscience): choline alphoscerate - a prescription cholinergic precursor - improves cognition in MCI/AD/vascular impairment, reduced MCI-to-AD conversion (8.2% vs 26.1% over 3 yr in a Russian prospective study), improved ADAS-cog by 2.34 points at 12 weeks, reduces brain atrophy with donepezil, improves depression/apathy and behavioural symptoms, and is positioned as preventive MCI-to-AD therapy plus a novel cholinergic-sleep-support role.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: P-1217 establishes at population scale (125,594 UKB participants) that adequate dietary choline intake is associated with lower dementia/AD risk with a U-shaped curve, while P-1215 reviews the pharmacological form (choline alphoscerate) as an MCI-to-AD preventive therapy - together they bound the choline axis as a modifiable MCI-to-AD prevention target from nutrient intake (P-1217) to regulated drug (P-1215), yet no corpus study links an individual's dietary choline status or circulating choline to their alphoscerate treatment response, so the dose-response physiology (acetylcholine/phospholipid/betaine pathways) connecting the two evidence levels remains unbridged.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Choline-adequacy screening (dietary recall or circulating choline) should be tested as a responder-stratifier in choline alphoscerate MCI trials; the U-shaped population curve argues against high-dose supplementation without individual adequacy assessment.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, High): Nutrient-to-pharmaceutical axis pairing. Population U-shaped dietary protection (P-1217, N=125k UK Biobank) bounds the pharmacological prevention claim (P-1215). The clinical implication's U-shaped caution against blind high-dose supplementation is evidence-appropriate.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1220 (UERJ Brazil, N=94: 16 MCI / 30 AD / 48 HC; ethnically mixed, comorbidity-free): 1H-NMR multi-biofluid (plasma/urine/saliva) metabolomics finds stage-specific signatures - valine increases progressively control<MCI<AD while alanine is biphasic (down in MCI, up in AD); six GWAS genes (CYCS, NFAT5, GRIN2B, SLC43A2, MAPT, SLC38A1) common to all three biofluids; cross-sectional metabolic state.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1222 (DodoNA EHR, N=1,249: AD cohort 215/483, MCI cohort 116/435; decade pre-onset lipid measurements): longitudinal lipid trajectories (group-based trajectory modelling) and variability-independent-of-the-mean (VIM) quintiles improve AD and MCI risk prediction beyond APOE genotype and polygenic risk scores - lower HDL-C trajectories (OR 2.8-3.9) and lowest TC/non-HDL-C VIM quintiles (OR 2.2-2.5) raise risk; longitudinal dynamics of routine lipids carry risk information independent of genetics.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: P-1220 reads blood metabolic STATE cross-sectionally (stage-specific NMR signatures across three biofluids) while P-1222 reads the same class of blood metabolic signals LONGITUDINALLY (lipid trajectory groups and variability over a decade) and shows the dynamics - not just the level - carry independent AD/MCI risk beyond APOE/PRS. Together they argue that the field's cross-sectional metabolic MCI/AD biomarker literature (P-1220 and most metabolomics studies) is missing the longitudinal dimension P-1222 shows is informative, and that the stage-specific metabolites P-1220 identifies (valine, alanine, scyllo-inositol) have never been tested in P-1222-style trajectory/VIM frameworks - a methodological blind spot neither paper alone reveals.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Stage-specific NMR metabolites should be re-measured longitudinally and modelled with trajectory/VIM approaches (as P-1222 does for lipids) to test whether metabolic DYNAMICS add conversion-prediction value beyond cross-sectional stage signatures.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, High): Methodological blind-spot identification. P-1220 reads metabolic state cross-sectionally; P-1222 shows that lipid dynamics (trajectory + variability) carry independent risk beyond genetics. The combined insight - that cross-sectional metabolomics is missing the longitudinal dimension - is a sharp, field-relevant critique.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1225 (Careggi Hospital, Florence, N=79 SCD/MCI/AD-d; 72 with CSF): plasma p-tau181 by Simoa detects AT(N)-defined AD pathology with AUC 0.910 (cut-off 2.69 pg/mL; sens 0.86, spec 0.82) - a protein-level, AT(N)-anchored readout of AD pathology in SCD/MCI, cross-sectional, internal-only validation.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1232 (Guangzhou community cohort, N=310: 155 MCI / 155 controls; external AddNeuroMed/GSE63060 N=184): plasma exosomal lncRNA panel (LINC001380, ENST00000484033, ENST00000531087) diagnoses MCI at AUC 0.700 (95% CI 0.641-0.760; sens 72.0%, spec 60.7%); external validation via target genes ATP2A2/PSEN1 AUC 0.695 - an RNA-level transcriptomic readout, Chinese-population-only.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: P-1225 and P-1232 are the batch's two plasma-based molecular diagnostics aimed at the same SCD/MCI window but on orthogonal molecular axes: a single high-specificity protein (p-tau181, AT(N)-anchored, AUC 0.910) versus a three-analyte exosomal RNA panel with broader, lower-specificity transcriptomic coverage (AUC 0.700). Neither paper alone can state that the two axes are complementary rather than redundant, because P-1225 measures only protein and P-1232 measures only RNA - the combined read is that an AT(N)-anchored protein screen (high specificity, pathology-grounded) could triage to a broader RNA panel for molecular staging, and the moderate RNA-only AUC (0.70) vs protein-only AUC (0.91) quantifies what a single-axis blood test gives up. A two-axis blood panel has never been tested in this corpus.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: A staged blood workflow - p-tau181 screen first, exosomal lncRNA panel for RNA-level stratification of screen-positives - should be evaluated in one cohort; the performance gap (0.91 vs 0.70) argues the protein axis is the gate and the RNA axis adds subtype/molecular context, not vice versa. The exosomal lncRNA panel is not currently clinically viable at AUC 0.700 with 60.7% specificity: 'the protein axis is the gate' describes the relative ordering of the two axes, not an endorsement of the RNA panel for use.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Moderate) - minor caveat: The orthogonal molecular-axes insight is valid, but P-1232's performance is modest (AUC 0.70, specificity 60.7%). The staged-workflow clinical implication is reasonable as a hypothesis, but the 'protein axis is the gate' claim must not imply that the RNA panel is currently clinically viable - it is not. Performance caveat for P-1232 added to the record text.
complementary_findings.operator_caveat: Operator G4 required this caveat to appear as an explicit limitation in the manuscript text, not as a quality-flag footnote. The combined_insight / clinical_implication above already carry it.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1226 (Shanghai-derived Cog_Vol composite validated in ADNI1/GO/2, N=843 MCI, 220 PET-amyloid-elevated): PET-amyloid x MRI-volume cognitive composite stratifies MCI-to-AD conversion risk from 94.1% (Cog_Vol<101) to ~0% (>=340) within 2-4 years in elevated-amyloid MCI; group-level stratification, no tau biomarkers, intermediate band unclassifiable.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1227 (ADNI, N=648: 90 3-yr converters; conference abstract): multi-step ML on STANDARD CLINICAL data alone (no imaging) with CSF t-tau/Abeta ratio strata and SHAP interpretability reaches 3-year conversion accuracy 88% (AD-like CSF stratum), 86% (CSF-negative), 84% (overall) - near-parity with imaging-based models at far lower cost, but abstract-only with no model specification.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: P-1226 and P-1227 attack the same ADNI MCI-to-AD conversion problem from opposite resource ends: P-1226 needs PET + MRI volumetry to resolve the extreme risk bands (94.1% vs ~0%) while P-1227 shows standard clinical data plus a CSF ratio reaches 84-88% accuracy with no imaging at all. Together they define a resource-tiered conversion-prediction strategy that neither paper alone articulates: clinical-data ML (P-1227) is sufficient for population-level triage, and the expensive imaging composite (P-1226) adds value precisely in the intermediate-risk band P-1227's coarse accuracy cannot separate - the band P-1226 explicitly leaves unclassifiable (~60%). The two ceilings are complementary: cheap methods saturate at ~85%, expensive methods stratify the tails but miss the middle.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Conversion-prediction deployment could in principle be two-tiered - clinical-data ML for first-pass triage (P-1227), imaging composite reserved for the intermediate-risk group where its extreme-band resolution can actually change management - since neither tier alone covers the full risk spectrum. P-1227 is a conference abstract with no model specification, so its 84-88% accuracy is unverifiable and its near-parity with the imaging composite cannot be independently assessed. It is not established evidence and must be peer-reviewed and replicated before any tiered deployment strategy rests on it.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Moderate) - major caveat: The two-tiered resource-stratification insight (cheap clinical ML for triage, expensive imaging for the intermediate-risk band) is clinically valuable and well articulated. However, P-1227 is a conference abstract with no model specification, making its 84-88% accuracy claim unverifiable and its near-parity with imaging impossible to assess independently. The clinical implication must not treat P-1227 as established evidence; the abstract-only caveat is stated in the record text.
complementary_findings.operator_caveat: Operator G4 required this caveat to appear as an explicit limitation in the manuscript text, not as a quality-flag footnote. The combined_insight / clinical_implication above already carry it.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1223 (two Italian memory clinics, N=196 MCI, median 2.9-yr follow-up): LOW serum ApoJ/clusterin tertile predicts doubled MCI-to-dementia conversion risk (adjusted HR 2.01, 95% CI 1.18-3.43) that emerges only AFTER 2 years of follow-up - a cheap, single-timepoint blood protein marker, no predictive effect within the first 2 years.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1226 (Shanghai->ADNI, N=843 MCI): Cog_Vol composite of PET amyloid x MRI volume + cognition stratifies MCI-to-AD conversion from 94.1% to ~0% - but the conversion signal concentrates in the FIRST 2-4 years of follow-up (most conversion happens in the first 3 years).
complementary_findings.combined_insight: P-1223 and P-1226 occupy opposite temporal halves of the same MCI conversion window: P-1226's imaging composite resolves early conversion (first 2-4 years, most conversions) while P-1223's serum ApoJ carries conversion information only after year 2 - so a cheap blood draw (ApoJ) and an expensive imaging composite (Cog_Vol) are temporally complementary risk signals for the same outcome, and neither alone spans the full follow-up horizon. This temporal dissociation is only visible by pairing the two: P-1223 never measures imaging and P-1226 never measures serum proteins, so the combined claim - early window belongs to imaging, late window to the serum marker - is a cross-paper discovery neither source supports alone.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Follow-up protocols could use Cog_Vol early and ApoJ after year 2 to cover the full conversion window at lower cumulative cost, and the late-window ApoJ signal may flag the 'post-2-year' converters that early imaging misses. The temporal dissociation is a cross-paper hypothesis drawn from two entirely independent cohorts (Italian memory clinics vs ADNI), not an established phenomenon: co-measurement of Cog_Vol and serum ApoJ in a single cohort is required before any follow-up protocol is redesigned.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Moderate) - minor caveat: Elegant temporal complementarity: imaging captures early conversion, serum ApoJ captures late conversion. However, the two cohorts are entirely independent (Italian memory clinics vs ADNI), so the temporal dissociation is a cross-paper hypothesis, not an established phenomenon. The co-measurement validation requirement is now stated in the record text.
complementary_findings.operator_caveat: Operator G4 required this caveat to appear as an explicit limitation in the manuscript text, not as a quality-flag footnote. The combined_insight / clinical_implication above already carry it.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1233 (Thessaloniki, serum N=57 / CSF N=124; AD/MCI/controls): serum and CSF bacterial LPS and COX-1/2 elevated in AD and MCI (CSF), serum LPS discriminating HC-vs-AD and MCI-vs-AD with good ROC performance; LPS correlates positively with Abeta42, tau and negatively with MMSE - a cross-sectional DIAGNOSTIC readout of the microbial/inflammatory axis.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1239 (8 Dutch memory clinics, N=268 SCD/MCI/AD, 2-yr follow-up): lower baseline CSF NGAL (lipocalin-2) predicts MCI-to-AD conversion with OR 2.27 (95% CI 1.15-4.46), and CSF NGAL correlates positively with Abeta1-42 in MCI - a PROGNOSTIC readout of neuroinflammation; serum NGAL null.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: The batch's two neuroinflammatory fluid-marker studies cover the same biological axis (inflammation) on opposite sides of the diagnostic-prognostic divide: P-1233 shows LPS/COX inflammation discriminates MCI/AD cross-sectionally (with no follow-up) while P-1239 shows a different inflammation marker (CSF NGAL) predicts conversion at 2 years (without ROC-based diagnostic value analysis). Neither paper alone spans both: P-1233 never follows patients to conversion and P-1239 never evaluates NGAL as a diagnostic discriminator, so the combined claim - that the inflammatory axis may serve as BOTH a cross-sectional MCI marker and a conversion predictor - is only visible by pairing them. Both share the same ceiling: single-region cohorts, no external validation, no combined inflammatory panel.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: A single MCI cohort measuring LPS/COX (or a broader inflammation panel) and CSF/serum NGAL together with conversion follow-up would test whether the inflammatory axis carries independent diagnostic and prognostic value. LPS/COX and NGAL may index different inflammatory biology, so treating them as one 'inflammatory axis' is provisional; that cohort must establish whether the markers are additive or redundant before a combined panel is claimed.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Moderate) - minor caveat: The diagnostic-prognostic divide framing is useful, but the two markers (LPS/COX vs NGAL) may capture different inflammatory biology. The claim that they represent a single 'inflammatory axis' is somewhat loose. Accepted with the caveat that a combined panel would need to establish whether the markers are additive or redundant.
complementary_findings.operator_caveat: Operator G4 required this caveat to appear as an explicit limitation in the manuscript text, not as a quality-flag footnote. The combined_insight / clinical_implication above already carry it.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1240 (Trondheim, N=135: 52 control / 55 aMCI / 28 AD; 24-mo + 6-10 yr re-eval): CSF NfL elevated in aMCI and AD, lower in stable than converter aMCI (p=0.004), but substituting NfL for T-tau in the core Abeta42/P-tau/T-tau model does NOT improve control-vs-AD or stable-vs-converter separation - an axonal neurodegeneration marker with no added value over core biomarkers.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1241 (ADNI, EMCI 187 + LMCI 119, 36-mo): low CSF VGF serves as a non-tau N marker in the ATN framework, raising EMCI conversion accuracy 66.5->76.5% (p=0.0012) and LMCI 71.6->81.1% (p=0.0014) when added to AT markers, and predicts conversion even in AT-negative MCI (replicated within ADNI) - a synaptic/activity-dependent peptide with clear added value.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: The batch's two CSF N-candidates bracket the ATN framework's neurodegeneration slot from opposite directions: the axonal marker (NfL) carries conversion signal alone (p=0.004) yet adds nothing to the core model when substituted for T-tau, while the synaptic/activity marker (VGF) is the marker that actually improves AT-based conversion prediction and works in AT-negative patients. Together they argue the N component of ATN should be a synaptic/activity marker (VGF) rather than a redundant axonal one (NfL) - a conclusion neither paper reaches alone, because P-1240 never tests VGF and P-1241 never compares against NfL. Caveat recorded: P-1241 is ADNI-only (same-source replication), P-1240 is single-centre, so the head-to-head claim is a cross-paper hypothesis requiring one cohort with both markers.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Measure CSF VGF and NfL together with AT biomarkers in a single MCI cohort with conversion follow-up to test whether a synaptic N marker (VGF) outperforms an axonal one (NfL) for ATN-based conversion prediction.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, High): Sharp head-to-head hypothesis for ATN framework refinement. NfL adds nothing when substituted for T-tau; VGF improves prediction and works in AT-negative patients. The conclusion that the N component should be synaptic (VGF) rather than axonal (NfL) is clinically important and testable. Caveat about single-centre vs ADNI-only is noted.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1234 (Thessaloniki, N=60: 20 MCI / 20 AD / 20 HC): salivary GFAP is SIGNIFICANTLY DECREASED in MCI and AD vs controls (ELISA 13.35 -> 6.82 -> 3.56 ng/mg protein) and excellently discriminates controls from MCI (J=0.95, sens 95%/spec 100%) - a non-invasive astrogliosis readout moving DOWNWARD with pathology.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-54 (ADNI, N=111): plasma GFAP is ELEVATED and, combined with plasma NfL and tau-PET, classifies MCI with AUC 0.93, with tau-PET partially mediating the blood-marker-to-cognition pathway - a blood astrogliosis readout moving UPWARD with pathology (consistent with the broader plasma-GFAP literature).
complementary_findings.combined_insight: The same astrocytic protein (GFAP) moves in OPPOSITE directions across two biofluids in the corpus: plasma GFAP rises with AD pathology (P-54 and the wider plasma-GFAP literature) while salivary GFAP falls in MCI/AD (P-1234). This compartment-specific direction conflict is invisible from either paper alone - P-1234 has no blood comparison and P-54 has no saliva - and has direct measurement implications: a one-size-fits-all GFAP threshold is impossible until the salivary vs plasma relationship is resolved in the same individuals. If confirmed, the opposing directions suggest the two fluids capture different GFAP biology (diffusion from blood vs salivary-gland production) rather than the same signal at different sensitivity.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Measure plasma and salivary GFAP in the same participants across the control-MCI-AD spectrum to resolve the direction conflict, establish cross-fluid concordance, and define which fluid (or ratio) carries diagnostic value.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, High): Striking compartment-specific direction conflict for the same protein. Exactly the kind of non-obvious, measurement-critical observation cross-fertilisation should surface. The clinical implication (co-measurement in the same individuals to resolve the conflict) is precise and urgent.
