complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1236 (ADNI, 630 MCI; 260 with plasma proteins; GBMT): two cerebral atrophy-rate classes (slow, fast); plasma microglial proteins AXL, CD40, TNF-R2 associated with the classes, with higher CD40 predicting faster decline in the slow-atrophy class and higher AXL/TNF-R2 predicting slower decline in the fast-atrophy class - a MOLECULAR heterogeneity axis.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1242 (ADNI, 147: 46 MCI / 101 CU): cognitive reserve (estimated VIQ) moderates the CBF-language association - in MCI, stronger positive CBF-category-fluency associations at higher VIQ - a PSYCHOSOCIAL reserve axis modulating how perfusion relates to cognition.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Two ADNI MCI studies characterise orthogonal axes of within-MCI heterogeneity: P-1236 subdivides patients by molecular (microglial-protein x atrophy-rate) biology that flips the direction of protein-cognition associations, while P-1242 shows a psychosocial modifier (cognitive reserve) changes the strength of the CBF-cognition link. Neither paper models the other's axis - P-1236 has no reserve measure and P-1242 has no microglial/atrophy-rate stratification - so the combined claim that MCI progression is jointly shaped by molecular subtyping AND cognitive reserve is only visible by pairing. Both share the ADNI single-source ceiling, and both report moderation/interaction rather than conversion outcomes, so the synthesis is a hypothesis about two non-overlapping sources of MCI outcome variance rather than a validated model.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Hypothesis-generating: both papers report moderation or interaction without conversion outcomes, so this is a proposal to test in a conversion cohort rather than a basis for practice change. An ADNI (or non-ADNI) study stratifying MCI by atrophy-rate/microglial class AND cognitive reserve simultaneously, with dementia-conversion follow-up, would test whether reserve buffers the adverse molecular-subtype trajectories.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Moderate) - minor caveat: Conceptually interesting orthogonal heterogeneity axes (molecular vs psychosocial), but both papers report moderation without conversion outcomes. The synthesis is abstract and hypothesis-generating rather than clinically grounded; the clinical implication is framed as 'test in a conversion cohort' rather than immediate practice change.
complementary_findings.operator_caveat: Operator G4 required this caveat to appear as an explicit limitation in the manuscript text, not as a quality-flag footnote. The combined_insight / clinical_implication above already carry it.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1245 (ADNI, Cohort 1 n=625 / Cohort 2 n=393): two-stage RLR + random forest models integrating plasma (NfL, p-tau181, Abeta42/40), MRI, demographics/APOE4 and cognitive composites predicted multi-domain cognitive decline (cross-validated correlations 0.50 memory / 0.49 language / 0.42 EF / 0.44 VS) and progression to MCI/dementia (combined C-index 0.76 CU, 0.79 MCI), with MRI > plasma in importance.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1247 (ADNI, n=29: 14 HC / 15 MCI): longitudinal temporal-lobe TBM showed MCI > HC atrophy, but plasma Abeta42/Abeta40/Abeta42-40 showed no consistent group differences and NO significant plasma Abeta-TBM associations at baseline or 24 months (only scattered 48-month positive associations, beta 0.60-0.70).
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Together the two ADNI studies delimit the role of plasma Abeta in ADNI prediction: P-1245 finds plasma biomarkers add value for memory-domain decline and progression only when combined with MRI, demographics and cognitive scores (and NfL/p-tau181 outperform Abeta42/40), while P-1247 shows plasma Abeta alone does not track regional temporal-lobe atrophy longitudinally. The paired reading explains why: plasma Abeta carries diagnostic/prognostic signal in a multimodal prediction context but is too weak a stand-alone correlate of regional neurodegeneration, so prediction models should not rely on plasma Abeta as a proxy for atrophy, and its value is conditional on multimodal integration - a boundary condition invisible from either paper alone.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Plasma Abeta should not be used as a stand-in for MRI-based atrophy monitoring; multimodal models (plasma + MRI + cognitive) are the appropriate use of plasma biomarkers, with NfL/p-tau181 preferred over Abeta42/40 when selecting plasma panels.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, High): A precise boundary-condition pairing. P-1245 shows plasma biomarkers (including Abeta42/40) contribute to multimodal prediction when bundled with MRI, demographics and cognition - but MRI dominates importance. P-1247 demonstrates that plasma Abeta alone does not track regional temporal-lobe atrophy longitudinally. The combined insight - that plasma Abeta carries signal only in integrated models but is not a stand-in for atrophy monitoring - is a clinically critical distinction that prevents biomarker misuse. The clinical implication to prefer NfL/p-tau181 over Abeta42/40 in plasma panels is evidence-consistent.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1246 (NCT03080818, N=169, double-blind placebo-controlled 3-month LGG RCT): Prevotella ruminicola, Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron and B. caccae significantly more prevalent in MCI; LGG supplementation decreased Prevotella/Dehalobacterium abundance in the MCI group, correlated with improved cognitive scores.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1251 (N=68 older adults): 16S rRNA oral microbiome found Pasteurellaceae and Lautropia mirabilis differentially abundant in MCI; blood inflammatory markers did not differentiate groups, but five CSF inflammatory mediators were identified with significant associations with MCI.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: The two microbiome studies cover different body-site communities on opposite sides of the intervention question: P-1246 shows a gut-microbiome genus (Prevotella) enriched in MCI can be shifted downward by a probiotic in a direction correlated with cognitive improvement, while P-1251 shows an oral-microbiome profile (Pasteurellaceae, L. mirabilis) associates with MCI alongside CNS (CSF) - not peripheral blood - inflammatory mediators. Read together they indicate microbiome-MCI associations are body-site specific (gut vs oral), that peripheral blood inflammation may not capture CNS-relevant microbiome-inflammation links, and that the modifiability demonstrated for the gut community (P-1246) has no oral-microbiome equivalent tested - leaving open whether oral taxa are also manipulable with cognitive benefit.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Microbiome-targeted MCI interventions should measure both gut and oral communities, and should include CSF (or CNS-proxy) inflammatory endpoints because peripheral blood markers may miss the relevant inflammatory pathway.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, High): Strong body-site cross-fertilisation. P-1246 is a double-blind RCT showing gut microbiome modifiability (Prevotella decrease correlated with cognitive improvement); P-1251 shows oral microbiome associations with MCI alongside CSF - not peripheral blood - inflammatory mediators. The combined insight that microbiome-MCI links are body-site specific and that peripheral blood may miss CNS-relevant inflammatory pathways is non-obvious and methodologically important. The clinical implication to measure both gut and oral communities with CSF endpoints in future trials is directly actionable.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1249 (N=88: 55 T1DM [31 MCI, 24 non-MCI] + 33 controls): astrocyte-exosome complement C5b-9/C3b/Factor B elevated in T1DM-MCI; C5b-9 independently associated with MCI (OR 1.20, 95% CI 1.00-1.44); combined complement AUC 0.76 for distinguishing T1DM-MCI.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1250 (N=579 T2DM: 273 MCI / 306 controls): plasma CDR1as protective against MCI (OR 0.45, 95% CI 0.31-0.65) and positively associated with memory (beta 0.29); alpha-Syn partially mediated 34.03% (MCI) and 31.71% (memory) of the CDR1as effect.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: The two diabetes-specific fluid-marker studies establish that MCI in diabetes carries disease-subtype-distinct blood/exosome markers: complement-mediated astrocytic neuroinflammation in T1DM (P-1249) versus a CDR1as-alpha-Syn molecular pathway in T2DM (P-1250). Both achieve discriminative/protective associations in cross-sectional cohorts, but neither spans the other's pathway nor provides longitudinal conversion data. The complementary claim - that diabetes-subtype-specific MCI marker panels (exosomal complement for T1DM, CDR1as/alpha-Syn for T2DM) may be needed rather than a single diabetes-MCI marker - is only visible by pairing the two studies, and both share the untested prognostic dimension.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: MCI screening in diabetic populations may require subtype-specific biomarker panels (T1DM: astrocyte-exosome complement; T2DM: CDR1as/alpha-Syn), and neither marker class should be assumed to transfer across diabetes subtypes without validation.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, High): Excellent disease-subtype stratification. Two large, independent diabetes cohorts (T1DM n=88, T2DM n=579) identify distinct fluid-marker pathways for MCI: complement-mediated astrocytic neuroinflammation in T1DM versus a CDR1as-alpha-Syn molecular axis in T2DM. The combined insight that diabetes-MCI screening may need subtype-specific panels rather than a single 'diabetes-MCI' marker is clinically novel and immediately testable. Both studies are cross-sectional, so the clinical implication correctly limits itself to screening stratification, not prognostic validation.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1243 (UCSF pilot, N=13 aMCI): eight 60-min 40-Hz gamma tACS sessions targeting hippocampus/IPL/pars triangularis improved multiple episodic-memory metrics with an electric-field dose-response, but plasma AD biomarkers showed no change; RSFC and E/I balance shifts indicated network engagement.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1252 (MICOIL substudy, N=88: 22 normal / 44 MCI [22 EVOO, 22 without] / 22 AD): one-year daily 50 ml EVOO restored serum PARP-1, 8-OHdG, NOS2, Abeta1-42 and p-tau in MCI to near-healthy levels vs untreated MCI, with in silico docking support for PARP-1/NOS-2 binding.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: The two intervention studies occupy opposite poles of the cognitive-vs-biomarker response spectrum: P-1243's gamma tACS improved cognition with no plasma biomarker change (suggesting functional/network-level rescue that fluid biomarkers do not capture), while P-1252's EVOO restored oxidative-stress and AD-hallmark biomarkers (PARP-1, 8-OHdG, NOS2, Abeta, p-tau) with biomarker-only endpoints and no cognitive-outcome reporting in this substudy. Read together they expose a systematic measurement gap: neither intervention study demonstrates simultaneous cognitive improvement AND biomarker normalization, so it remains unknown whether functional gains (tACS) and molecular restoration (EVOO) occur independently, in sequence, or are different response modalities of the same disease process - and neither can claim a full cognitive-plus-biomarker therapeutic effect.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Intervention trials in MCI should report cognitive and fluid-biomarker endpoints together, because this batch shows interventions can move one axis while leaving the other unchanged; claiming therapeutic benefit from either alone is incomplete.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, High): Outstanding meta-scientific gap identification. This pairing exposes a systematic reporting failure in MCI intervention trials: functional/network interventions (tACS) improve cognition without biomarker movement, while molecular interventions (EVOO) restore biomarkers without reported cognitive outcomes. The combined insight - that no intervention in this batch demonstrates simultaneous cognitive and biomarker normalisation, and that these may represent independent response modalities - is a field-level observation of genuine methodological importance. The clinical implication to mandate dual-endpoint reporting in future trials is proportionate and would improve evidence quality. A model cross-fertilisation entry.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1254 (northwest-China community, miRNA/ROC cohort n=72: 24 MCI / 24 age-matched HC / 24 younger HC): plasma exosomal miR-483-5p (AUC 0.901, sens 79.2%, spec 100%) and miR-502-5p (AUC 0.872, sens 79.2%, spec 83.3%) discriminated MCI from age-matched controls.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1253 (Vienna Memory Clinic, N=976: 90 SCD / 496 MCI / 390 AD, retrospective): elevated serum homocysteine independently predicted 5-year mortality (lg10 OR 11.20, categorical OR 1.84) and correlated negatively with MMSE and NTBV attention/memory factors, with no cognitively normal control group.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Two non-invasive blood markers span complementary phases of the SCD/MCI/AD continuum: P-1254 detects the MCI state (exosomal miRNA, AUC 0.901) while P-1253 stratifies survival risk within the already-impaired population (homocysteine, 5-year mortality lg10 OR 11.20). Read together they outline a two-stage blood-based pathway - screening for MCI with exosomal miRNA, then prognosticating with homocysteine - but each study omits the other's measurement, P-1254 has no follow-up for progression and P-1253 lacks a normal-control arm, so the proposed detection-to-prognosis pipeline is assembled from non-overlapping evidence rather than demonstrated in a single cohort.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: A combined non-invasive blood panel (exosomal miRNA plus homocysteine) could in principle take a community-dwelling elderly person from MCI detection to mortality-risk stratification, but the pipeline needs a prospective cohort measuring both markers with conversion and survival endpoints before clinical use.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 2): Different blood markers cover detection vs survival prognosis; coherent sequential complement, but never jointly tested. Evaluation: Unit-fidelity fix applied: the insight's mortality OR now carries the lg10 qualifier present in the source finding; cohort flag (NW-China vs Vienna) noted.
complementary_findings.operator_caveat: Operator G4 required this caveat to appear as an explicit limitation in the manuscript text, not as a quality-flag footnote; the combined_insight / clinical_implication / human_evaluation_note above already carry it.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1258 (Shanghai community, N=87 MCI, 2-year follow-up): baseline decrease of Ruminococcaceae and increase of Megamonas (16S rDNA) were independently associated with rapid MCI progression (Ruminococcaceae with P-tau181 B -1.895 p=0.003; Megamonas with diabetes B 2.271 p=0.026).
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1246 (RCT NCT03080818, N=169 community-dwelling adults, 3 months): Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG lowered MCI-associated Prevotella abundance with correlations to improved cognition; a gut-microbiome intervention study.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: The two gut-microbiome studies approach the same brain-gut axis from opposite designs: P-1258 shows baseline compositional risk markers (Ruminococcaceae decrease, Megamonas increase) predict 2-year MCI progression observationally, while P-1246 shows an interventional microbiome shift (LGG lowering Prevotella) accompanies cognitive improvement in a randomized trial. Together they suggest gut flora may be both a prognostic axis and a modifiable therapeutic target in MCI, motivating probiotic or butyrate-producing interventions with progression endpoints - yet neither study measured the other's taxa, so whether shifting the P-1258 risk markers would alter progression remains untested.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Gut-microbiome-guided MCI care (risk screening on Ruminococcaceae/Megamonas, intervention with LGG-class probiotics) is plausible but requires a trial that measures both risk taxa and progression outcomes together.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 2): Observational progression markers plus randomized microbiome intervention are genuinely complementary, but taxa differ and causality is untested. Evaluation: Softened 'coherent case' to 'suggest... may', because LGG shifted Prevotella, not the P-1258 risk taxa.
complementary_findings.operator_caveat: Operator G4 required this caveat to appear as an explicit limitation in the manuscript text, not as a quality-flag footnote; the combined_insight / clinical_implication / human_evaluation_note above already carry it.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1265 (ADNI-1, N=783: 224 CN / 181 sMCI / 193 pMCI / 185 AD): lower baseline serum glutamate (cutoff 94.2 uM) predicted MCI-to-AD progression by Cox regression adjusted for age/gender/education, but serum Glu had no diagnostic value (ROC not significant).
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1267 (BALTAZAR, N=106 MCI, 3-year follow-up): highest quartile of free plasma Abeta1-42/Abeta1-40 (>=25.8%) predicted lower conversion risk (HR 0.36, 95% CI 0.15-0.87), equivalent to total ratio (HR 0.37), with ~60% lower conversion risk above threshold.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Two independent blood-based conversion predictors sit on orthogonal molecular axes: P-1265's serum glutamate (excitatory amino-acid / metabolic axis) and P-1267's free plasma Abeta1-42/1-40 (amyloid axis) both stratify MCI-to-dementia risk, but no corpus study measures them jointly; a combined metabolic-plus-amyloid blood panel is untested, and each study's threshold (94.2 uM vs 25.8%) was derived in a single cohort.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: A dual-axis blood panel (amyloid ratio + metabolic marker such as glutamate) could improve MCI conversion-risk stratification, but requires joint-cohort validation before clinical use.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 1): Two independent blood predictors of MCI-to-AD on distinct molecular axes; clear additive-information question. Evaluation: Distinct cohorts (ADNI vs BALTAZAR) and single-cohort thresholds correctly flagged in the record.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1263 (Korea, N=47: 20 AD / 16 MCI / 11 HC): PAN-based plasmonic biosensor quantified plasma p-tau species (pT231, pT181, pS396) at attomolar LOD and an SVM classifier separated HC/MCI/AD at 94.47% accuracy (pT231 AUC 0.9659 MCI-HC; pT181 AUC 0.9682 AD-HC).
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1267 (BALTAZAR, N=106 MCI): free plasma Abeta1-42/Abeta1-40 ratio predicted 3-year MCI-to-dementia conversion (HR 0.36 highest quartile), equivalent to the total ratio (HR 0.37).
complementary_findings.combined_insight: The two blood biomarkers map onto complementary stages of the AD continuum: P-1263's plasma p-tau biosensor delivers cross-sectional differential diagnosis (HC vs MCI vs AD) with an ML classifier, while P-1267's plasma Abeta ratio delivers longitudinal conversion risk - together they resemble a blood-based AT(N)-style staging (p-tau for tau status, Abeta ratio for amyloid status) deployable from a single non-invasive draw, but no corpus study combines the two axes in one cohort or device.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Combining a plasma p-tau biosensor with an Abeta42/40 ratio could give blood-based AT(N)-like staging for both differential diagnosis and conversion prediction, pending joint validation.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 1): Cross-sectional p-tau diagnosis plus longitudinal amyloid-risk prediction gives a strong stage-complementary blood model. Evaluation: Cohort flag (Korea N=47 vs BALTAZAR France N=106) noted; otherwise logic sound with appropriate 'AT(N)-style' hedging.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1266 (Vallecas/CIEN, N=128: 51 AD / 27 MCI / 50 HC): 1H NMR serum metabolomics PLS-DA discriminated AD from HC (AUC 0.9816) and AD from MCI (AUC 0.9281), with alanine/aspartate/glutamate, pantothenate/CoA and beta-alanine pathways altered in MCI-to-dementia vs HC.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1265 (ADNI-1, N=783): lower baseline serum glutamate predicted MCI-to-AD progression (Cox, cutoff 94.2 uM) but had no diagnostic value.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Both serum-metabolomics studies converge on the glutamatergic axis in MCI progression: P-1266 implicates the alanine/aspartate/glutamate pathway in MCI-to-dementia (pathway level), while P-1265 shows lower serum glutamate predicts MCI-to-AD (analyte level) - independent cohorts (Madrid vs ADNI) and platforms (NMR vs UPLC-MS/MS) reaching the same axis, but neither study tests the other's metabolite panel, and P-1266's HC-MCI model failed while P-1265's diagnostic ROC was null, so the MCI-versus-HC boundary remains unvalidated for serum glutamate.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Serum glutamatergic markers warrant joint evaluation as both a diagnostic and conversion-prediction panel, with the HC/MCI boundary requiring further work.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 1): Independent cohorts and platforms converge on glutamatergic biology at pathway and analyte levels. Evaluation: Rare convergent-evidence synthesis with failure modes disclosed ('HC-MCI model failed' while 'diagnostic ROC was null'); 'HC-MCI model failed' is not in the finding field - verify against full text before citing.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1274 (HSROC meta-analysis, 17 studies n=2083): blood-based biomarkers distinguish AD and aMCI from controls - plasma Abeta42 (DOR 32.2 AD / 60.4 aMCI), Abeta oligomer (DOR 29.1) and tau (DOR 52.1) with 79-90% sensitivity and 81-94% specificity.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1282 (Rome Memory Clinic, N=70 aMCI: 41 A+/29 A-): fully-automated Lumipulse G plasma assays distinguish aMCI due to AD from aMCI unlikely due to AD, with the Abeta42/p-tau181 ratio most accurate (AUC 0.895, sens 95.1%, spec 82.8%) and strong CSF-plasma correlations.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Taken together the two papers outline a translation pathway for blood biomarkers of the AD continuum: P-1274 supplies meta-analytic evidence that blood Abeta42 and tau reach clinically useful diagnostic accuracy for AD and aMCI, while P-1282 demonstrates that a fully-automated, high-throughput immunoassay (Lumipulse G) can operationalise that accuracy within a homogeneous prodromal (aMCI) population by separating AD-continuum from non-AD cases. P-1274's synthesis supplies pooled diagnostic context for the aMCI-stage stratification that P-1282's platform-level result operationalises, and P-1282 adds the feasible implementation mechanism (automated chemiluminescent assays) that P-1274's constituent studies, mostly research-grade assays, do not cover. Neither study alone bridges pooled diagnostic evidence with a deployable assay workflow for the MCI window.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Supports a pathway in which meta-analytically validated blood Abeta/tau markers are delivered through automated clinical immunoassay platforms to stratify aMCI patients for AD-continuum biological diagnosis, potentially reducing reliance on invasive CSF or costly PET.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 2): Meta-analysis supplies pooled diagnostic evidence; automated assay supplies implementation evidence. Useful translation complement, not direct validation. Evaluation: Overclaim fix: 'P-1274 materially strengthens... depends on' replaced by pooled-context framing, because the two arms use different contrasts (AD/aMCI vs controls; A+ vs A- within aMCI).
complementary_findings.operator_caveat: Operator G4 required this caveat to appear as an explicit limitation in the manuscript text, not as a quality-flag footnote; the combined_insight / clinical_implication / human_evaluation_note above already carry it.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1275 (systematic review + meta-analysis, 107 studies): NfL and GFAP are elevated in MCI in both CSF (NfL SMD 0.69; GFAP SMD 0.41) and blood (T-tau SMD 0.19; NfL SMD 0.41; GFAP SMD 0.39), supporting fluid neuronal-injury and astroglial markers across compartments.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1282 (N=70 aMCI, A+/A-): fully-automated Lumipulse G plasma Abeta42, Abeta42/40 and p-tau181 assays (best = Abeta42/p-tau181 ratio, AUC 0.895) distinguish aMCI in the AD continuum from aMCI unlikely due to AD, with plasma markers significantly correlating with CSF measures.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: The two papers address complementary molecules of the same fluid-biomarker project for MCI: P-1275 establishes pooled evidence that neurodegeneration (NfL) and astrogliosis (GFAP) markers are elevated in MCI in both CSF and peripheral blood, while P-1282 shows that functional markers of amyloid and tau pathology (Abeta42, p-tau181) measured on an automated plasma platform separate aMCI by A/T(N) status. Read together they indicate that a blood-based MCI work-up could combine an N/X injury-glial pair (NfL, GFAP) with an A/T amyloid-tau axis (Abeta42/p-tau181), each evidenced independently: P-1275 formalises the injury side across compartments, and P-1282 demonstrates the pathology-side specificity in a tightly phenotyped aMCI cohort. No single study in either work integrates both biomarker families on the same automated assay panel.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Motivates evaluation of combined automated plasma panels pairing neurodegeneration/astroglial markers (NfL, GFAP) with amyloid/tau markers (Abeta42/p-tau181) to characterise MCI biology and aMCI AD-status in routine, fully-automated blood workflows.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 1): Strong orthogonal biomarker pairing: NfL/GFAP injury biology plus amyloid/tau pathology biology. Evaluation: Measured complementarity with the joint-assay gap stated explicitly.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1285 (1Florida ADRC, 378 cross-sectional: 76 CNAD-/198 MCIAD-/104 MCIAD+; 207 MCI longitudinal ~3yr): plasma p-tau217 (ALZPath) stratified MCI into AD- (34.4%) and non-AD-etiology groups; p-tau217 independently predicted MCI-to-dementia progression (OR 10.37, 95% CI 3.00-35.02), alongside age (OR 1.14) and neuropsychiatric symptoms (OR 1.19); MCIAD+ were more clinic-recruited (74.8% vs 47.5%) and more APOE-e4 carriers (51.5% vs 26.6%).
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1289 (FACEHBI, Barcelona, 200 SCD followed 5 years): low baseline plasma Abeta42/40 by antibody-free mass spectrometry (ABtest-MS, cutoff <=0.241) was associated with increased amyloid accumulation (beta=0.257), higher risk of conversion to Abeta-PET positivity (HR 2.84) and to MCI due to AD (HR 3.25, 95% CI 1.17-9.01), plus hippocampal/cortical atrophy and ventricular enlargement.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Taken together the two studies map a plasma-only staging axis across the predementia continuum: ABtest-MS Abeta42/40 flags the earliest amyloid-driven risk in SCD (HR 3.25 for SCD-to-MCI conversion), while ALZPath p-tau217 resolves AD versus non-AD etiology at the MCI stage and carries the strongest single-marker progression signal (OR 10.37 to dementia). The two markers therefore operate at different points of the AT(N)-style cascade - Abeta42/40 first, p-tau217 later - so a combined plasma panel spanning both could deliver stage-sensitive prediction from SCD through MCI, but neither of these two studies measures both markers in one cohort. Corpus studies that do measure plasma/serum Abeta42/40 and p-tau217 together in a single cohort include P-1343 (110 amnestic MCI, multi-model biomarker combinations), P-1421 (2148 community dementia-free participants, six serum markers incl. Abeta42/40 and p-tau217 across NC-to-MCI and MCI-to-dementia transitions), P-584 (102 PREVENT-AD cognitively unimpaired adults, plasma Abeta42/40 and p-tau217 in Cox models for CU-to-MCI) and P-1423 (314 SCD + 253 MCI, plasma Abeta42/40 with pTau217 in a 197-patient subset), so the joint (non-redundant) contribution of the two markers is testable in existing corpus data rather than absent from the corpus.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: A plasma cascade combining Abeta42/40 (early SCD risk enrichment) with p-tau217 (MCI etiological stratification and progression risk) could support two-step, cost-effective screening and trial enrichment across the entire predementia window.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 1): SCD amyloid-risk marker and MCI p-tau progression marker form a coherent longitudinal plasma staging concept. Evaluation: Caveats carried in note: OR 10.37 has a wide CI (3.00-35.02) and the arms differ in clinic-recruitment enrichment (74.8% vs 47.5%), so the OR should not be over-read.
complementary_findings.audit_note_2026_09_14: Audit 2026-09-14 (CHALLENGE, major): the confirmed gap clause 'no corpus study measures both markers in one cohort' is false. Refuting blocks: P-1343 line 189424 ('baseline plasma biomarkers (p-tau217, NfL, GFAP, Abeta42/40) ... in amnestic MCI'); P-1421 line 196793 ('six baseline serum AD biomarkers (Abeta42/40, p-tau181, p-tau217, t-tau, NfL, GFAP) ... NC-to-MCI ... MCI-to-AD dementia, including biomarker combinations'); P-584 line 50039 ('plasma Abeta42/40 ratio and p-tau217 ... Cox regression'); P-1423 line 196983 ('plasma pTau181, pTau217 (197-patient subset), Abeta42/40, GFAP and NfL' in 314 SCD + 253 MCI). Clause rescoped to 'neither of these two studies' and the refuting papers named. Status 'confirmed' kept (operator verdict stands); flagged for operator re-check.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1283 (AAV-AD rat model, n=35): chronic DYRK1A inhibition with Leucettine L41 reduced soluble hyperphosphorylated tau (Thr181/Thr212/Ser422) without changing Abeta42 and prevented MCI onset (120h probe target-quadrant preference, p=0.003), establishing that soluble P-tau is necessary - alongside Abeta42 - for the asymptomatic-to-prodromal transition.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1290 (Phase 3 TRx-237-039, 598 amyloid-PET+ participants: 263 MCI / 335 mild-moderate AD, 82 centres): oral tau aggregation inhibitor hydromethylthionine mesylate (HMTM) 16 mg/day significantly reduced NfL progression (p=0.0291) and gray-matter atrophy at 52/104 weeks, reduced pTau217 progression in MCI (p=0.0165), and produced significant MCI cognitive separation (ADAS-cog13) at 78 (p=0.0291) and 104 (p=0.0308) weeks in a modified delayed-start design.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: The pair connects tau-pathology necessity at the molecular level to tau-targeted intervention at the clinical level: the rat pharmacology shows that lowering soluble P-tau alone prevents MCI onset (with Abeta42 held constant), and the human Phase 3 shows that inhibiting tau aggregation with HMTM slows neurodegeneration biomarkers (NfL, pTau217, atrophy) and MCI cognitive decline. The preclinical necessity result is consistent with the clinical tau-targeting signal being detectable in biomarker and delayed-start cognitive endpoints, and both converge on tau as a disease-modifying target in the MCI window; however the rat study targets tau phosphorylation (DYRK1A) while the trial targets tau aggregation, so the exact species modulated differs and cross-species dose/mechanism translation remains unproven.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Supports tau-directed disease-modifying therapy in MCI: biomarker endpoints (NfL, pTau217) may show tau-target engagement earlier than primary cognitive endpoints, informing trial design for oral tau-aggregation inhibitors.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 2): Preclinical tau-phosphorylation mechanism and human tau-treatment result converge, but species/mechanism differ. Evaluation: 'Explains why' softened to 'is consistent with' (species modulated differs: DYRK1A/phosphorylation vs aggregation); duplicate p=0.0291 (NfL progression and 78-week ADAS-cog13) flagged for source verification.
complementary_findings.operator_caveat: Operator G4 required this caveat to appear as an explicit limitation in the manuscript text, not as a quality-flag footnote; the combined_insight / clinical_implication / human_evaluation_note above already carry it.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1292 (matched case-control, Seoul: 212 aMCI + 848 controls; 267 AD + 1,068 controls): higher urinary PAH metabolites 1-OHP (OR 1.15 aMCI / 1.16 AD per log-unit) and 2-NAP (OR 1.11 aMCI / 1.13 AD) were associated with increased aMCI and AD risk, after creatinine adjustment and confounder control (age, education, BMI, smoking, alcohol, disease history).
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1291 (ADNI-1, 618 AD-free: 226 CN / 392 MCI, 48-month follow-up): circulating saturated long-chain fatty acids C14:0, C16:0 and C18:0 were associated with increased risk of MCI-to-AD progression (fully-adjusted HR 1.3-2.2, P=0.0005-0.003), while C20:0 showed no association and no LCFA-MCI association was seen from CN.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Both studies implicate modifiable exogenous or dietary exposures in MCI/AD risk but at different biological levels: P-1292 links an inhaled/ingested environmental toxicant class (urinary PAH metabolites) to aMCI and AD risk in a large matched case-control, while P-1291 links circulating dietary-metabolic saturated fatty acids to MCI-to-AD conversion in a prospective cohort. One is an exposure-outcome association measured at the body-burden level, the other a metabolic-intermediate association; neither adjusts for the other's exposure axis, so the independent versus joint contribution of PAH burden and saturated-fat status to MCI/AD risk remains untested in a single cohort.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Suggests combined modifiable-risk assessment - environmental PAH exposure and dietary saturated-fat status - could sharpen MCI/AD risk stratification and motivate exposure-reduction and dietary prevention strategies.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 2): Environmental PAH burden and circulating saturated fatty acids are distinct modifiable risk axes for the same disease continuum. Evaluation: Honest non-adjustment recorded; reverse-causation risk of urinary PAH (recent-exposure biomarker in a prevalent case-control) is unaddressed - flagged.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1287 (SEACURE consensus, six SEA countries - Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam): current MCI diagnosis/management in Southeast Asia is limited by insufficient resources and awareness; recommended community awareness + screening for vascular-risk individuals, country-level validation of cognitive screening tests, greater blood-biomarker access, and development/validation of novel digitized diagnostics.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1288 (narrative review of Asia, Australasia and Pacific Nations [AAPN]): early-AD (MCI/mild dementia) prevalence and diagnostic practice data are limited and non-comparable across AAPN; lecanemab/donanemab are approved in several AAPN countries but the most appropriate diagnostic pathway is unestablished, and biomarker-testing availability and dementia-specialist capacity in Australia/New Zealand/Korea are flagged as concerns for delivering amyloid-targeting therapies; guidelines need updating.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: The two region-focused syntheses are complementary in coverage and conclusion: the SEACURE consensus defines the scalable diagnosis/management roadmap for the resource-limited, high-risk SEA subregion (awareness, country-validated tests, blood biomarkers, digitized diagnostics), while the AAPN review identifies the readiness bottlenecks in the higher-income Asia-Pacific countries that already approve amyloid-targeting therapies (biomarker/specialist capacity, guideline updates, subtype differentiation). Together they define a two-tier Asia-Pacific early-AD preparedness landscape - capacity-building in SEA, capacity-consolidation and guideline modernisation in Australasia/Northeast Asia - that neither paper covers alone.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Regional health-system planning for early-AD detection and amyloid-targeting-therapy delivery should treat SEA capacity-building and AAPN guideline/capacity modernisation as distinct but coordinated tracks.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 2): Two regional health-system syntheses genuinely cover different but complementary implementation barriers. Evaluation: Review-pairing flag applied for consistency with the review-pairing practice used elsewhere in this batch.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1293 (Hirosaki multiomics, discovery 25 aMCI + 25 HC, validation 12 + 12): peripheral-blood multiomics + AI (XGBoost) yielded the hsa-miR-4455/hsa-let-7b-3p ratio discriminating aMCI from healthy controls (AUC 0.971, sensitivity 0.8, specificity 1.0), with GCN1/ISR pathway and Treg/immunosuppressive-phenotype associations.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1296 (600 subjects, seven international cohorts): blood mtDNA methylation (D-loop/ND1) in a Random Forest predicts MCI-to-ADD progression independently of beta-amyloid status (AUC-ROC 0.903, test sensitivity 95.1%, specificity 70.7%), with D-loop methylation differences visible even before amyloid positivity.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Two minimally invasive blood molecular axes cover the two clinical questions of the MCI window: P-1293's miRNA ratio detects the aMCI state cross-sectionally (AUC 0.971) while P-1296's mtDNA methylation predicts progression to dementia from the same kind of blood draw (AUC 0.903). Neither study measures the other's marker - P-1293 validates only its miRNA layer and has no conversion endpoint, and P-1296 does not test circulating miRNA - so together they outline a detection-to-prognosis blood pipeline (miRNA screen, then mtDNA-methylation prognosis) that no single study has assembled, and each marker's independent contribution to the other's model is untested.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: A combined blood draw measuring both the hsa-miR-4455/let-7b-3p ratio and D-loop/ND1 mtDNA methylation could in principle screen for aMCI and then stratify progression risk, but joint-cohort validation with conversion endpoints is required before clinical use.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 2): miRNA detects aMCI while mtDNA methylation predicts progression; clear detection-to-prognosis complement despite validation asymmetry. Evaluation: Small-N fragility surfaced: validation 12+12 with specificity 1.0; discovery 25+25, AUC 0.971 - carry when citing.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1301 (TTB randomized trial, 76 MCI): 7-month physical+cognitive training reduced plasma IL-6, IL-17A, TNF-alpha and CCL11 and maintained IL-10/TGF-beta/IL-4/BDNF versus control-group decline, with IL-10 proposed as an efficacy biomarker.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1302 (randomized VRADA trial, 29 MCI): 12-week VR cycling+cognitive training produced a favourable serum AD-hallmark profile versus control (higher Abeta42/Abeta40, lower Abeta42, total tau, p181-tau and p181-tau/Abeta42) and lower IL-1beta at follow-up, but reports no cognitive endpoint.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: The two non-pharmacological training trials in MCI move complementary biomarker axes - P-1301 the peripheral inflammatory fingerprint (cytokines/BDNF) and P-1302 the AD-hallmark serum profile (amyloid/tau ratios) - but neither trial reports the other's biomarkers, and neither links its observed biomarker change to cognitive outcome within the same participants (P-1302 has no cognitive endpoint; P-1301's cognitive benefits were established in earlier TTB reports, not in this biomarker study). The joint claim that training-induced biomarker restoration translates to cognitive benefit is therefore assembled from two single-axis studies rather than demonstrated, and combining inflammatory and AD-hallmark panels in one training trial with paired cognitive endpoints is the untested next step.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Future multidomain/VR training trials in MCI should co-measure inflammatory and AD-hallmark serum panels with cognitive endpoints, so biomarker change can be linked to cognitive benefit in the same participants.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 2): Two randomized training studies affect different biomarker families; useful combined hypothesis, though cognition-biomarker linkage is incomplete. Evaluation: Insight honesty exemplary ('assembled from two single-axis studies rather than demonstrated'). Source anomaly to verify before citing: P-1302's 'higher Abeta42/40, lower Abeta42' direction contradicts standard AD biomarker direction.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1299 (meta-analysis, 106 studies / 18,145): group-level serum/plasma IL1beta, IL6, IL8, IL18, CRP and hsCRP are significantly raised in AD (CSF YKL40/MCP-1 raised in AD, YKL40 in MCI) versus healthy controls, with cognition- and sex-modulated heterogeneity.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1300 (ACE, 1,360 with paired CSF-plasma SOMAscan): of 63 inflammatory mediators, only sIL6RA robustly predicted MCI-to-dementia conversion (HR 1.936/SD, Bonferroni-robust) and only 6 of 63 showed any CSF-plasma correlation; SMOC1 was an independent progression marker via amyloid/tau association (HR 1.3).
complementary_findings.combined_insight: The pair quantifies the diagnostic-to-prognostic gap of the inflammatory hypothesis: P-1299 shows circulating pro-inflammatory cytokines are elevated at group level in AD/MCI, while P-1300 shows that in a large paired CSF-plasma cohort nearly none of those markers survive as individual-level conversion predictors (only sIL6RA of 63, Bonferroni-robust) and most lack central-peripheral correlation. The apparent tension - meta-analytic group elevations versus near-total absence of individual-level predictive value - is itself the finding: cross-sectional inflammation differences (P-1299) are not portable to MCI-to-dementia risk stratification (P-1300), a boundary condition invisible from either study alone and unresolved for IL6/YKL-40 specifically.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Inflammatory markers validated for MCI/AD group differences should not be assumed to predict individual MCI-to-dementia progression; candidate markers (IL6, YKL-40, sIL6RA) need individual-level conversion-validation before clinical use.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 1): Particularly strong boundary finding: group-level inflammatory elevation does not translate into individual conversion prediction. Evaluation: Genuine triangulation ('the apparent tension is itself the finding'); part of the group-vs-individual gap is statistical (pooled SMD vs individual HR under Bonferroni), not purely biological - noted.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1315 (Thessaloniki CSF cohort, N=124): bacterial FliC and DING protein levels are elevated in AD CSF vs controls (FliC also in MCI), correlate with each other, tau and COX-1/2, and multilinear regression shows COX-2 determines both - evidence that microbiome-derived PAMPs track neuroinflammation and AD hallmarks in the fluid compartment.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1320 (Alzheimer Hellas Day Care Centre, N=74 MCI): 3-month physical exercise with/without cognitive training reduced serum IL-1beta, IL-6 and p-tau181; PE-only raised Abeta42 and Abeta42/40 and lowered p-tau181/Abeta42; Mixed-only lowered TNF-alpha, Abeta40 and t-tau - showing inflammation and AD-hallmark serum markers are modulable by lifestyle intervention.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: P-1315 and P-1320 are two views of the same inflammation-AD-hallmark axis in the same Greek MCI/AD population that never condition on each other: P-1315 shows bacterial-driven inflammatory signalling (FliC/DING via TLR5/COX) is elevated and correlates with tau in CSF in the association layer, while P-1320 shows exercise and cognitive training can move the serum inflammatory and p-tau/amyloid signals in a protective direction in the intervention layer. A shared mechanism - COX-mediated neuroinflammation observable in both compartments - is implied by the two studies but never tested jointly: whether the modifiable serum biomarker changes P-1320 observes actually shift the CSF bacterial-protein inflammatory burden P-1315 measures is unstudied, and the two compartments (CSF vs serum) and two inference modes (association vs intervention) are complementary rather than redundant evidence.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Intervention trials measuring exercise-induced serum biomarker improvement should also measure CSF or microbiome-derived inflammatory markers (FliC/DING/COX) to test whether peripheral modifiable changes propagate to the CNS compartment, linking the bacterial-inflammation layer to lifestyle responsiveness.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 2): CSF inflammation association plus serum intervention evidence form a genuine compartment/design complement, with caveats. Evaluation: Same-lab Thessaloniki pair: CSF-vs-serum complementarity is source-declared, but cohort overlap is unquantified and content is hypothesis-forward - flagged.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1323 (10 AD / 9 MCI / 10 NC, RSC Adv 2025): plasma exosomal miRNA stage signature across NC-MCI-AD with miR-210-3p and miR-151-3p ROC AUC >0.9 - a small-RNA blood axis spanning the full AD continuum.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1332 (19 P-MCI / 29 S-MCI, IJMS 2021): 20-metabolite plasma panel with 80.3% fivefold-CV accuracy for MCI-to-AD conversion and an eight-metabolite index AUC 0.96, with indole-3-propionic acid (gut-microbiota-derived) predicting progression - a metabolite blood axis aimed at the same conversion question.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: P-1323 and P-1332 are two complementary blood-based molecular axes targeting the same NC-MCI-AD trajectory that are never assayed jointly: exosomal miRNAs (P-1323, small non-coding RNA cargo) and untargeted metabolites including a bacterial tryptophan product (P-1332) both show stage-specific signal from peripheral blood, but no corpus study measures miRNA and metabolite axes in the same MCI cohort to test whether they carry independent or redundant conversion information - a combined multi-omic blood panel (miRNA + metabolome) for MCI-to-AD conversion was not found in the corpus.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: A combined plasma exosomal-miRNA + metabolomics panel could stratify MCI conversion risk across two independent molecular axes, potentially improving specificity over either alone; a joint-assay feasibility study is the natural next step.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 2): Two peripheral molecular axes address diagnosis and progression; both studies are small single-centre cohorts. Evaluation: Explicit corpus-search statement ('was not found in the corpus') is good practice; flags appropriate.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1327 (BAAD, ADNI + 4 external sets, Front Neurol 2021): VBM+SVM on structural MRI diagnoses AD at 90.5% and predicts MCI progression at 83-85%, outperforming radiologists - an imaging-only, scalable AD-spectrum classifier.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1330 (401 MCI AT(N)-classified, 176 analysed, NeuroImage: Clinical 2021): among ADNI MCI participants, A+T-(N+) 'mismatch' MCI is non-AD-like - milder baseline memory loss, slower decline, MTL-restricted atrophy vs prodromal AD (A+T+(N+)) - showing biomarker-defined subgroups within the AD spectrum have distinct trajectories.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: P-1327 and P-1330 are complementary views of the same ADNI AD-spectrum that never inform each other: P-1327's structural-MRI classifier sorts everyone into an AD-spectrum bucket at high accuracy without distinguishing the tau-negative 'mismatch' subgroup P-1330 shows has a markedly milder course, while P-1330's CSF-tau-based separation is invisible to the imaging-only classifier. No corpus study tests whether the imaging spectrum P-1327 defines can itself detect the tau-negative mismatch profile P-1330 characterises (e.g., via the MTL-restricted atrophy pattern), which would let an MRI-only pipeline flag probable non-AD pathology without lumbar puncture. The pair exposes an imaging-vs-CSF-ladder gap in ADNI-based MCI stratification.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: MRI-only AD-spectrum classifiers should be benchmarked against P-1330's A+T-(N+) mismatch group; if MTL-restricted atrophy serves as an imaging proxy for the mismatch profile, non-invasive triage of probable non-AD MCI becomes feasible.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 1): MRI classifier and CSF AT(N) subgroup expose a specific, testable MRI-versus-biomarker stratification gap. Evaluation: P-1330's '401 classified, 176 analysed' (56% not analysed) noted; both-ADNI shared substrate makes the proposed test directly feasible (a positive).

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1333 (ADNI, 732 MCI: 270 converters / 462 stable, Transl Neurodegener 2021): PRS including/excluding the APOE region predicts MCI-to-dementia conversion with the association significantly stronger in APOE e4 non-carriers (PRS+APOE HR 1.710, 95% CI 1.244-2.351) than carriers (HR 1.167), interaction p=0.0378 - APOE-genotype-stratified genetic conversion prediction.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1335 (ADNI 767 MCI + NACC 1373 MCI, J Alzheimers Dis 2021): a 40-SNP non-APOE PRS predicts time to AD from MCI (beta 0.182, p=0.003) with independent NACC replication (beta 0.094, p=0.009), tracks ADAS-Cog/tau/amyloid and atrophy, with Abeta42 mediation - an externally replicated non-APOE genetic predictor.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: The two papers triangulate the genetic signal for MCI-to-AD conversion from complementary design edges: P-1333 stratifies by APOE genotype in a single cohort and finds the PRS effect is APOE-dependent (strongest where APOE e4 is absent), while P-1335 deliberately removes the APOE region and shows the residual 40-SNP signal itself replicates across ADNI and NACC and operates through Abeta42-mediated pathways. Together they resolve the apparent tension in the genetic-risk literature: the APOE-stratified view (P-1333) and the non-APOE-averaged view (P-1335) are not contradictory but describe the same gradient at different grain, since P-1335's replication of the non-APOE component complements P-1333's demonstration that total-signal strength varies with e4 carrier status. P-1333 itself reports the non-APOE score's hazard stratified by e4 status within ADNI (non-carriers PRS-APOE HR 1.429, 95% CI 1.182-1.728 vs carriers HR 1.172), so the residual gap is not joint reporting but external replication of the stratified analysis: P-1333 has no independent replication cohort and P-1335 does not stratify by APOE genotype, which is why the two PRS lenses remain complementary rather than redundant. Limitation: both arms draw their MCI participants from ADNI (732 in P-1333 vs 767 in P-1335), so the two findings are partially same-cohort and not independent; the independence reading rests on P-1335's NACC replication (1373 MCI), not on the ADNI arms.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Genetic MCI risk models should report APOE-stratified estimates (P-1333-style) alongside replicated non-APOE PRS (P-1335-style) so trials can enrich non-carriers with polygenic signal and carriers with APOE-knowledgeable priors - noting that the two source studies overlap in ADNI MCI participants, so their agreement is not two independent confirmations.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 1): APOE-stratified PRS and independently replicated non-APOE PRS illuminate complementary parts of the same genetic risk signal. Evaluation: CAVEAT: both arms use overlapping ADNI MCI samples (732 vs 767) - the NACC replication inside P-1335 is what supports the independence reading, so 'triangulate' must not be read as full sample independence.
complementary_findings.operator_caveat: Operator G4 required this caveat to appear as an explicit limitation in the manuscript text, not as a quality-flag footnote; the combined_insight / clinical_implication / human_evaluation_note above already carry it.

NACC (1373 MCI ...)'). Venues verified: Transl Neurodegener 2021 (line 188565), J Alzheimers Dis 2021 (line 188754). Status kept.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1336 (meta-analysis, 7 studies n=902, Front Aging Neurosci 2021): olfactory-identification score correlates with hippocampal volume (pooled r=0.34), with the correlation stronger in AD (r=0.40) and MCI (r=0.37) than controls (r=0.13) - linking a behaviour (olfaction) to MTL structure.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1339 (ADNI 1654: 605 NC / 766 MCI / 283 AD, Adv Sci 2022): R2SN radiomics-similarity networks split MCI into A-CI (AD-like, 61.5% 3-year progression) and N-CI (NC-like, 21.8%) subtypes with distinct gene enrichment - structure-derived MCI risk stratification.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: P-1336 and P-1339 converge on the medial-temporal-lobe axis from opposite measurement sides in the same disease population: P-1336 shows a behavioural probe (olfactory identification) correlates with hippocampal volume, and more strongly in MCI and AD, precisely the population in which P-1339's radiomics-similarity networks define structure-linked high- versus low-risk MCI subtypes. Together they suggest a combined risk model in which an inexpensive olfactory test (whose MTL correlation P-1336 has now pooled) could pre-screen candidates whose radiomics-defined subtype (P-1339) then refines conversion risk - a two-tier non-invasive pipeline, olfaction to imaging, that no single corpus study evaluates as an integrated sequence.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Olfactory testing operating at near-zero cost could enrich or triage toward structural-MRI-based subtype stratification (A-CI vs N-CI), making P-1339's imaging stratification more efficient in primary care.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 2): Olfaction provides low-cost MTL-related screening, while radiomics supplies structural conversion stratification; plausible two-stage pathway. Evaluation: 'Converge on the MTL axis' overstates the equivalence of the two structural readouts (pooled r=0.34 vs whole-brain radiomic-similarity networks) - noted.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1340 (ADNI 471 CN + HABS external, Front Aging Neurosci 2022): a sex-specific CN-to-MCI risk score from age, APOE e4, MMSE and CDR reaches C-statistics 0.902/0.911 (female/male) with strong external performance (0.950/0.965) - an externally validated clinical risk tool at the earliest transition.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1342 (Shanghai Aging Study, 316 MCI, 4.5-year follow-up, Front Genet 2022): PVRL2 rs6859 AG/AA carriers progress from MCI to AD more than GG (HR 2.75, p=0.007), and in carriers each +1 mmol/L LDL-C lowers AD risk 48% (HR 0.52) - a genotype x lipid interaction at the MCI stage.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: P-1340 and P-1342 address conversion risk at two adjacent transitions with tools that never meet: P-1340 flags who will enter MCI from CN using a cheap externally validated clinical score whose genetic component is APOE e4 alone, while P-1342 shows that beyond the CN-to-MCI boundary, progression within MCI is modulated by a different genetic variant (PVRL2) interacting with lipids. Together the papers imply that genetic awareness at the CN-to-MCI stage (APOE-based score, P-1340) and at the MCI-to-AD stage (PVRL2 x LDL-C, P-1342) captures distinct loci, so a unified genetic-aware care pathway would need both markers across the two transitions - an integrated risk-ladder design no corpus study currently implements.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Prevention pathways should combine an APOE-based CN-to-MCI clinical score (P-1340) with PVRL2 x LDL-C-aware follow-up during MCI (P-1342), testing both markers in one longitudinal cohort.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 2): Different genetic loci operate at adjacent CN-to-MCI and MCI-to-AD transitions; valid staged-risk complement. Evaluation: Cross-population flag (ADNI/HABS US vs Shanghai) missing; external C-statistics (0.950/0.965) exceeding internal (0.902/0.911) is atypical and worth a source-check.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1343 (Flutemetamol PET trial cohort NCT01028053, Lund/Skane, Sweden, 110 amnestic MCI - 26 progressors, Alzheimer's Research & Therapy 2022): a parsimonious model combining plasma p-tau217 with the mPACC cognitive composite reaches AUC 0.87 (0.89 for the full model adding hippocampal volume and APOE) for conversion to amyloid-positive AD dementia within 3 years, computed without amyloid-PET status as a predictor.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1346 (Swedish BioFINDER cohort 1 + Skane University Hospital Memory Clinic, n=199, Alzheimer's Research & Therapy 2022): a head-to-head comparison shows the novel Simoa p-tau217+Janssen assay matches the established Lilly assay for both CSF-Abeta42/40-based amyloid detection and MCI-to-AD prognosis prediction.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: P-1343 and P-1346 jointly make plasma p-tau217 deployable for MCI-to-AD progression: P-1343 shows that pairing p-tau217 with an accessible cognitive composite (mPACC) is enough to reach AUC 0.87 (0.89 with hippocampal volume and APOE added) without PET as a predictor, and P-1346 shows the two leading p-tau217 assay platforms agree on both amyloid status and prognosis. Read together they imply the blood p-tau217 + cognition pathway is not assay-vendor-dependent - the accuracy gains of P-1343 should survive transfer across the interchangeable platforms characterised in P-1346 - a claim neither study alone can support because P-1343 used one assay and P-1346 never added mPACC to its model. Both studies come from the same Lund group (shared authors including Bali, Janelidze and Hansson), so the portability claim rests on one team's two cohorts rather than on independent replication.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: A blood-first triage for MCI-to-AD using p-tau217 plus a short cognitive composite can be adopted without vendor lock-in or PET access, provided the specific assay x cognition interaction is re-verified once.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 2): p-tau217 accuracy plus cross-assay equivalence; genuine portability complement, but assay-by-cognition interaction remains untested. Evaluation: same_region_caution correctly applied (both Lund/Skane); vendor-independence claim is genuinely pair-level.

AUC conflation fixed per P-1343 line 189436 ('parsimonious p-tau217 + mPACC model had AUC 0.87'; 'adding hippocampal volume, cognition and APOE raised discrimination to AUC 0.89') and endpoint per line 189430. Same-team non-independence added from author lists (line 189508: Bali, Janelidze, Hansson; line 189792: Bali, Janelidze, Hansson). 'Skane' ASCII-normalised (U+00E5). Status kept.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1344 (ADNI plasma gene-expression, n=358 - 46 unstable / 312 stable MCI, Int J Environ Res Public Health 2022): a 31-probe (29-gene) random-forest classifier separates stable from unstable MCI with 10-fold CV AUC 0.841 and independent ADNI test AUC 0.775 - a transcriptomic fingerprint of the stable MCI boundary.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1352 (NCGG Biobank Japan, 856 RNA-seq samples - 317 AD / 432 MCI / 107 CN; 145 MCI followed for a mean of 896 days, about 2.5 years): a blood immune-repertoire model combining IGK+TRA repertoire diversity and WDR37 expression with age, sex and APOE4 covariates classifies MCI-to-AD progression risk with C-index 0.694 (discovery) / 0.643 (validation split) - an adaptive-immune-composition readout of conversion.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: P-1344 and P-1352 probe two orthogonal layers of the same stable-vs-progressing MCI question that no single study combines: P-1344 reads the transcriptomic state of blood cells with a 29-gene panel, while P-1352 reads the clonal composition of the adaptive immune repertoire (IGK+TRA) plus one immune candidate gene (WDR37), alongside age, sex and APOE4 covariates in its final model. Because P-1344's genes and P-1352's repertoire features are mechanistically disjoint (expression programme vs clonal diversity) yet both rank MCI on the same conversion axis, a joint blood panel could in principle capture variance invisible to either layer alone - though P-1352's immune-repertoire layer is the weaker predictor (C-index 0.643 vs P-1344's AUC 0.841/0.775 - a C-index and an ROC-AUC are not directly commensurable, so this is a loose weaker/stronger flag only), so whether it adds variance beyond the transcriptomic panel is untested; the two studies come from different continents (ADNI vs NCGG Japan) so any cross-layer signal would also be a cross-ethnic claim.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Combine the 29-gene expression panel with immune-repertoire diversity measures in one longitudinal MCI cohort to test whether transcriptomic and adaptive-immune layers carry independent conversion information.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 2): Transcriptomic state and adaptive immune repertoire are orthogonal blood predictors of MCI progression. Evaluation: Performance asymmetry surfaced in-insight: P-1352 is the weaker layer (C-index 0.643 vs AUC 0.841/0.775), so the joint-panel additivity premise is untested.
complementary_findings.operator_caveat: Operator G4 required this caveat to appear as an explicit limitation in the manuscript text, not as a quality-flag footnote; the combined_insight / clinical_implication / human_evaluation_note above already carry it.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1347 (AIBL, Australia, n=186 - 154 cognitively healthy + 32 MCI; Biomedicines 2022): CSF neurofilament light predicts dementia onset in cognitively healthy older adults (HR 4.77) and stratifies the rate of cognitive decline in MCI - a fluid-based molecular early-warning signal.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1348 (multi-centre Italian community cohort, n=459 - 80 preserved / 379 MCI; Front Aging Neurosci 2022): hierarchical clustering shows a hypertension/bone-joint chronic-disease cluster predicts progression from preserved cognitive health to MCI (OR 4.0) and low WBC count predicts MCI-to-dementia progression (OR 4.2), while higher Na and lower TSH predict MCI reversion - modifiable clinical and biochemical predictors of both directions of cognitive change.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: P-1347 and P-1348 predict cognitive trajectories from opposite ends of the measurement spectrum: P-1347 with a single molecular neurodegeneration marker (CSF NfL) in an Australian cohort, P-1348 with routine clinical/biochemical predictors (hypertension, bone-joint disease, WBC, Na, TSH) in Italian community-dwellers. Neither study tests the other's feature class, so the corpus has no model asking whether NfL elevation and modifiable clinical-signal derangement carry independent progression information; P-1348 is additionally rare in predicting reversion (Na up, TSH down), a transition P-1347's NfL framework never addresses, so the two markers may subserve different decision nodes (who declines fast vs who may recover).
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: A combined score using CSF NfL for decline-rate stratification (P-1347 measured CSF NfL only and lists the absence of a plasma NfL comparison as a gap, so any blood-NfL version is an untested extrapolation) plus modifiable clinical-biochemical clusters (blood pressure control, WBC, Na, TSH) could cover both progression and reversion counselling in memory clinics.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 2): CSF NfL and routine clinical/biochemical predictors cover different progression/reversion decision nodes. Evaluation: Note: P-1347 measured CSF NfL only (the 'CSF/blood NfL' extrapolation is avoided in the promoted text); reversion coverage rests on n=32 MCI within n=186.
complementary_findings.audit_note_2026_09_14: Audit 2026-09-14 (CHALLENGE, major). Venue/year invented: P-1347 block line 189890 'Biomedicines 10(5): 1045, 2022 (MDPI)' (record said Alzheimers Dement 2019). Two-transition conflation in finding_b fixed per P-1348 line 189910 ('Hypertension/bone-and-joint disease cluster predicted PCH-to-MCI progression (OR 4.0); ... lower white blood cells predicted MCI-to-dementia (OR 4.2)'). 'CSF/blood NfL' extrapolation - which the operator note says was avoided but was present in clinical_implication - flagged per P-1347 line 189845 ('no plasma NfL comparison') and line 189824 ('plasma NfL evaluation for clinical applicability' as an improvement). Note: the operator note's 'reversion coverage rests on n=32 MCI within n=186' misattributes reversion to P-1347; reversion is P-1348's finding (379 MCI) - note left untouched, flagged for operator. Status kept.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1350 (Asan Medical Center Seoul, n=103 amyloid-negative amnestic MCI, 39 converters; ADNI UC Berkeley florbetaben replication n=48; Alzheimer's Research & Therapy 2022): in amyloid-NEGATIVE amnestic MCI, subthreshold regional 18F-florbetaben SUVR still predicts dementia conversion - left parietal SUVR was the best single predictor (AUC 0.762) and a precuneus+parietal+composite model reached AUC 0.763, with converters showing higher SUVR across temporal, parietal, precuneus, posterior cingulate and occipital regions; the ADNI replication was much weaker (left precuneus AUC 0.596) - challenging the PET-positivity dichotomy for prognosis.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1343 (Flutemetamol PET trial cohort NCT01028053, Lund/Skane, n=110 amnestic MCI; Alzheimer's Research & Therapy 2022): plasma p-tau217 plus the mPACC cognitive composite predicts conversion to amyloid-positive AD dementia within 3 years at AUC 0.87 (0.89 for the full model adding hippocampal volume and APOE), computed without amyloid-PET status as a predictor.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: P-1350 and P-1343 both chip at the amyloid-binarity assumption from opposite ends of the biomarker ladder: P-1350 shows that among PET-amyloid-negatives, residual subthreshold regional SUVR signal still predicts conversion (left parietal AUC 0.762 in the Seoul cohort; the ADNI replication reached only AUC 0.596, so the residual is weakly replicated), while P-1343 shows a plasma tau + cognition pathway reaches AUC 0.87-0.89 with no amyloid-PET input as a predictor (its endpoint is conversion to amyloid-positive AD dementia, so amyloid status still anchors the outcome). Together they define an amyloid-window problem with two unintegrated handles - subthreshold regional PET quantitation (P-1350) and plasma p-tau217 (P-1343) - neither of which is used by the other, so a study combining both could resolve whether the prognostic residual in the 'negative' band is tau-driven, subthreshold-plaque-driven, or both.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: For PET-amyloid-negative aMCI, add plasma p-tau217 and regional (not global) subthreshold SUVR quantitation to a combined progression risk score before declaring patients low-risk by binary amyloid status - noting that the subthreshold-SUVR prognostic signal replicated only weakly in ADNI (AUC 0.596).
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 1): Subthreshold amyloid PET and plasma p-tau217 address complementary pieces of the amyloid/tau progression window. Evaluation: The same_region_caution on this pairing is a flag-propagation artifact (Seoul/ADNI/Berkeley vs Sweden share no region) - not applied to the promoted record; the amyloid-window framing itself is strong.
complementary_findings.audit_note_2026_09_14: Audit 2026-09-14 (CHALLENGE, critical). finding_a named 'lateral temporal cortex' as the standout predictive region; P-1350 block line 190099 states 'left parietal SUVR best predicted conversion (AUC 0.762, P<0.001); precuneus+parietal+composite model AUC 0.763; in ADNI, left precuneus SUVR highest (AUC 0.596)' - 'lateral temporal' appears nowhere in the block. Venue/year corrected: P-1350 block line 190174 'Alzheimer's Research & Therapy 14: 93, 2022' (record said Ann Clin Transl Neurol 2018); P-1343 block line 189511 'Alzheimer's Research & Therapy 14: 46, 2022' (record said Alzheimers Dement 2025). Weak ADNI replication (AUC 0.596, lines 190099/190123) added as a qualifier. P-1343 outcome scoped per block line 189430 ('conversion to amyloid-positive AD dementia within 3 years') and AUCs per line 189436 (0.87 parsimonious, 0.89 full). Operator human_evaluation_note left untouched.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1359 (Sixth People's Hospital Shanghai n=609, PET-confirmed; Communications Medicine 2023): integrated decision-tree models of plasma Simoa biomarkers (A-beta42/40, T-tau, P-tau181, NfL) plus cognition/APOE predict brain A-beta-PET positivity with AUC 0.94 overall and 0.97 in MCI, validated in ADNI.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1360 (GEO peripheral-blood transcriptomes >65 years + qRT-PCR; J Alzheimers Dis 2024): mitochondrial complex-I genes NDUFA1 and NDUFS5, combined with age, diagnose late-onset AD (AUC 0.723 LOAD-vs-CN) and discriminate MCI (AUC 0.65-0.67), with expression lower in LOAD/MCI blood.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: P-1359 and P-1360 are two non-invasive blood panels reading orthogonal molecular layers of the same MCI/AD discrimination problem: P-1359 measures the circulating protein state (amyloid/tau/NfL concentrations) while P-1360 reads mitochondrial mRNA expression of blood cells, and neither study combines protein biomarkers with blood gene-expression features. The two panels also diverge in mechanism (amyloid-pathway signalling vs bioenergetic/mitochondrial status), so a joint liquid-biopsy model could capture variance invisible to either layer alone; their different ethnic settings (Chinese vs public multi-cohort GEO) make cross-layer signal a potential cross-population claim that no corpus paper yet tests.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: A staged blood triage that first predicts A-beta status (P-1359) and then adds a qPCR mitochondrial gene panel (P-1360) might add complementary information, but the two panels target different endpoints (A-beta-PET positivity vs clinical LOAD) and the gene-expression layer is the weaker discriminator (AUC 0.65-0.67), so the additive value is untested and should not be assumed before a joint cohort exists.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 2): Protein biomarkers and mitochondrial transcriptomics are genuinely orthogonal liquid-biopsy layers. Evaluation: Endpoint mismatch (A-beta-PET positivity vs clinical LOAD) and the weak gene-expression layer (AUC 0.65-0.67) bound the 'could improve' claim - revised in the implication.
complementary_findings.operator_caveat: Operator G4 required this caveat to appear as an explicit limitation in the manuscript text, not as a quality-flag footnote; the combined_insight / clinical_implication / human_evaluation_note above already carry it.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1362 (BIOCARD n=269 cognitively normal, mean age 57.7y, 16.3y follow-up; Ann Neurol 2023): lower baseline CSF NPTX2 predicts earlier MCI symptom onset (HR 0.76, p=0.023) and is additive and independent of CSF A-beta42/40, p-tau181 and t-tau (chi-square=11.5, p<0.01) with no biomarker interactions.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1357 (ADNI GO/2 n=606 CN+MCI; Alzheimers Res Ther 2023): baseline MTL-subregion structural MRI plus plasma p-tau181/NfL jointly discriminate fast from slow progressors of longitudinal atrophy/cognition with AUC 0.89-0.93 in MCI and 0.65-0.73 in CN.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: P-1362 and P-1357 attack the same early-AD trial-enrichment problem from two different temporal windows that no single study bridges: P-1362 identifies who will cross the normal-to-MCI threshold at all (synaptic-circuit-homeostasis marker NPTX2, additive to amyloid/tau, acting in mid-life), while P-1357 predicts, among people already at risk, how fast subsequent atrophy and cognitive decline will run (structural MRI plus plasma state markers). One is a transition-onset marker, the other a rate-of-decline marker, so a trial design that screens for imminent onset with NPTX2 and then stratifies enrolled MCI for decline speed with MRI+plasma would use complementary information; the corpus contains no study combining a synaptic CSF marker with MTL-subregion MRI and plasma in one cohort.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Preclinical screening could pair NPTX2 (onset prediction in CN) with MRI/plasma progressor scoring (decline-rate prediction in MCI) to enrich trials for fast, imminent converters.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 2): NPTX2 predicts entry into MCI while MRI/plasma predicts subsequent rate; clear sequential complement. Evaluation: Clean onset-vs-rate window logic (BIOCARD mid-life HR 0.76 vs ADNI MCI AUC 0.89-0.93); cohort flag noted.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1353 (ADNI 767 + NACC 1373 MCI; J Alzheimers Dis 2023): six novel neurotrophin-pathway SNPs (TP73, PIK3R1, CALM1, PLCG2) and their PRS improve 3-year MCI-to-AD prediction (ADNI AUC 0.720 vs 0.682, p=0.003; NACC 0.609 vs 0.586), and the PRS tracks longitudinal cognition, CSF tau/A-beta and MTL atrophy.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1357 (ADNI GO/2 n=606; Alzheimers Res Ther 2023): baseline MTL-subregion MRI and plasma p-tau181/NfL jointly predict fast vs slow progressors with AUC 0.89-0.93 in MCI, outperforming either modality alone.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: P-1353 and P-1357 predict the same outcome, MCI progression, from two measurement axes that are constitutionally different: P-1353 uses fixed germline genotypes (inherited neurotrophin-pathway risk), whereas P-1357 uses time-varying baseline state biomarkers (structural integrity and plasma p-tau/NfL). Because the two axes are mechanistically disjoint - inherited pathway signalling propensity vs current neurodegeneration load - the variance each explains in conversion risk is plausibly additive, yet no corpus paper fits a model that enters a pathway PRS alongside MTL-subregion MRI and plasma biomarkers together; such an integrated genetic-plus-state model would test whether trial enrichment gains from combining both, and it would settle whether P-1353's ADNI-only longitudinal associations survive when state biomarkers are co-adjusted. Limitations: both studies draw their MCI participants from ADNI (P-1353's discovery arm is 767 ADNI MCI; P-1357 is ADNI-GO/2, n=606), so the two findings are partially same-cohort with unquantified participant overlap and are not fully independent; and the PRS increments are marginal (ADNI AUC 0.682 to 0.720, +0.038; NACC 0.586 to 0.609, +0.023) against the MRI/plasma model's AUC 0.89-0.93, so additivity is plausible but unquantified.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Add the 6-SNP neurotrophin PRS to MRI/plasma progressor models in trial enrichment; if additive, genotyping becomes a cheap pre-screen before imaging - but the PRS increments are small (+0.038 ADNI, +0.023 NACC) and the two source studies share ADNI participants, so the pre-screen implication must not be over-read.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 1): Germline PRS and current-state MRI/plasma biomarkers address distinct sources of conversion risk. Evaluation: CAVEAT: unquantified ADNI participant overlap (P-1353 ADNI 767 + NACC 1373 vs P-1357 ADNI GO/2 n=606); PRS increments are marginal (ADNI +0.038; NACC +0.023) against MRI/plasma AUC 0.89-0.93, so the 'cheap pre-screen' implication must not be over-read.
complementary_findings.operator_caveat: Operator G4 required this caveat to appear as an explicit limitation in the manuscript text, not as a quality-flag footnote; the combined_insight / clinical_implication / human_evaluation_note above already carry it.
