Venues verified (J Alzheimers Dis 2023 line 190458; Alz Res Ther 2023 line 190834). Status kept.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1365 (BioFINDER-1 n=504; Alzheimers Res Ther 2024): an aMCI-trained OPLS severity index from structural MRI predicts SCD-to-MCI/dementia over 8 years with AUC 0.72 (sens 72.3%, spec 60.9%) vs 0.57 for a dementia-trained model, with aMCI-like SCD at HR 2.9.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1368 (140 SCD/MCI/AD patients, Florence; Eur J Neurol 2024): plasma NfL detects ATN-defined biological AD with AUC 0.82, proposed SCD/MCI cutoffs of 19.45/20.49 pg/mL, and an NfL change rate <1.64 pg/mL/year that excludes MCI-to-AD progression (AUC 0.954).
complementary_findings.combined_insight: P-1365 and P-1368 are two non-invasive, state-marker approaches to the same SCD/MCI progression question that measure different neurodegeneration signals - P-1365 reads structural atrophy pattern (MRI-derived severity index) while P-1368 reads axonal damage burden (plasma NfL) - and both are single-centre European cohorts with no joint model; the corpus contains no study combining an MRI atrophy-severity index with plasma NfL and its change rate in the same SCD/MCI cohort, so whether the two signals are additive, redundant or complementary for conversion prediction is untested.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: A screening pipeline could use plasma NfL (cheap, repeatable) to rule out fast conversion via change rate and reserve MRI severity-index scoring for NfL-positive SCD patients, but the combined model needs direct evaluation.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 2): MRI atrophy and plasma NfL are distinct state markers for the same progression question. Evaluation: Cross-cohort flag (Sweden vs Italy) missing despite 'single-centre European' in the text; 'change rate... excludes progression (AUC 0.954)' conflates a rule-out (NPV property) with an AUC - noted.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1363 (60 Chinese subjects: 20 MCI, 20 AD, 20 CHC; Front Genet 2023): blood leukocyte DNA methylome EWAS identifies 441 common DMPs over 213 genes with single-CpG MCI-vs-control ROC AUC up to 0.988 (cg18771300; an in-sample ROC from 20 MCI vs 20 controls - the methylation difference was confirmed by pyrosequencing in independent samples but the AUC has no independent-cohort replication and should be read as optimistic) and cortex-enriched genes SYT7, SYN3, KCNT1.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1370 (ADNI WGS n=1545; Front Aging Neurosci 2023): imaging-informed oligogenic risk score adORS from 20 FDG/AV45-PET-correlated genes beats PRS for CN-vs-AD classification (0.750 vs 0.735 with APOE) but not for MCI conversion prediction (0.637 vs 0.643 with APOE), with SHAP-balanced gene contributions.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: P-1363 and P-1370 read two different genomic layers of AD risk in blood - P-1363 captures environmentally modifiable epigenetic marks (DNA methylation) in a Chinese cohort while P-1370 captures fixed germline sequence variants (oligogenic SNP burdens) in ADNI; neither study combines methylation signatures with sequence-based risk scores, and the two populations (Chinese vs European-ancestry ADNI) make any cross-layer signal a cross-population claim; the corpus has no integrated blood genomic model entering both layers, so whether methylation adds variance beyond an oligogenic sequence score - and whether either transfers across ancestries - is untested. Limitation: P-1363's single-CpG AUC of 0.988 is an in-sample ROC on 20 MCI vs 20 controls with no independent-cohort replication of the classifier and must be cited with that caveat.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: An integrated blood genomic risk score combining germline oligogenic burden with leukocyte methylation marks could stratify AD/MCI risk before biomarker confirmation, but requires joint measurement in one cohort.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 2): DNA methylation and germline sequence risk are genuinely distinct genomic layers; clean integration gap. Evaluation: Data-integrity fix: P-1370 'beats PRS' holds for CN-vs-AD only, not MCI conversion (0.637 vs 0.643 per its own numbers); the single-CpG AUC up to 0.988 from n=20/20 is near-certainly overfit and must be cited with that caveat.
complementary_findings.operator_caveat: Operator G4 required this caveat to appear as an explicit limitation in the manuscript text, not as a quality-flag footnote; the combined_insight / clinical_implication / human_evaluation_note above already carry it.
complementary_findings.audit_note_2026_09_14: Audit 2026-09-14 (UPHOLD_WITH_NOTES, major): operator mandated that 'AUC up to 0.988 from n=20/20 ... must be cited with that caveat' (caveat_level=major) but finding_a cited it bare and the caveat lived only in human_evaluation_note. Caveat written into finding_a and combined_insight from the P-1363 block: line 191320 ('60 participants: 20 MCI, 20 AD and 20 cognitively healthy controls'), line 191323 ('cg18771300 AUC 0.988 ... Pyrosequencing confirmed cg07157030 and cg18771300 in independent samples'), line 191329 ('the identified signatures lack independent-cohort replication'). Venues verified (Front Genet 2023 line 191398; Front Aging Neurosci 2023 line 192056). Status kept.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1366 (192 subjects: 63 AD, 71 MCI, 58 NDC, Japan; Int J Mol Sci 2023): 8-protein LC-MS/MS plasma panel (ALB, APOC1, C3, C4G, A2AP, A2M, HPX, A1BG) discriminates AD vs NDC with AUC 0.90/0.80 and cognitive impairment vs NDC with 0.83/0.71 by sex.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1367 (424 subjects: 89 PD, 47 DLB, 147 AD, 111 MCI, 30 CN, Japan; Int J Mol Sci 2023): multimarker scores built around plasma FABP2/3/5/7 but also incorporating established biomarkers measured in the same assay run (alpha-synuclein, Abeta42, Tau, pTau181, GFAP, NF-L, UCHL1 - e.g. (FABP3 x NF-L x FABP5)/(FABP2 x GFAP x Abeta42) for AD vs DLB) discriminate MCI vs CN (AUC 0.9321) and disease pairs AD-DLB (0.8531), PD-DLB (0.8831), AD-PD (0.8593), with FABP3 tracking MMSE.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: P-1366 and P-1367 are two Japanese single-centre plasma panels that measure largely disjoint protein classes - P-1366 reads nutritional/coagulation/innate-immune homeostasis proteins while P-1367 reads fatty-acid-binding protein markers (FABP2/3/5/7) together with established neurodegeneration analytes (alpha-synuclein, Abeta42, Tau, pTau181, GFAP, NF-L, UCHL1) that enter its scoring formulas - and neither study assays the other's analytes (P-1367 does not measure ALB/APOC1/C3/C4G/A2AP/A2M/HPX/A1BG; P-1366 does not measure FABPs), so a combined plasma panel spanning both protein families could improve MCI detection and the PD/DLB/AD differential diagnosis that each panel addresses only partially; no corpus paper measures FABPs together with an ALB/APOC1/C3-class panel in one cohort.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: A single multiplexed plasma assay combining FABP scores with the 8-protein homeostasis panel could support both MCI screening and synucleinopathy differential diagnosis from one blood draw.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 2): Two Japanese plasma panels measure largely disjoint protein families; reasonable additive-information hypothesis. Evaluation: Contamination fix: GFAP/NfL/UCHL1 removed from P-1367's analyte list (its finding names FABP2/3/5/7 only); the disjoint-family pairing itself is sound.
complementary_findings.operator_caveat: Operator G4 required this caveat to appear as an explicit limitation in the manuscript text, not as a quality-flag footnote; the combined_insight / clinical_implication / human_evaluation_note above already carry it.
complementary_findings.audit_note_2026_09_14: Audit 2026-09-14 (CHALLENGE, major): the G4 'contamination fix' removed GFAP/NfL/UCHL1 from P-1367's analyte list on the premise that 'its finding names FABP2/3/5/7 only', but the P-1367 block line 191687 states the paper measured FABPs 'together with established biomarkers (alpha-synuclein, Abeta42, Tau, pTau181, GFAP, NF-L, UCHL1)' and line 191693 gives the scoring formula '(FABP3 x NF-L x FABP5)/(FABP2 x GFAP x Abeta42) for AD vs DLB'. finding_b and combined_insight restored to the block's analyte list; the narrower disjointness claim (no ALB/APOC1-class proteins in P-1367, no FABPs in P-1366; P-1366 line 191590+) retained. Venues verified (Int J Mol Sci 2023, lines 191680/191774). Status kept.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1368 (140 SCD/MCI/AD patients, Florence; Eur J Neurol 2024): plasma NfL detects ATN-defined AD (AUC 0.82) and its change rate <1.64 pg/mL/year excludes MCI-to-AD progression (AUC 0.954).
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1372 (209 subjects: 91 AD, 92 MCI, 26 controls; GeroScience 2024): CSF neutral lipids CE(11D3:1) and an unknown lipid associate with MCI-to-AD progression (model AUC 0.88) and TG(O-52:2) with faster progression over median 58 months, with 52.2% of MCI converting.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: P-1368 and P-1372 predict the same outcome, MCI-to-AD progression, from two different fluid compartments and metabolic axes - P-1368 uses a blood marker of axonal damage (NfL and its longitudinal change) while P-1372 uses CSF markers of lipid metabolism and storage (cholesteryl esters, ether-linked triglycerides) - and neither study measures the other's analytes, so the corpus contains no cohort testing whether CSF neutral lipids add predictive value beyond plasma NfL change rate, or whether lipid dysregulation and axonal injury mark independent progression paths; both studies are single-centre with no external validation, making their joint model doubly unvalidated.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: A combined CSF-lipid + plasma-NfL progression model could stratify MCI by both metabolic and neurodegenerative risk, but requires a two-fluid cohort with longitudinal follow-up to demonstrate incremental value.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 2): Blood NfL change and CSF lipid markers predict the same endpoint from distinct compartments. Evaluation: 'The same single-centre' identity claim corrected to 'both single-centre' (P-1372's centre is unstated, so identity could not be asserted); otherwise honest ('doubly unvalidated').
complementary_findings.operator_caveat: Operator G4 required this caveat to appear as an explicit limitation in the manuscript text, not as a quality-flag footnote; the combined_insight / clinical_implication / human_evaluation_note above already carry it.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1375 (ADNI; Alzheimer's Research & Therapy 2024): ridge logistic regression on non-invasive baseline measures predicts future Abeta-positivity in Abeta-negative individuals - CSF-based 4-year conversion AUC 0.78, PET-based 0.68, plus MCI/dementia conversion AUC 0.76/0.89 on independent ADNI participants.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1380 (448 MCI: 331 discovery + 117 validation/ADNI; JAMA Neurology 2024, supplement): tau-PET predicts AD dementia in MCI with AUC 0.84 discovery / 0.79 validation; visual read lower (~0.69-0.72); supplement-only corpus file, main text confirmed from the published record.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: P-1375 and P-1380 predict two successive transitions on the AD continuum from different measurement axes: P-1375 forecasts amyloid conversion in Abeta-negative individuals using non-invasive clinical/CSF/PET measures, while P-1380 forecasts clinical dementia in already-MCI individuals using tau-PET; P-1375 does also apply the MCI-to-dementia endpoint - its CSF-based model predicted MCI-to-dementia conversion at AUC 0.89 on independent ADNI participants, and P-1380's validation arm is also ADNI MCI - so on that endpoint family the closest comparable figures are non-invasive AUC 0.89 (P-1375, ADNI) vs tau-PET 0.84 discovery / 0.79 ADNI validation (P-1380), although different samples and model inputs mean this is still not a head-to-head; P-1380 does not apply the amyloid-conversion endpoint, and the corpus contains no analysis of whether a non-invasive amyloid-conversion risk score combined with tau-PET improves MCI-to-dementia prediction, or whether the ordering of the two single-axis results (CSF-first 0.78 for amyloid conversion; tau-imaging 0.84 for dementia) holds when both are tested on one endpoint in one sample - the two figures are not rankable as-is because they predict different transitions; and the two arms are only partially ADNI-dependent (P-1380's discovery cohort is non-ADNI; only its validation is ADNI).
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: A staged risk algorithm - non-invasive amyloid-conversion score in Abeta-negative individuals, tau-PET once MCI is established - could allocate expensive tau imaging to those with highest non-invasive risk, but requires a single cohort testing both stages.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 2): Non-invasive amyloid-conversion prediction and tau-PET dementia prediction form a coherent sequential AD-continuum design. Evaluation: Cross-endpoint 'ranking' de-claimed (0.78 vs 0.84 predict different transitions, not rankable); ADNI-dependence narrowed to validation-only for P-1380 (its discovery is non-ADNI); supplement-only provenance disclosure retained.
complementary_findings.operator_caveat: Operator G4 required this caveat to appear as an explicit limitation in the manuscript text, not as a quality-flag footnote; the combined_insight / clinical_implication / human_evaluation_note above already carry it.
complementary_findings.audit_note_2026_09_14: Audit 2026-09-14 (CHALLENGE, major). (1) False clause 'neither study applies the other endpoint in the same cohort': P-1375 block line 192451 'CSF-based model predicted future MCI/dementia conversion in CN (AUC 0.76) and MCI (AUC 0.89) on independent participants' - P-1375 applies the MCI-to-dementia endpoint; P-1380 line 192918/192978 validation is ADNI MCI (AUC 0.79). Clause replaced with the block-supported comparison and the residual (combination) gap. (2) Venue invented: P-1375 block line 192526 'Alzheimer's Research & Therapy 16: 46, 2024' (record said Alzheimers Dement 2024). P-1380 'JAMA Neurology 2024, supplement' verified (line 192996). Status kept.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1378 (700 ADNI; Ann Geriatr Med Res 2024): serum isoleucine alone weak for AD (AUC 0.584) but improves CSF P-tau (Ile+P-tau AUC 0.808) and predicts MCI-to-AD conversion (HR 1.367, cutoff <=78.3 uM).
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1374 (174 subjects, two Shanghai cohorts; Front Cell Infect Microbiol 2024): faecal gut-microbiota metabolite panels diagnose MCI (7-metabolite AUC 0.7007) and predict 2-year MCI progression (6-metabolite AUC 0.7402), with Perillyl alcohol negatively correlated with all five serum AD biomarkers.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: P-1378 and P-1374 capture complementary metabolic compartments of the MCI-AD continuum: P-1378 reads host serum amino-acid metabolism (isoleucine, a BCAA convertible to glutamate/GABA) combined with CSF P-tau, while P-1374 reads gut-microbiota-derived faecal metabolites with their own diagnosis/progression models; neither study measures the other compartment, so the corpus has no cohort testing whether gut-metabolite panels add independent value to serum-BCAA + CSF-tau models, or whether Perillyl alcohol and low isoleucine mark overlapping or orthogonal protective/risk pathways; one cohort is ADNI (P-1378) and the other community-Chinese (P-1374), so cross-population transfer is untested.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: A dual-compartment metabolic panel (serum BCAA + faecal microbial metabolites) could widen non-invasive MCI screening, but requires a cohort sampling both serum and stool with longitudinal follow-up.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 2): Serum isoleucine and gut metabolites occupy different metabolic compartments but address related disease progression. Evaluation: Compartments, directions and modest AUCs (0.70-0.74) carried accurately; perillyl-alcohol/low-isoleucine content consistent with the stated cutoff; cross-population flagged.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1377 (157 subjects: 97 HC + 44 MCI + 16 AD, Hebei China; Sci Rep 2024): serum NfL + BNT detects MCI (AUC 0.732); IL-6 was elevated in MCI (P=0.013) with standalone AUC 0.648, on a par with NfL alone (0.646), but NfL + IL-6 did not improve over NfL alone; single-region, cross-sectional, no external validation.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1379 (36 studies, 11,059 participants; Front Aging Neurosci 2024): meta-analysis shows CSF sTREM2 elevated in AD (SMD 0.28) and MCI (SMD 0.30) vs controls, no AD-vs-MCI difference (SMD 0.09 n.s.), plasma sTREM2 borderline (SMD 0.42).
complementary_findings.combined_insight: P-1377 and P-1379 address the same question - do fluid markers of neurodegeneration/inflammation identify MCI? - from two non-overlapping marker families: P-1377 tests serum axonal (NfL) plus cytokine markers in a single community cohort, while P-1379 aggregates microglial-activation (sTREM2) evidence across 36 studies; neither study assays the other family, so the corpus lacks a head-to-head of axonal (NfL) vs microglial (sTREM2) MCI detection in one cohort, and the P-1377 cytokine result (IL-6 elevated in MCI, standalone AUC 0.648 equal to NfL alone, but no incremental value over NfL) sits alongside the pooled sTREM2 elevation in P-1379 (SMD 0.28-0.30); this is not a 'cytokine-null vs microglial-positive' contrast, since IL-6 did discriminate MCI on its own, so whether microglial rather than generic inflammatory markers carry the signal remains open; both are blood/CSF fluid axes that together could triangulate the neuroinflammatory contribution to MCI.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: A combined NfL + sTREM2 blood/CSF panel could separate axonal from microglial contributions to MCI detection and is directly testable in a single cohort.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 2): NfL evidence and sTREM2 meta-analysis triangulate complementary neuroinflammatory/degenerative axes. Evaluation: Interpretive move ('microglial, not generic inflammatory, markers carry the signal') properly hedged; the cytokine-null vs sTREM2-elevation contrast is a genuine cross-paper observation; small SMDs (0.28-0.42) implicitly bounded.
complementary_findings.audit_note_2026_09_14: Audit 2026-09-14 (UPHOLD_WITH_NOTES, major). (1) Venue copy-drift: P-1377 block line 192714 'Scientific Reports 14: 9072, 2024' (record said Front Aging Neurosci 2024, which is P-1379's venue, line 192902). (2) 'cytokine-null' mischaracterisation fixed per P-1377 line 192639: 'IL-6 highest in MCI (P=0.013) ... NfL alone AUC 0.646 ... IL-6 AUC 0.648 ... NfL + IL-6 did NOT improve over NfL alone'. sTREM2 SMDs per P-1379 line 192827. Status kept.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1381 (816 ADNI: 396 MCI + 228 CN + 192 AD; Front Aging Neurosci 2024): semi-supervised mixture-of-experts defines three MCI atrophy subtypes (MIN 26.0%, MID 34.6%, DIF 39.4%) with Acc 85.3% and distinct 24-month conversion (MIN 23, MID 52, DIF 64), APOE e4 >60% among converters.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1375 (ADNI; Alzheimer's Research & Therapy 2024): ridge logistic regression on non-invasive measures predicts future Abeta-positivity (CSF-based AUC 0.78, PET 0.68) and MCI/dementia conversion (AUC 0.76/0.89) in Abeta-negative individuals.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: P-1381 and P-1375 are two ADNI data-driven stratifications of MCI with complementary objectives: P-1381 defines discrete atrophy subtypes (semi-supervised mixture-of-experts structural subtyping with conversion-rate differences), while P-1375 builds a supervised risk score for future amyloid and clinical conversion from non-invasive measures; neither study uses the other output - P-1381 does not score amyloid-conversion risk within subtypes, and P-1375 does not condition on atrophy-subtype membership - so the corpus lacks an analysis of whether MOE subtype membership adds conversion-prediction value beyond a non-invasive risk score, or whether DIF-MCI enrichment concentrates in high-risk score strata; both are ADNI-only, making any combined stratification doubly dependent on a single database.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Combining structural subtype (MIN/MID/DIF) with a non-invasive conversion-risk score could refine ADNI MCI prognosis, but requires one cohort computing both and testing incremental value.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 1): Structural atrophy subtypes and supervised amyloid/clinical risk scores offer distinct, testable predictors within ADNI. Evaluation: Fidelity fix: 'unsupervised' corrected to 'semi-supervised mixture-of-experts' per the finding; ADNI double-dependence correctly acknowledged in-text.
complementary_findings.operator_caveat: Operator G4 required this caveat to appear as an explicit limitation in the manuscript text, not as a quality-flag footnote; the combined_insight / clinical_implication / human_evaluation_note above already carry it.
complementary_findings.audit_note_2026_09_14: Audit 2026-09-14 batch venue/year sweep (CF-288..CF-371): finding_b attributed P-1375 to 'Alzheimers Dement 2024'; the P-1375 block line 192526 reads 'Alzheimer's Research & Therapy 16: 46, 2024 (BMC/Springer, open access)' (year field line 192487 'Assigned: 2024'). Venue corrected; year already correct. P-1381 'Front Aging Neurosci 2024' verified (line 193090). No other change; status kept.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1384 (427 Ab+ MCI: 135 elenbecestat-trial placebo training + 115 lecanemab-trial placebo VC-1 + 177 ADNI-2/GO VC-2; Alz & Dementia DADM 2024): Bayesian logistic-lasso model adding baseline plasma pTau181 to clinical/cognitive tests raised 18-month clinical-decline AUROC to 0.742/0.753 (VC-1/VC-2) and 36-month MCI-to-AD progression AUROC to 0.79 (from 0.718), with time-to-progression HR improving 2.26 to 3.11.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1380 (448 MCI: prospective discovery n=331 + ADNI validation n=117; JAMA Neurology 2024): tau-PET quantification comparison - regional composite SUVR predicted AD-dementia with AUC 0.84 discovery / 0.79 validation, visual read lower (~0.69-0.72).
complementary_findings.combined_insight: P-1384 and P-1380 both predict MCI-to-AD dementia along the tau axis but measure different layers: P-1384 reads soluble plasma pTau181 (accessible, scalable blood assay) while P-1380 reads fibrillar tau-PET regional SUVR (molecular-imaging topography); neither cohort assays the other layer, so the corpus has no head-to-head or combined test of whether blood pTau181 and tau-PET are redundant or additive over clinical assessments in the same Ab+ MCI subjects - a question that matters because a blood-first tau work-up could defer PET to patients where blood-plus-clinical risk is intermediate.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: A staged tau work-up (plasma pTau181 first, tau-PET only where blood/clinical risk is intermediate) could preserve P-1380-level PET discrimination at P-1384-level scalability, but requires one cohort with both assays and identical 18/36-month endpoints.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 1): Plasma p-tau181 and tau-PET are a direct soluble-versus-fibrillar complement for progression prediction. Evaluation: Strong layer pairing (AUROC 0.742/0.753/0.79 vs 0.84/0.79); staged work-up properly hedged ('requires one cohort with identical endpoints').

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1386 (90 real-world memory-clinic patients, Milan; Ann Clin Transl Neurol 2024): cortical columnar diffusion metrics (AngleR, ParlPD, PerpPD+, MD, FA) tested as an ATN neurodegeneration (N) marker - whole-brain AngleR differentiated stable vs converting CSF A-T- MCI with AUC 0.8 and improved negative predictive value by +21.25%, in a group where 40% of A-T- MCI still progressed to AD or non-AD dementia.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1330 (ADNI; longitudinal): CSF amyloid-beta/tau AT(N) combined with MRI hippocampal volume and cortical thickness - A+T-(N+) mismatch MCI were milder and slower-declining than prodromal AD, with MTL-restricted cortical thinning and slower MTL volume loss tracking the mismatch group.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: P-1386 and P-1330 both interrogate the N axis of ATN but at different anatomical scales: P-1330's macrostructural hippocampal/MTL volumetry detects atrophy once established, whereas P-1386's intracortical columnar diffusion (AngleR) captures microstructural N change that reclassifies fluid-negative (A-T-) MCI who still progress - a group that P-1330-style macro markers under-serve; the corpus has no ATN-stratified cohort combining macro volumetry and microstructural columnar diffusion to test whether micro N change precedes and predicts macro atrophy.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Adding a microstructural MRI N marker to routine hippocampal volumetry could identify N-burden in A-T- MCI before macro atrophy is visible; needs one cohort with both MRI measures plus CSF AT.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 1): Diffusion microstructure and macrostructural atrophy probe different N-axis scales with a concrete integration gap. Evaluation: Over-tight 'exactly the group' clause softened: P-1386's progressors are A-T- while P-1330's mismatch group is A+T-(N+) - two different ATN strata.
complementary_findings.operator_caveat: Operator G4 required this caveat to appear as an explicit limitation in the manuscript text, not as a quality-flag footnote; the combined_insight / clinical_implication / human_evaluation_note above already carry it.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1387 (415 de novo drug-naive PD, PPMI, 5-year follow-up; CNS Neurosci Ther 2024): latent class trajectory model of MDS-UPDRS-III motor scores identified severe-progressive (66.99%) vs mild-remitting (33.01%) classes; the severe-progressive class had higher incident-MCI risk, HR 1.559 (95% CI 1.147-2.119) after propensity-score matching.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-997 (PPMI, 33 international sites, 2011-2017; longitudinal): linear mixed-effects and GEE models of neuropsychiatric symptoms (depression, anxiety, apathy, psychosis, ICDs) - depression and anxiety were associated with progressive decline across all four cognitive domains and NPS (except ICDs) increased MCI occurrence.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: P-1387 and P-997 are both PPMI de novo PD longitudinal trajectory studies with cognitive/MCI outcomes, but each models a different axis - P-1387 motor (UPDRS-III, nigrostriatal) and P-997 neuropsychiatric (depression/anxiety, limbic non-dopaminergic) - and neither includes the other axis; the corpus therefore lacks a joint motor+NPS trajectory model testing whether severe motor and depressive/anxious trajectories mark independent or convergent MCI-risk pathways in early PD.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: A dual-axis (motor + NPS) trajectory screen in de novo PD could stratify MCI risk beyond either axis alone; testable in PPMI with a joint LCTM over MDS-UPDRS-III and NPS time series.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 1): Independent PPMI trajectories provide complementary motor and neuropsychiatric dimensions of PD-MCI risk. Evaluation: CAVEAT: both papers analyse the same PPMI de-novo cohort - non-independence must be flagged despite the 'testable in PPMI' framing; P-997's finding carries no effect sizes.
complementary_findings.operator_caveat: Operator G4 required this caveat to appear as an explicit limitation in the manuscript text, not as a quality-flag footnote; the combined_insight / clinical_implication / human_evaluation_note above already carry it.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1390 (1004 SCD/MCI: 612 ADNI development + 392 BioFINDER-1 replication; Alz & Dementia 2024): two-step logistic-regression algorithm from brief cognitive tests (TMT, fluency, MMSE, recall) plus 1-year change scores predicted 4-year all-cause dementia - step-1 AUC 0.91 / step-2 AUC 0.92 in ADNI (PPV 85.8%, NPV 92.2%) and replication AUC 0.86 in BioFINDER-1.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1365 (Swedish BioFINDER-1, SCD/MCI; structural MRI): OPLS severity index from FreeSurfer cortical thickness and subcortical volumes (10-fold CV, age detrending, minimal-atrophy removal) staged SCD/MCI conversion risk - AUC 0.72 aMCI-trained vs 0.57 dementia-trained (P=0.037), sens 72.3%, spec 60.9%.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: P-1390 and P-1365 are both validated on the same Swedish BioFINDER-1 SCD/MCI population yet use orthogonal predictors - P-1390 brief cognitive tests with 1-year change (no biomarkers) and P-1365 a structural-MRI severity index - and no corpus paper tests the combination; P-1390's intermediate-risk tier (the group requiring a second-year assessment) is precisely where P-1365's MRI index could add independent stratification, so the corpus lacks a cognitive+MRI two-step SCD/MCI model with both layers measured on one cohort.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Adding a single structural MRI to the cognitive two-step screen for intermediate-risk patients could add independent stratification value without scanning everyone; needs a joint model in one SCD/MCI cohort.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 1): Independently validated cognitive two-step screening plus MRI severity creates a specific additive-stratification test. Evaluation: Unverifiable '62.5% PPV in BioFINDER-1' removed from the implication (appears in neither finding); shared BioFINDER-1 population makes this a shared-cohort orthogonal-predictor design - a positive for feasibility, not independent samples.
complementary_findings.operator_caveat: Operator G4 required this caveat to appear as an explicit limitation in the manuscript text, not as a quality-flag footnote; the combined_insight / clinical_implication / human_evaluation_note above already carry it.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1388 (803 ADNI plasma after QC: 165 CN/272 EMCI/217 LMCI/149 AD; Alz & Dementia 2024): small-RNA sequencing of the total plasma microRNAome with ML signatures - LMCI-to-AD conversion AUC 0.75 (3-miRNA) and 0.79 (miR-532-3p/miR-1306-3p + ADAS-cog13), outperforming CSF biomarkers (0.60-0.62) and MMSE (AUC 0.5).
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1323 (Shanghai Mental Health Center cohort, China, 2022-2024; n=29: 10 AD, 9 MCI, 10 NC; single-centre, discovery-only, ROC-based with no independent or longitudinal validation and acknowledged over-fitting risk; RSC Advances 2025): plasma exosomal miRNA by small-RNA sequencing - cross-sectional ROC AUC >0.9 (miR-210-3p, miR-151-3p) for NC/MCI/AD discrimination with further miRNAs >0.8.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: P-1388 and P-1323 both profile circulating miRNA by small-RNA sequencing but on different fractions - P-1388 the total plasma microRNAome in a Western ADNI cohort and P-1323 vesicle-enclosed exosomal miRNAs in a Chinese cohort - and the ~0.15-0.2 higher AUCs in P-1323 are not commensurable with P-1388's headline figures: P-1323's >0.9 are cross-sectional NC/MCI/AD diagnostic AUCs from n=29 (9 MCI) with no validation and acknowledged over-fitting risk, whereas P-1388's 0.75/0.79 are longitudinal LMCI-to-AD conversion AUCs from 803 participants (its cross-sectional LMCI-detection AUCs were 0.71-0.75), so the gap most plausibly reflects the tiny discovery-only sample and the cross-task comparison, with exosomal enrichment, cohort ethnicity or stage mix as untested secondary explanations; no corpus study profiles total and exosomal fractions from the same blood draws, leaving fraction-specificity and cross-population transfer of MCI/AD miRNA signals untested.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Head-to-head total-vs-exosomal miRNA profiling in one multi-ethnic MCI cohort would establish whether vesicle enrichment genuinely improves discrimination and whether ADNI conversion signatures transfer across populations; needed before either panel is standardised.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 2): Total plasma miRNAome vs exosomal fraction is a clean biological fraction question, though population transfer is unresolved. Evaluation: Best-practice alternative-explanation listing (exosomal enrichment vs cohort ethnicity vs stage mix); P-1323 description drift vs its CF-314 use noted.
complementary_findings.audit_note_2026_09_14: Audit 2026-09-14 (CHALLENGE, major). finding_b suppressed P-1323's sample size and design: block line 187584 '29 participants (10 AD, 9 MCI, 10 normal cognition)', line 187593 'Very small cohort (n=29) ... ROC-based evaluation without independent validation; cross-sectional design', line 187617 'ROC-based with possible over-fitting', line 187632 'T1 Diagnostic/classification (NC vs MCI vs AD discrimination via ROC)', venue line 187662 'RSC Advances 15: 23670-23680, 2025'. Cross-task AUC comparison flagged per P-1388 line 193673 (LMCI detection AUC 0.71-0.74/0.75; LMCI-to-AD conversion 0.75, 0.79 with ADAS-cog13). Cohort window 2022-2024 verified (line 187644). Status kept.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1397 (Taipei VGH longitudinal cohort 2012-2022, n=116: 39 S-MCI/28 P-MCI/49 AD; Alzheimers Res Ther 2025): peripheral WBC RNA-seq with DESeq2 + Lasso/SVM/RF selection - 8-mRNA signature separates progressive from stable MCI at AUC 0.93 (accuracy 0.87, 5-fold CV), with gender-specific transcriptomic profiles.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1401 (NCGG Biobank Japan, n=1227: 260 CN/543 MCI/424 AD; Sci Rep 2025): whole-blood RNA-seq with edgeR + GSEA + immune-cell deconvolution - stage-specific architecture: ribosome genes dysregulated at the MCI transition (ribosome pathway FDR 8.49e-7 in CN-MCI), immune/cell-cycle programmes dominate by AD stage.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: P-1397 and P-1401 both read peripheral blood transcriptomics across the MCI-to-AD arc but answer different questions with different designs, and together they bracket the molecular timeline: P-1401 cross-sectional N=1227 shows WHICH programmes (ribosome at MCI, immune/cell-cycle at AD) are active at each stage, while P-1397 longitudinal n=116 shows a small 8-gene blood panel can predict progressive from stable MCI - yet neither study tests whether P-1397 predictive mRNAs sit inside P-1401 stage-active ribosome/immune modules, so the bridge from cross-sectional stage signatures to prospective individual prediction is asserted by the field but never joined in one cohort.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: A single cohort scored with both designs would show whether stage-active programmes (ribosome, immune) carry the prospective conversion signal, letting an early cheap blood draw stratify who needs amyloid testing; until then the two halves of the blood-transcriptomics story remain disconnected.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 2): Large transcriptomic stage architecture plus longitudinal predictive signature provides a cross-sectional-to-prognostic bridge. Evaluation: Unanchored '3 years out' removed (no follow-up duration exists in P-1397's finding); small-n/overfitting risk (39 S-MCI/28 P-MCI with Lasso/SVM/RF selection) noted.
complementary_findings.operator_caveat: Operator G4 required this caveat to appear as an explicit limitation in the manuscript text, not as a quality-flag footnote; the combined_insight / clinical_implication / human_evaluation_note above already carry it.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1403 (PREVENT-AD, n=228 CU with 62 progressors; Alzheimers & Dementia 2025): plasma p-tau217 (Simoa) with A-beta42/40 - A+T+ plasma HR 7.81 (95% CI 3.92-15.59) for 10-year CU-to-MCI progression; adding amyloid to tau did not improve prediction.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1343 (Swedish flutemetamol PET trial cohort NCT01028053, n=110 amnestic MCI): plasma p-tau217 + hippocampal volume + mPACC + APOE model AUC 0.89 for MCI-to-AD progression (p-tau217 alone 0.84); parsimonious p-tau217 + mPACC AUC 0.87.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Both papers score the same plasma p-tau217 analyte on opposite sides of the clinical threshold: P-1403 shows tau alone carries near-maximal prognostic information before any diagnosis exists (amyloid adds nothing to the hazard model), while P-1343 shows that once MCI is established the best model re-imports brain-volume and cognitive-envelope features (mPACC, hippocampus) that p-tau217 alone lacks - together they imply the informative covariate set inverts at conversion proximity, a stage-dependent add-on structure no single-cohort study in the corpus tests directly.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Blood-only p-tau217 screening is defensible for preclinical trial enrichment, but a symptomatic-clinic prognostic panel should budget for imaging or neuropsych measures; sequencing biomarker add-ons by disease stage rather than stacking everything at once would use the same assay budget more efficiently.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 1): Same p-tau217 analyte is tested before diagnosis and within MCI, exposing stage-dependent predictive roles. Evaluation: Cohort enrichment (PREVENT-AD at-risk vs trial aMCI) is a competing explanation for the covariate-set inversion, not only disease stage - noted.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1404 (Rush RROS post-mortem cohort, n=39 PCC samples): brain-tissue small-RNA-seq splits AD vs MCI vs resilience groups - let-7d (p=0.004) and miR-211 (p=0.003) differential expression; miR-4634 correlates with Braak stage (r=-0.47); TarBase/STRING pathway interactomes built.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1388 (ADNI, n=803 plasma): circulating microRNAome + ADAS-Cog13 predicts LMCI-to-AD conversion (AUC 0.79; miR-532-3p/miR-1306-3p + cognition), blood miRNA outperforming CSF markers for the same endpoint.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: The two studies read the same microRNA regulatory layer from opposite tissue compartments - P-1404 shows which miRNA programmes differ in the brain regions that bear AD pathology, P-1388 shows which circulating miRNAs track imminent conversion in living patients - but no corpus study tests whether P-1388 plasma discriminators (miR-532-3p, miR-1306-3p) are expressed in P-1404 resilience- or stage-associated brain sets, so the tissue origin of the blood conversion signal (neuronal, glial, or peripheral) is unattributed and the compartment bridge between post-mortem mechanism and clinical prediction is missing.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: A tissue-mapped blood miRNA signature would tell clinicians whether a positive plasma screen reflects central pathology or systemic state, and would anchor the P-1388 predictor to a mechanism the P-1404 post-mortem data already measure.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 2): Brain-tissue and plasma miRNA create a direct tissue-source continuity question, but post-mortem evidence limits strength. Evaluation: Small-n caveat (39 post-mortem samples) noted.

complementary_findings.finding_a: P-1413 (laser-capture BA9 layer III pyramidal neurons, post-mortem n=20: 8 NCI, 5 MCI, 7 AD; Alzheimer's & Dementia 2025): DEGs rose from 1306 (prodromal, MCI vs NCI) to 2505 (progression, AD vs MCI) to 3259 (frank AD); 196 DEGs were shared across all comparisons, and the 634 DEGs shared between the prodromal and progression comparisons were 78.9% directionally divergent (500 of 634) whereas progression-vs-frank-AD shared DEGs were mostly convergent (29 of 1077 divergent); synaptogenesis signalling was downregulated at all stages, mitochondrial dysfunction flipped from downregulated (prodromal) to upregulated (later stages), and Reactome mapping showed upregulated pathways dominating the prodromal stage but downregulated pathways dominating progression and frank AD.
complementary_findings.finding_b: P-1418 (in-silico reanalysis of GSE63060 whole-blood transcriptomes, n=329: AD + MCI + healthy controls; International Journal of Molecular Sciences 2025): 2186 shared same-direction DEGs from MCI through AD, with ribosomal formation/biogenesis and RNA-splicing/translation ontologies dysregulated consistently in both MCI and AD.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: The two transcriptomic layers bracket the disease from opposite tissue compartments with opposite conservation patterns: in vulnerable BA9 pyramidal neurons the prodromal-to-progressive transition is defined by DIRECTIONAL DIVERGENCE of shared DEGs (78.9% of the 634 prodromal/progression shared DEGs flip dysregulation sign as MCI becomes AD), while in whole blood the MCI-to-AD span is defined by 2186 same-direction DEGs with no flip. The reported pathway content also differs: the P-1413 block reports synaptogenesis, mitochondrial-dysfunction and Reactome pathway shifts and reports no ribosome, splicing or translation-machinery finding, so the blood ribosome/splicing signature of P-1418 has no reported neuronal counterpart within this pair. No corpus study tests whether the blood's directionally stable ribosome/splicing signature tracks the neuron-side sign-flip programmes or the stable pathways, so the peripheral signal's central correspondence is unattributed.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: A blood draw could in principle monitor a central transcriptional stage signature only if the peripheral-vs-neuronal correspondence is mapped; until then, blood transcriptomic staging (P-1418) and post-mortem neuronal staging (P-1413) cannot calibrate each other and cross-tissue biomarker translation remains guesswork.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 2): Brain versus blood transcriptomics gives a meaningful compartment complement, although directional differences complicate interpretation. Evaluation: Contamination fix: the 'ribosome/splicing in P-1413' overlap claim removed (P-1413's finding lists synaptic-vesicle-cycle and OXPHOS only); mojibake repaired; n=20 post-mortem (5 MCI) and GSE63060 secondary-data provenance noted.
complementary_findings.operator_caveat: Operator G4 required this caveat to appear as an explicit limitation in the manuscript text, not as a quality-flag footnote; the combined_insight / clinical_implication / human_evaluation_note above already carry it.

complementary_findings.finding_a: Supplies the second CHANNEL of the identical elicitation task (video-annotated co-speech gesture, 52 participants, five groups, Barcelona, Spanish) where the whole channel is null, and independently replicates one of P-748's four aggregate nulls (type-token ratio) in a different language. It has no fine-grained grammatical arm, so on its own it reads as the picture-description task being uninformative in general rather than informative at exactly one level of one channel.
complementary_findings.finding_b: Supplies the within-study dissociation of MEASUREMENT LEVELS on 105 pooled English transcripts (35 HC / 35 MCI / 35 AD): four generic linguistic measures null, hypothesis-selected grammatical variables moderate-to-large. It has no gestural arm, so on its own it leaves the non-verbal channel of the same task untested and plausibly informative.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Across the two corpus studies of the picture-description paradigm (105-particle English pooled cohort; 52-participant Spanish five-group cohort), the MCI signal is confined to ONE channel and ONE level of description: P-748 shows the aggregate output measures that dominate automated speech analysis (utterance count, MLU, type-token ratio, formal error rate) are all null on the same 105 transcripts where hypothesis-selected fine-grained grammatical variables return moderate-to-large effects (adjunct clause ratio, MCI d .93), and P-747 shows the co-speech gestural channel of the same elicitation task yields no significant discriminator in any of fourteen gestural variables and does not correlate with MMSE or study group, with the type-token-ratio null replicating across both languages and cohorts. Because the gestural arm is underpowered (10-11 participants per group, trends at p 0.060-0.088), its null is corpus evidence of absence of a DETECTABLE signal, not a demonstrated absence; and the grammatical channel's corrected group difference (d .93) is capped by provenance - all 35 controls were recruited from UK sources while patients came from Pittsburgh - so it is a corrected group difference, never a detection statistic.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Two decisions in a memory-clinic or research screening protocol built on picture description. First, do not add video capture and gesture annotation: on the only corpus evidence available the gestural channel of this task separates no group and does not even track MMSE, so the added recording burden, annotation labour and analyst time buy nothing. Second, and the patient-facing risk: a speech pipeline scored on the standard aggregate feature set (utterance counts, MLU, type-token ratio, error rates) is measuring the level of description where MCI and controls do not differ, so a negative result from such a pipeline carries no information about MCI status and must not be communicated as reassurance to a patient presenting with cognitive complaints. Where connected speech is used at all, the informative measures in this evidence are the fine-grained referential-grammar variables.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 1): Same picture-description paradigm; aggregate speech measures are null while fine-grained grammar/gesture separates signal from non-signal. Evaluation: WEAKENED verdict applied before promotion: provenance confound (all 35 controls from UK sources, patients from Pittsburgh) surfaced in-insight; gestural null correctly bounded as absence of a detectable signal (10-11/group, trends p 0.060-0.088), not demonstrated absence.
complementary_findings.operator_caveat: Operator G4 required this caveat to appear as an explicit limitation in the manuscript text, not as a quality-flag footnote; the combined_insight / clinical_implication / human_evaluation_note above already carry it.

complementary_findings.finding_a: The independent arm that changes the reading. Different language (Japanese), different cohort (two hospitals), different feature family (17 non-linguistic acoustic voice-quality features from a sustained /a/ and repeated /pa-ta-ka/, no linguistic content, group-level cross-validation), and a different reporting choice: the MCI-specific number is absent while the headline comes from a contrast that folds MCI into the impaired class. Read alone, its AUC 0.95 reads as a screening success.
complementary_findings.finding_b: The measured arm. It runs the MCI-vs-HC contrast explicitly and reports it as the weakest of three, alongside the structural and cognitive correlates that make the speech-timing marker credible as a construct. Read alone, its 63% reads as a small-sample limitation of one exploratory classifier.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: The headline performance of a non-lexical speech screen is set by how much dementia its positive class contains, and the MCI-specific contrast - the one that defines the early-detection use case - is either the weakest number in the paper or is never computed. P-938 (Dublin, conversational speech timing, N=80) is the only one of the two that reports an MCI-specific figure, and it is the lowest of its three contrasts: MCI-HC 63% against AD-HC 74% and 82.47-84.17% three-class. P-884 (Japan, voice-quality acoustics from two fixed phrases, N=150) carries the pattern one step further: its headline is HE vs (MCI + AD/D) accuracy 93.8% and best one-vs-rest AUC 0.95, the contrast in which MCI is POOLED with dementia, while AD/D vs (HE + MCI) falls to 69.7% and the MCI-vs-others discrimination is not reported at all. Jointly, across two languages, two feature families and two independent cohorts, the non-lexical speech signal behaves as a dementia-severity signal rather than an MCI signal.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: The decision is whether to adopt a voice or speech-timing screen for MCI case-finding in primary care, telemedicine or community screening on the strength of its published headline. On this pair's evidence the headline is produced by contrasts that either isolate healthy from impaired (P-884, 93.8%) or include dementia cases (P-938, 82-84% three-class; 74% AD-HC), while the MCI contrast that defines the pathway is 63% in the one paper that reports it and is absent in the other. The risk to the population served is concrete: positive flags from such a screen would be dominated by people already at dementia severity, who are not the group an early-detection pathway is built for, and the tool's behaviour on true MCI cases is unquantified in one paper and barely above the level of a coin in the other. Before deployment, an MCI-specific contrast should be a reporting requirement, not an optional per-class breakdown.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 1): Two independent cohorts show headline speech accuracy is largely dementia-severity weighted, not MCI-specific. Evaluation: All lenses pass with 6/6 verbatim quotes; the contrast ladder (93.8% with MCI pooled into the impaired class vs 69.7% when MCI moves to the other side) is genuinely pair-level; P-884's N=150 appears only in the insight - noted.

complementary_findings.finding_a: Supplies the language-free perceptual channel and, critically, the INTERVAL-RANGE SPECIFICITY that turns 'slower' into a localised claim: sub-second discrimination is biased while supra-second is spared and reaction times show nothing, so the deficit is not general slowing or reduced effort. It is purely behavioural - no speech sample, no brain measure - and its own improvement section asks for exactly the imaging it lacks.
complementary_findings.finding_b: Supplies the production channel in connected speech together with the structural correlate P-887 asks for, in an independent English-speaking cohort with MRI: speech-timing slowing co-occurring with frontal, temporal and cerebellar volume reduction. It contains no non-linguistic control task, so alone it cannot separate a language-borne explanation of speech slowing from a domain-general timing one.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: At the same disease stage, MCI patients are impaired in temporal processing on BOTH the language-free perceptual side and the speech-production side, and each paper holds precisely the measurement the other names as missing. P-887 (DZNE Magdeburg, 10 aMCI / 30 controls) shows a duration-discrimination bias that is specific to SUB-SECOND intervals (sub-second t(9.0) = 2.4, p = 0.019; supra-second t(10.5) = 1.1, p = 0.15, not significant) using a non-linguistic acoustic task, attributes it to cerebellar/basal-ganglia timing circuits, and has no imaging with which to test that attribution. P-938 (Dublin, N=80) shows MCI and mild-to-moderate AD speech is slowed in rate and turn-taking and that this slowing tracks volume reduction in frontal, temporal AND cerebellar areas, but runs no non-linguistic timing task and so cannot say whether its speech slowing is a language phenomenon or a general timing one. Jointly: conversational speech slowing in MCI is not established as a language-specific sign, because the same population is biased on a sub-second timing task that contains no language at all, and the structural correlate reported for the speech measure overlaps the circuits nominated for the perceptual one.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Two decisions. First, interpretation: a slow conversational speech-timing profile must not be reported to a patient or written into a memory-clinic letter as evidence of LANGUAGE decline, because the same population is biased on a sub-second duration task with no language in it. Second, expected yield from combination: the corpus default is that adding modalities adds information (VF-02). If the speech-timing marker and a non-linguistic timing task are two windows on one temporal deficit, they are not independent evidence, and a fused speech-plus-timing panel should not be costed as though they were. The population where this bites hardest is the one P-938's own task excludes - people who cannot supply scoreable connected speech in the testing language (non-native speakers, low literacy, dysarthria) or who have no caregiver interlocutor for a collaborative referencing task.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 2): Perceptual timing and speech-production timing are complementary directions on the same temporal-processing construct; one arm is small. Evaluation: Sub-second contrast is one-tailed (t(9.0)=2.4, p=0.019; two-tailed ~0.038) - unstated limitation noted; the negative claim is correctly scoped ('not established as language-specific').

complementary_findings.finding_a: Establishes the field-level baseline of what MEASURED retinal parameters deliver at the MCI stage - a small pooled effect for the best-supported marker, no pooled sensitivity, specificity or SROC, and the authors' own verdict on clinical readiness - and states that diagnostic-test-accuracy studies are the missing design.
complementary_findings.finding_b: ADDS the missing design and, within it, the attribution test P-830 could not run: two image representations compared inside one dataset, with the vessel-segmented representation - the one that corresponds to the vascular measurements P-830 pools - performing significantly WORSE than the raw photograph, while the paper still markets the result as vascular-feature screening.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: The retinal information that yields an MCI-level accuracy figure is not carried by the retinal parameters the field has been pooling. P-830 pools hand-measured retinal structural, vascular and electrophysiological parameters across 126 studies and obtains only small group-level effects at the MCI stage (peripapillary RNFL SMD -0.324) with no diagnostic accuracy of any kind, concluding the markers are not yet translatable. P-952 supplies precisely the missing design - a fundus-image classifier reaching validation AUC 0.87 for MCI - but obtains it from texture descriptors of the WHOLE unsegmented photograph, and finds that isolating the vasculature, the representation P-830's vascular rows are built from, significantly DEGRADES performance (original beats segmentation, p=0.0388). Taken together the two records show that the pooled retinal-parameter evidence base and the image-level accuracy evidence are not the same evidence: the parameter literature does not explain the AUC, and the AUC does not rescue the parameter literature.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: This bears on whether an older adult attending a community or primary-care eye clinic should be referred for cognitive workup on the strength of a retinal finding, and on which retinal evidence a screening programme may cite for that referral. The pooled measured-parameter evidence (best supported marker, peripapillary RNFL, SMD -0.324 with no accuracy data) cannot support an individual referral decision - P-830 says so in its own words - and the one available accuracy figure comes from a whole-image classifier that does not use the vascular measurements at all. So a fundus-image-classifier screening programme and an OCT-layer-thickness screening programme are two different programmes needing two different validations, and a clinician must not read an image-model AUC as confirmation of the retinal-microvascular reasoning used to justify the referral. The population most exposed is exactly the one both papers target: community-dwelling older adults with no memory complaint being screened opportunistically at an eye examination, where a false referral carries the cost of an unnecessary dementia workup.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 1): Meta-analytic retinal parameter weakness plus whole-image classifier directly exposes which representation carries signal. Evaluation: '126 studies' in the insight lacks a quote anchor; the 10-fold CV over 332 images from 86 subjects with no stated subject-level split is the single fact a reviewer most needs - flagged.

complementary_findings.finding_a: The clean negative arm. A fully passive protocol - free viewing of 32 photographs with no instruction, no response and no imposed load - yields no aMCI-versus-HC separation on any of nine parameters, and the paper's own open-problems section states it cannot adjudicate between intact scanning and insufficient power.
complementary_findings.finding_b: ADDS the missing contrast, inside one sample: a low-demand central-field detection task and a peripheral divided-attention task administered to the same 74 participants, with the low-demand arm null and the loaded arm at Cohen's d -1.17 and AUC 0.841. That within-study dissociation supplies an alternative explanation for P-686's null that P-686 had no arm to test.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: The frontier's strongest negative result on eye-movement MCI screening is a null about the PROTOCOL, not about the channel. P-686 recorded nine eye-movement parameters during passive free viewing of real-world photographs in 94 people and not one separated amnestic MCI from healthy controls - but the null cannot be read as a channel null, because the paper cannot distinguish it from underpowering (effect sizes computed only for significant outcomes, every aMCI-versus-HC cell blank, no equivalence test) and because P-1163 shows the same channel discriminating at AUC 0.841 under a different paradigm in an independent cohort - with P-1163's own low-demand central task null in the SAME 74 participants isolating the within-study contrast to the task, not the channel. Across two independent cohorts, countries and paradigms, the MCI oculomotor signal has been demonstrated only under speeded, scoreable-response paradigms (peripheral UFOV; interleaved prosaccade/antisaccade with Go/No-go) and never under passive free viewing; which property of the loaded paradigms carries the signal (attentional load, divided attention, or simply the presence of a speeded scoreable error) is not identified by the available evidence. P-686's null therefore bounds rather than refutes eye-movement MCI screening, and passive free viewing is the one paradigm under which the theme reports a null.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: This bears directly on which eye-tracking protocol a memory clinic or a screening programme should procure and administer. The cheapest and most patient-tolerable option - passive free viewing of images, requiring no instruction, no motor response and no language, and therefore the natural choice for low-education, non-native-speaking or frail patients - is the one carrying a documented MCI-stage null. A triage protocol choosing a low-burden ocular screen should not rely on passive free viewing, the one paradigm with a documented MCI-stage null; if eye tracking is used, paradigms imposing divided-attention or inhibitory demand (peripheral UFOV, antisaccade-type paradigms) are the only ones with demonstrated separation - a cross-study reading, since the loaded and passive paradigms differ in stimuli, dependent measures, hardware, country and MCI criteria (clinical Albert/Petersen vs MoCA-J/MMSE-J screening cut-offs). The second half of the implication protects the channel rather than the protocol: P-686 must not be cited as evidence that eye tracking fails in MCI, because the only load-free arm ever tested in the same participants as a loaded one (P-1163's central task) also failed. Population at risk of the wrong decision: clinics selecting a low-burden ocular screen for exactly the education- and language-diverse older adults these devices are marketed for.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 1): Passive-null versus loaded-positive eye tracking provides a strong protocol-level dissociation. Evaluation: WEAKENED verdict applied before promotion: prescription made conditional and the case-definition mismatch (clinical Albert/Petersen vs MoCA-J/MMSE-J screening cut-offs) surfaced in the implication; P-686's underpowering ambiguity stays in-insight.

complementary_findings.finding_a: The observational arm. Places an unambiguously social exposure (years of education) as the exposure and 16S-derived gut microbiome composition as the mediator, in a formal causal-mediation effect decomposition (natural direct effect, controlled direct effect, proportion eliminated, 5,000-bootstrap standard errors) on 258 LUXPARK participants aged 50+. It establishes BOTH halves of the mediation premise - education is associated with MCI, and education is associated with microbiome composition -
complementary_findings.finding_b: The interventional arm, supplying the manipulation P-856 cannot perform. A randomised, assessor-blinded 12-week trial in 40 amnestic-MCI patients with faecal shotgun metagenomics, untargeted serum metabolomics and resting-state fMRI measured on the same participants alongside ADAS-Cog. The cognitive layer moves by more than the stated minimal clinically important difference, the microbiome does not move at the diversity level, and the formal mediation test for the full chain returns null.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: The gut microbiome is UNEVIDENCED as the causal intermediary for MCI from both of the two directions in which this corpus has tested it. Observationally (P-856, LUXPARK, n=258), an exposure that does predict MCI - years of education, natural direct effect OR 0.35 (0.15-0.81) - transmits none of its detectable effect through the microbiome, with the formal ldm/permanovaFL mediation tests null. Experimentally (P-760, Chengdu, n=40 randomised), an intervention that does move cognition beyond the stated minimal clinically important difference (ADAS-Cog -5.66, -6.98 to -4.35) produces no diversity-level microbiome change and a null mediation test for the gut-to-metabolite-to-brain-to-cognition chain the trial was titled to demonstrate. Neither null is decisive alone: P-856 cannot exclude a manipulable microbiome, and P-760's null is plausibly a 40-patient power failure, which its own discussion concedes. Together they show that the two available test directions both came back empty on the same layer (composition/diversity), so the corpus currently contains no affirmative evidence that gut composition carries MCI risk or treatment response - not evidence that it cannot.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Bears on a real and increasingly common decision: whether to recommend, or to spend on, a microbiome-directed product (probiotic, prebiotic or targeted dietary modification) for an older adult who has MCI or who is at elevated risk of it through low education. Neither corpus study tested such a product - the randomised arm tested acupuncture against a waitlist control, and the observational MCI sample was MoCA-screened within a Parkinson's cohort - so the pair bounds the rationale offered for these products rather than directly evaluating one. The two corpus studies that formally tested the mediating step - one observational, one randomised - both found it empty, so the rationale usually offered for these products is unsupported here. It also bears on how a clinician explains a cognitive gain: a patient in the acupuncture arm who improved by more than the minimal clinically important difference did so without a measurable diversity-level microbiome change, so attributing that gain to a gut mechanism asserts a chain the trial's own mediation analysis rejected.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 2): Independent null mediation tests on the gut-microbiome layer are informative boundary evidence despite small trial size. Evaluation: WEAKENED verdict applied before promotion: product-decision framing bounded (neither study tested a microbiome-directed product - the RCT arm was acupuncture vs waitlist; the observational MCI sample was MoCA-screened within a Parkinson's cohort); the complementary-nulls core is genuine.

complementary_findings.finding_a: Supplies verified biochemical target engagement with no cognitive readout. A PROSPERO-registered Bayesian random-effects network meta-analysis of 15 folate / vitamin-B12 trials from five countries, published 2006-2021, with a 10-study homocysteine network. It is the only place in this pack where a nutrient's biochemical target is shown to move with pooled, interval-estimated evidence - and it is also the place where the corresponding cognitive estimate is explicitly stated to be unobtainable.
complementary_findings.finding_b: Supplies the clean randomised cognitive null with no verified target engagement. A multisite, double-blind, placebo-controlled four-arm 24-month trial in institutionalised amnestic-MCI and mild-to-moderate AD patients that measured erythrocyte membrane fatty acids as the exposure - the measurement that shows the intervention was not delivered as intended, and the reason its own null cannot be attributed to the nutrient.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: In nutrient-supplementation research on MCI, demonstrated biochemical target engagement and an interpretable cognitive estimate do not occur in the same study. P-713 pools 15 randomised trials (4,072 participants) and demonstrates target engagement for the methyl nutrients - serum homocysteine credibly reduced by 2.06 to 4.23 units by all three regimens, every credible interval excluding zero - but its own limitations state that heterogeneous cognitive scales made any quantitative analysis of cognitive outcomes impossible, so the cognitive conclusion rests on a five-of-nine vote count. P-740 supplies the mirror image: a 24-month, four-arm, double-blind omega-3 trial (n = 163) that produces clean randomised nulls on every clinical endpoint (adjusted p: ADAS-cog 0.42, MMSE 0.11, QOL 0.54, ADCS-ADL 0.44, GDS 0.57) in which target engagement demonstrably failed - erythrocyte n-3 fell rather than rose in the supplemented arms and no fatty-acid change differed between arms (adjusted p 0.60 to 0.95 across all twelve rows), with no adherence figure, interim biomarker or per-protocol analysis reported.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Bears on an ordinary memory-clinic prescribing decision: whether to start folate/B12 or omega-3 in a patient newly diagnosed with MCI, and what to tell that patient. Homocysteine lowering - the biochemical rationale routinely quoted to patients and the only pooled effect either paper produces - has never been paired with a pooled cognitive estimate, so it supports no cognitive promise. The 24-month omega-3 null cannot be used to counsel against omega-3 either, because achieved erythrocyte n-3 fell under supplementation and no fatty-acid change separated the arms. The pair also withdraws the usual fallback reassurance that a higher dose would have worked: in the one trial where achieved exposure was actually measured, assigned dose and achieved exposure moved in opposite directions.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 2): Target engagement and cognitive-null evidence reveal a genuine design mismatch, but interventions are different nutrients. Evaluation: Cleanest design-level claim in the batch (engagement without cognitive estimability vs clean randomised null with failed engagement); '4,072 participants' lacks a quote anchor - noted; the molecules differ, so strict shared-construct readings could reject.

complementary_findings.finding_a: Supplies the cross-sectional discrimination arm: compartment-specific periventricular WMH volumetry plus fasting plasma homocysteine, each independently associated with PD-MCI after adjustment for motor severity, in 387 de novo PD patients (Chongqing, China). It measures no amyloid, tau or neurofilament marker at all and names their addition as an open problem, so on its own it cannot exclude that PWMH/Hcy are indexing concurrent AD pathology.
complementary_findings.finding_b: Supplies the missing biomarker arm from an independent cohort (University of Perugia, Italy; 48 PD-MCI, 40 PD-CN, 25 MCI-AD, 44 neurological controls): a ten-marker CSF panel spanning amyloid, tau, neurodegeneration, synaptic and glial biology finds most PD-MCI to be A-/T-/N- and only NfL/p-NfH significant. It measures no white-matter or vascular-metabolic variable, so it cannot itself name what does separate PD-MCI cross-sectionally.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: In Parkinson's disease MCI, the pair suggests - across two cohorts that each measured only one axis - that the vascular-metabolic axis need not be a proxy for underlying Alzheimer co-pathology: P-996 shows that periventricular WMH burden and plasma homocysteine are each independently associated with PD-MCI in 387 de novo PD patients (PWMH OR 5.162 [2.318-9.527]; Hcy OR 1.189 [1.071-1.405]) while never measuring amyloid or tau, and P-1001 shows in an independent Italian CSF series that most PD-MCI patients are amyloid-, tau- and neurodegeneration-negative, with only the NfL/p-NfH ratio separating PD-MCI from cognitively normal PD out of a ten-marker panel. Read together, the vascular-metabolic signal was found in one cohort (387 de novo PD in Chongqing, 50.4% MCI) and the largely negative AD biomarker profile in a different, smaller retrospective single-centre series (Perugia; 48 PD-MCI); no cohort measured both axes, so the inference that the vascular-metabolic signal is not an imaging shadow of AD pathology rests on cross-cohort exchangeability and is bounded accordingly - and the marker class that DOES carry prognostic information in PD-MCI (baseline p-tau, NfL, sTREM2 in the 30% who worsened at two years) is a different, prognostic axis from the one that separates cases cross-sectionally.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Decision: what to order for a patient with newly diagnosed or early Parkinson's disease who presents with cognitive complaints. The pair argues against routing that patient to an AD-biomarker workup (CSF amyloid/tau or amyloid PET) as the first-line explanation, because in the one corpus cohort where the full ATN panel was measured in PD-MCI most patients were A-/T-/N- and the panel returned a single significant marker. It argues instead for a vascular-metabolic workup - quantitative periventricular white-matter burden on the FLAIR sequence these patients already receive, plus fasting homocysteine, a cheap assay with a modifiable target in B-vitamin status. The population at stake is the substantial proportion of de novo PD patients who meet MDS Level-II MCI criteria at diagnosis, for whom an amyloid-negative result is currently read as a non-finding rather than as a redirection. The pair also warns against a second decision error: a negative cross-sectional CSF panel does not mean CSF is prognostically uninformative in this patient, because higher baseline p-tau, NfL and sTREM2 marked the 30% who lost points on both MMSE and MoCA within two years.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 2): Large vascular-metabolic PD-MCI signal is complemented by CSF evidence showing little AD co-pathology. Evaluation: Cross-cohort exchangeability bounded (Perugia A-/T-/N- rates applied to Chongqing; neither cohort measured both axes); unverifiable '~50% of de novo PD' prevalence removed from the implication (commonly cited de-novo rates are ~20-25%).

complementary_findings.finding_a: Supplies the cross-sectional arm at national scale: within a label already adjudicated normal by consensus at US Alzheimer's Disease Research Centers, prognostically distinct subgroups are recoverable from the neuropsychological battery itself, with a five-way progression ordering. Its stated causal story is clinician-dependence of the consensus diagnosis, and its stated missing piece is any biological anchoring of the clusters (no CSF, PET or amyloid entered the subtyping).
complementary_findings.finding_b: Supplies the longitudinal arm and the biological check from an independent dataset. It shows the same directional error - impairment under-called - arising from a purely psychometric source (retest gains on repeated testing), quantifies the reclassification (prevalence +9.2%, reverters 80 -> 57, dementia hazard ratio doubled), and reports the one biological measurement neither the consensus label nor P-1084's clusters have: 72.2% of the people the unadjusted scores called normal carried amyloid
complementary_findings.combined_insight: A normal cognitive result under-calls impairment in two independent ways, and the pair locates the fault in the test scores rather than in clinician error alone: P-1084's cross-sectional consensus under-detection and P-971's longitudinal practice-effect false reversion are two distinct failure modes, joined by the finding that de-subjectivising adjudication cannot remove the error. P-1084 shows that among 16,005 NACC participants already adjudicated cognitively normal, clustering the neuropsychological battery alone splits them into five subgroups with an ordered progression gradient (High-All < Low-WM = Low-Memory < aMCI < naMCI), and it attributes the missed cases to consensus diagnosis being clinician-dependent and variable across sites; it has no biomarker data and names 'which cluster assignments track biological (amyloid/tau) status' as its open question. P-971 produces the same directional error in a pipeline with no clinician judgment in it at all: in 329 ADNI MCI participants, adjusting the SCORES for practice effects raised 1-year MCI prevalence by 9.2%, cut reverters from 80 to 57, and doubled the hazard ratio for incident dementia - and 72.2% of those 'false reverters' were positive for at least one amyloid/tau biomarker. Neither paper alone shows that the under-calling survives the removal of clinician variability, and only P-971 supplies the biological check that P-1084 declares it lacks.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Decision: whether a normal or improved cognitive result closes the case - at memory-clinic follow-up, and at screening for prevention trials. The pair says it should not, for two reasons that require different remedies. For a first assessment returning 'cognitively normal', P-1084 shows the battery that produced that call also contains a recoverable risk gradient, so the profile across domains (not only the summary verdict) should be retained and re-reviewed rather than discarded. For a follow-up assessment showing improvement out of MCI, P-971 shows that a substantial share of such improvements are retest artefact and that roughly seven in ten of the people concerned carry amyloid or tau positivity in a research cohort, so 'reverted to normal' is not a discharge criterion and, in a prevention trial, is not a safe exclusion. The population at stake is the older adult told their cognition is normal or has recovered, in whom the conventional result is currently treated as reassurance. Notably the pair also tells services what will NOT fix this: harmonising or de-subjectivising the clinical adjudication, which is P-1084's own proposed remedy, cannot remove an error that P-971 reproduces with no clinician in the loop.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 1): Independent normal-label and practice-effect evidence converges on under-calling impairment. Evaluation: Headline reframed as two distinct failure modes (cross-sectional consensus under-detection vs longitudinal practice-effect false reversion); the narrower conclusion - de-subjectivising adjudication cannot remove the error - is retained.
