complementary_findings.finding_a: Contributes the stage-ordered status signature and the prognostic intent attached to it. 1H NMR of plasma, urine and saliva in 94 Brazilian participants (16 MCI, 30 AD, 48 controls); valine increases progressively control -> MCI -> AD and alanine is biphasic; the design is entirely cross-sectional and the authors themselves name validation of these signatures 'as progression biomarkers' as the next step. Plasma is the only biofluid with positive cross-validated predictive power (PLS-DA R2=0.72)
complementary_findings.finding_b: Contributes the test P-1220 cannot run. Paired plasma SOMAscan proteomics (3630 proteins) and Metabolon metabolomics (540 metabolites) on 800 EMIF-AD participants across 11 European cohorts, with 194 MCI followed for conversion (91 converters, 103 stable). It fits BOTH a multiclass NC/MCI/AD status model and a conversion model on the same plasma, and reports that the conversion features - tTau, alpha-synuclein, junctophilin-3, properdin, PI15, PPY, PLA2G1B, TEX29 - are features the status models did not select.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Stage-monotonicity is not a prognostic credential for a plasma molecular marker. P-1220 supplies a stage-ORDERED multi-biofluid metabolite signature (valine rising control < MCI < AD, alanine biphasic) from a comorbidity-free, ethnically mixed Brazilian cohort and offers it for progression monitoring, but never observes a conversion. P-1221 supplies the missing half in 800 EMIF-AD participants with follow-up: the 14 paired-omics features that actually predict which MCI patients convert (AUC 0.872) were 'features not selected by the multiclass models', i.e. status-grading and conversion-predicting molecules are DISJOINT sets in the same plasma of the same participants - disjoint in this pipeline; whether the disjointness is biological or methodological is unresolved, since the two model families were not fitted comparably (800 participants with EDAR splits vs 194 MCI with 12 clinical covariates concatenated onto the omics). Combined, the pair shows that the very property that makes a metabolite look prognostic - moving monotonically with clinical stage across the control-MCI-AD axis - is the property that carries no demonstrated transfer to who progresses. Neither paper can show this alone: P-1220 has no conversion endpoint, and P-1221 never builds or evaluates an ordered status signature.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: In a memory clinic, an MCI patient's plasma metabolite or omics panel reported as 'AD-stage-like' must not be used to counsel that patient about conversion risk, or to select or exclude them from a disease-modifying trial. The decision at stake is prognostic counselling and trial enrichment of an individual MCI patient on the strength of a cross-sectional molecular result. This pair shows the corpus supplies no plasma feature set that does both jobs: the only study measuring both axes in the same plasma found the conversion features to be ones the status models did not select. A stage-graded panel therefore needs its own conversion-endpoint validation before it enters a prognostic conversation, and its stage-ordering is not a substitute for that validation.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 1): Stage-ordered metabolites versus conversion-predictive features create a strong status-versus-prognosis distinction. Evaluation: Disjointness bounded as pipeline-level (the two model families were not fitted comparably; the biological-vs-methodological question is left open); finding-field truncations repaired.

complementary_findings.finding_a: Supplies the invasive-compartment arm and the substitution test against the strongest available comparator (the core AT(N) CSF panel), in a non-ADNI single-centre Norwegian cohort. Establishes that NfL genuinely separates converters, then that the substitution buys nothing - but reports the null without any quantity, and never tests addition.
complementary_findings.finding_b: Supplies the accessible-compartment arm, the ADDITION mode P-1240 explicitly left open, and the quantified deltas P-1240 lacks, in a large cross-validated ADNI analysis with nested model variants. It also supplies the modality ranking (MRI over plasma) that shows the small gain is not merely a small-sample artefact.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Neurofilament light separates MCI converters from non-converters at group level and then fails to demonstrate decision-level value in either fluid compartment or either test mode. P-1240 (135 participants, Trondheim, 24-month conversion) shows CSF NfL significantly lower in stable than converting aMCI (p=0.004), yet substituting NfL for T-tau in the core Abeta42/P-tau/T-tau model did not improve separation of stable versus converter aMCI - a null reported with no AUC, interval or model-comparison test, and therefore a failure to demonstrate improvement rather than a demonstrated nil; the paper logs addition ('not substitution') as its own open problem. P-1245 (ADNI, cross-validated) supplies the addition mode in plasma with quantified deltas: the plasma block lifts progression prediction in cognitively unimpaired people from C-index 0.68 to 0.72, but in the MCI stratum the combined model reaches 0.79 against 0.76 demographics and 0.77 MRI - a 0.03 gain at BLOCK level (NfL plus p-tau181 and Abeta42/40), with no NfL-only ablation reported, MRI outranking plasma in importance, and NfL merely the best of a weak plasma set. Because the CSF substitution failure occurred in the compartment with no dilution, peripheral contamination or assay-sensitivity excuse, the standard rescue for a disappointing plasma NfL result (blame the peripheral matrix, wait for a better assay) is not available for the substitution failure - a marker can fail substitution yet still add value in addition mode, so the CSF substitution null and the plasma block-level gain (0.03 C-index) bound different claims; whether NfL adds value in CSF addition remains the single untested cell, and the demonstrated role in this corpus is group-level disease activity, not individual risk stratification.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Decision: whether to order an NfL assay - lumbar or venous - for an individual MCI patient in order to refine that patient's progression risk. Population: MCI patients already characterised by demographics, cognitive testing and structural MRI, or already carrying a core CSF Abeta42/P-tau/T-tau result. Risk: on this pair's evidence the result should not be expected to move the individual's risk stratum. In the MCI stratum the entire multimodal upgrade over demographics is 0.03 C-index (P-1245), and against a core CSF panel the substitution is a documented null (P-1240) - so NfL's demonstrated role here is as a group-level disease-activity measure, and using it to set monitoring intensity, to counsel an individual patient about conversion, or to gate trial eligibility for one person is not supported by either the invasive or the accessible measurement route. The corresponding evidence request is narrow and answerable: run the ADDITION test in CSF (NfL on top of, not instead of, AT) and report an AUC delta with an interval - the single cell neither paper covers.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 2): CSF substitution-null and plasma addition evidence isolate a concrete unanswered NfL incremental-value question. Evaluation: Mode-mixing clause bounded: substitution failure and block-level addition are different tests, so the 'rescue not available' reading applies to the substitution null only; CSF addition remains the single untested cell.
complementary_findings.operator_caveat: Operator G4 required this caveat to appear as an explicit limitation in the manuscript text, not as a quality-flag footnote; the combined_insight / clinical_implication / human_evaluation_note above already carry it.

complementary_findings.finding_a: Supplies the structural half plus the molecular null, as a within-cohort head-to-head: the same 233 MCI participants, the same covariates (age, gender, education, MMSE), MRI regional volume against partial-volume-corrected Flortaucipir PET in nine a priori regions including Braak 5-6. Volume wins, tau contributes nothing. But its 305 healthy comparators were deliberately selected to be free of neuropsychiatric symptoms, so the design cannot ask whether the PCC signal belongs to the cognitive impairment process.
complementary_findings.finding_b: Supplies exactly the missing arm, in an independent single-centre Nanjing cohort with a four-group design (remitted geriatric depression, aMCI, comorbid RGD-aMCI, healthy comparisons, n=137, matched on age, gender and education). The PCC-seeded functional deficit is shared and ungraded by diagnosis - present in depression that carries no MCI - which removes the attribution P-770's design leaves open.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Two independent cohorts jointly show that a posterior-cingulate abnormality accompanying neuropsychiatric symptoms in MCI does not cleanly index the cognitive-impairment process, with the strength of the conclusion differing by modality. P-770 (233 ADNI-3 MCI participants; covariates age, gender, education, MMSE) shows bilateral posterior cingulate volume as the only independent predictor of total NPI burden while regional Flortaucipir tau across nine a priori regions is not significantly associated with NPI - a within-cohort structural-beats-tau result whose MCI-specificity cannot be tested because the healthy comparators were selected to be free of neuropsychiatric symptoms, and whose symptom-level constituents do not reproduce the global association (sub-analysis reported only as 'data not shown'). P-774 (137 analysed, four matched groups, Nanjing) shows PCC-seeded connectivity to bilateral medial superior frontal gyrus reduced at similar magnitude in remitted geriatric depression without MCI, in clinically defined aMCI without depression, and in their comorbidity, with no significant differences among the patient groups. Therefore, for the FUNCTIONAL measure, a PCC connectivity deficit in an MCI patient with a depression history cannot be uniquely attributed to the cognitive-impairment process - remitted depression alone reproduces it - and depression is the most prevalent NPS in P-770's MCI cohort (26.1 per cent). Whether the structural (volumetric) PCC-NPS association is likewise non-specific, and whether the connectivity deficit is tau-linked, remain open: P-774 performed no structural imaging and no tau PET, and P-770 performed no functional imaging.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: The decision is attribution in a memory clinic: when an MCI patient with depressive or other neuropsychiatric symptoms shows a posterior-cingulate abnormality on structural or resting-state imaging, whether to read it as evidence of AD-type neurodegeneration (and escalate to amyloid/tau workup or a disease-modifying-therapy discussion) or as a competing affective explanation. The combined evidence says the imaging finding does not discriminate: tau explains none of the symptom burden (P-770) and remitted depression alone reproduces the PCC connectivity deficit (P-774). The population affected is the large majority of NPS-positive MCI - 61.4 per cent of P-770's MCI participants had at least one neuropsychiatric symptom, depression the most common.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 2): Structural PCC association and functional PCC non-specificity are genuinely complementary, though modality transfer is imperfect. Evaluation: Accepted in narrowed (modality-qualified) form; the merge artifacts (duplicate fp-code entries, notes-vs-lens_pass contradiction) belonged to the candidate record and are not carried; '61.4 per cent' in the implication lacks an anchor - noted.

complementary_findings.finding_a: Supplies the disease-matched comparator and the only structural control in the pair. Beijing single-centre PD imaging cohort, 25 PD-MCI / 25 PD-NCI / 25 HC, whole-brain voxel-wise binarised degree centrality. Because the comparator is Parkinson's disease WITHOUT cognitive impairment rather than healthy controls, the increases cannot be explained by the disease itself, only by the cognitive impairment arising within it; and VBM of the two ROIs derived from the significant clusters returns no group difference.
complementary_findings.finding_b: Supplies the healthy-control contrast, the purity of direction, and the sign of the behavioural link. Locally recruited drug-naive MCI-LB sample (35 MCI-LB / 28 HC), striatal seed-based resting-state connectivity with multi-echo acquisition. Unlike P-729 the result set is not bidirectional: every significant between-group difference is an increase, and the paper reports no comparison in the opposite direction anywhere - so in this syndrome the reduction that AD-type MCI connectivity markers are expected to show is absent.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: In Lewy-body-spectrum prodromal cognitive impairment the resting-state functional signature runs in the direction OPPOSITE to the reduction expected from the amnestic/AD-type MCI literature, and it is not underwritten by regional atrophy. P-811 finds that the ONLY significant striato-cortical differences anywhere across three seed maps in drug-naive MCI with Lewy bodies versus healthy controls are INCREASES, with no region of reduced connectivity reported in any direction, and the increase is associated with better executive performance. P-729 adds the disease-matched comparator and the structural control: against Parkinson's patients WITHOUT cognitive impairment, PD-MCI shows increased degree centrality in left cuneus and both precunei alongside decreases elsewhere, while voxel-based morphometry of the two ROIs derived from the significant clusters (left FFG+cerebellum VI and left precuneus) finds no volume difference among the three groups (F = 1.914, P = 0.155; F = 2.780, P = 0.069) - a structural null that covers two of the five clusters only, not the whole increase set. Combined: the increase survives both a healthy-control and a disease-matched contrast, in two different syndromes and two different connectivity operationalisations, without a structural correlate.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: The population is prodromal Lewy-body disease - PD-MCI in movement-disorder clinics and MCI-LB in memory clinics - and the decision is whether a resting-state connectivity marker developed, thresholded and signed on amnestic/AD-type MCI (where the expected abnormality is a reduction) can be read at face value in these patients. In both papers the abnormality is at least partly, and in MCI-LB entirely, an increase, and in MCI-LB stronger connectivity accompanies better executive performance. A marker whose decision rule is 'less connectivity means worse' would therefore return a normal or falsely reassuring read in exactly the patients it is being applied to, and the direction of any such marker must be re-established within the Lewy-body spectrum before transfer.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 1): Two Lewy-body-spectrum studies jointly show increased connectivity plus absence of accompanying atrophy. Evaluation: VBM-coverage misattribution corrected in-insight (the structural null covers two of five clusters only, not 'those very clusters'); under-correction fragility (p-values not BH-robust across five clusters; ~3.5-year education gap unadjusted) noted.
complementary_findings.operator_caveat: Operator G4 required this caveat to appear as an explicit limitation in the manuscript text, not as a quality-flag footnote; the combined_insight / clinical_implication / human_evaluation_note above already carry it.

complementary_findings.finding_a: Supplies the group-conditionality and the temporal dissociation. Single-institution US cohort (99 at baseline, 25 aMCI / 74 CN; 63 at follow-up), whole-region normative volumetry via free FreeSurfer + NOMIS, built as a double negative control - three pre-nominated occipital control regions plus a cognitively normal control group. It is the only paper in the pair that measures the volume-memory correlation in NON-impaired people, and the only one that measures both volume and memory over time.
complementary_findings.finding_b: Supplies the within-group anatomy the whole-region design cannot resolve. Independent CBR-TLSA cohort in Bangalore, India (27 MCI / 36 healthy controls), FreeSurfer subfield segmentation. It demonstrates that 'atrophied' and 'memory-relevant' are different sets of structures inside the same hippocampus: reductions are bilateral and widespread, correlations with ACE-III memory are left-lateralised and limited to three subfields.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: The medial-temporal volume-to-memory correlation that underwrites volumetric reporting in MCI is doubly restricted and does not license individual monitoring. P-864 shows it is GROUP-CONDITIONAL: average Spearman rho .51 between AD-relevant volumes and episodic memory in aMCI against -.07 in cognitively normal controls, with the between-group difference formally tested and significant for hippocampus (p=.005), parahippocampus (p=.002) and amygdala (p=.010), and no volume-memory association in the pre-nominated control regions in either group. P-899 shows it is ANATOMICALLY NARROWER than the atrophy that surrounds it: reductions are bilateral across nine or more hippocampal subfields, yet the memory correlation is confined to three left-sided subfields (presubiculum, parasubiculum, GC-ML-DG; left presubiculum r=0.460, p=0.024). P-864 further shows the coupling does not translate into within-person tracking: over follow-up, hippocampal and entorhinal volumes declined in aMCI only (both group-by-time interaction p=.038) while memory change showed no group difference at all (p=.925, scores rising in both groups) - a signature consistent with a practice effect, so the null temporal dissociation may reflect instrument insensitivity rather than a true structure-cognition dissociation; and the subfield-level restriction rests on an uncorrected family of tests in small groups (n=27/36), so the left-lateralised narrowing could be a selection out of many tests.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: This bears directly on the product class P-864 was built to validate - automated normative volumetry reports (FreeSurfer + NOMIS as the free analogue of NeuroQuant/Neuroreader) now routinely returned to clinicians alongside a structural MRI in the workup of a memory complaint. The combined evidence says the volume-memory relationship those reports trade on is between-person, group-conditional and subfield-restricted, and does not support three uses a clinician is likely to make of it: a normal-range volumetric report in a cognitively normal older adult carries no information about that person's memory (rho -.07); a report of widespread bilateral subfield reduction is not by itself a memory-relevant finding, since only a left-sided subset tracks memory; and a serial volume decline must not be read as memory decline, because in the one cohort that measured both over time, volumes fell in the impaired group while memory scores rose in both groups.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 1): Group restriction, anatomical restriction and failed longitudinal tracking combine into a specific structural-cognitive boundary. Evaluation: Practice-effect alternative for the temporal clause and the uncorrected-subfield caveat surfaced in-insight; group-difference p-values (.005/.002/.010) lack quote anchors - noted.
complementary_findings.operator_caveat: Operator G4 required this caveat to appear as an explicit limitation in the manuscript text, not as a quality-flag footnote; the combined_insight / clinical_implication / human_evaluation_note above already carry it.

complementary_findings.finding_a: Shows what happens when the adjustment IS run: the routine scan's conversion signal does not survive the cognitive covariate, but its rate-of-decline signal does. This is the only study in the pair that reports two prognostic endpoints under one adjustment, so it is the source of the endpoint dissociation.
complementary_findings.finding_b: ADDS the second imaging physics (SPECT perfusion rather than structural volume), the second health system, and the only conversion figures in the pair that a clinic could act on (AUC 0.719, cutoff 1.22, proposed as triage for cholinesterase-inhibitor and disease-modifying-therapy decisions) - and adds the decisive fact that its own cohort already holds every variable needed to repeat P-1097's test, since CASI, MMSE, CDR-SB, Fazekas and MTA were collected on the same 86 patients.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Two memory clinics on two continents, using two different imaging physics on the same prognostic question, jointly point to an omitted covariate adjustment as the leading explanation for the null-vs-positive split while identifying the dataset in which it could be settled retrospectively - though the alternative (case mix and endpoint definition: P-1097 pools SCD+MCI transitions with no AUC; P-1107 is MCI-only at a 47% event rate) cannot be excluded, and P-1107's AUC 0.719/cutoff 1.22 were derived and applied in the same 86 patients (optimism). P-1097 (Oslo University Hospital, n=156 SCD/MCI, NeuroQuant automated structural volumetry) is the only study of the pair that enters the cheap cognitive score into the model, and doing so splits its two prognostic endpoints apart: the CONVERSION association is extinguished ('neither remained significantly associated with conversion after adjusting for MMSE-NR') while the RATE-of-decline association survives ('Both hippocampus volume and WBV were associated with progression measured by annual change in CDR-SB, in both unadjusted and adjusted analyses'). P-1107 (National Cheng Kung University Hospital, Taiwan, n=86 MCI, eZIS SPECT perfusion) supplies the second modality, the second continent and the deployable numbers - AUC 0.719 with a cutoff of 1.22 for 3-year conversion - but reports no such adjustment in its summary block, despite having collected 'cognitive-test scores (CASI, MMSE, CDR-SB)' and 'Fazekas and MTA scores' on the very same 86 patients; its stated open problem is whether eZIS predicts conversion beyond conventional MRI/hippocampal markers and generalises across sites, not incremental value beyond the cognitive score, so the omitted MMSE-family adjustment is this pair's observation rather than the paper's own declared gap.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: For the memory-clinic decision of whether to order automated MRI volumetry or an eZIS SPECT in order to answer an SCD/MCI patient's question 'will I convert?', the combined evidence does not support the scan adding to the MMSE-family score already recorded: the only cohort in which that comparison was run lost the conversion association entirely. What the pair does support is using the scan to counsel on the expected PACE of functional decline (annual CDR-SB), the endpoint that survived adjustment. This bears directly on P-1107's proposed use of the 1.22 eZIS severity cutoff as a triage gate for cholinesterase-inhibitor and disease-modifying-therapy decisions: on this evidence that gate has not been shown to reclassify anyone beyond the cognitive score, and using it to allocate an expensive therapy would be acting on an unadjusted association.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 1): Two clinics/modalities identify omitted MMSE adjustment as a specific unresolved imaging-prognosis issue. Evaluation: Headline bounded: case-mix/endpoint alternative (SCD+MCI pooled vs MCI-only at 47% events) and in-sample cutoff optimism (AUC 0.719/cutoff 1.22 derived and applied in the same 86 patients) now in-insight.
complementary_findings.operator_caveat: Operator G4 required this caveat to appear as an explicit limitation in the manuscript text, not as a quality-flag footnote; the combined_insight / clinical_implication / human_evaluation_note above already carry it.

complementary_findings.finding_a: Supplies the BOLD network-coupling channel, the multiple-comparison-corrected memory null tested across CN, MCI and AD, the upper stage boundary (no DMN-cognition association in AD), and the demonstration that the executive/language association survives WMH adjustment. It contributes the only AD arm in the pair and the only test of whether the coupling persists past MCI.
complementary_findings.finding_b: Supplies the independent perfusion channel (ASL CBF), a memory null obtained under a different model form (three-way and two-way interaction terms rather than main-effect association), the lower stage boundary (no CBF x VIQ interaction in cognitively unimpaired adults), and the cognitive-reserve moderator that grades the surviving fluency coupling. It contributes the only moderator and the only cognitively-unimpaired contrast in the pair.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: COMPLEMENTARY FINDING (haemodynamic MRI markers in MCI; memory vs non-memory domains), narrowed. In two ADNI samples analysed by different groups through physiologically distinct haemodynamic channels, the brain-measure-to-cognition association that survives is a non-memory one restricted to the MCI stage, while the memory test each paper actually ran returns null. P-1182 (rs-fMRI DMN connectivity; 61 CN / 68 MCI / 25 AD) finds no corrected DMN-memory association in any group, while anterior-posterior DMN coupling tracks executive and language performance in MCI only (null in CN and AD, surviving WMH adjustment). P-1242 (ASL CBF; 46 MCI / 101 CU) finds no CBF x VIQ interaction on memory, while CBF x VIQ interactions on category fluency appear in all four a priori regions in the MCI group only (null in CU), formally confirmed by three-way CBF x VIQ x status interactions. What the pair adds over either paper alone: the MCI-restricted non-memory coupling and the accompanying memory null recur across two measurement channels (BOLD network coupling vs arterial perfusion) and two model forms (main-effect association vs reserve moderation), and P-1242 supplies a cognitive-reserve moderator (VIQ) grading the surviving fluency coupling that P-1182 never models. NOT claimed: that memory coupling is absent from the perfusion channel in general (P-1242 tested and nulled only the VIQ-moderated form; a main-effect CBF-memory association is unreported), and not that the pair is needed to bound the coupling on both sides of MCI (P-1182 alone reports nulls in both CN and AD). Both samples are ADNI, whose MCI entry criteria restrict memory-score range, and no effect sizes are reported for any null, so this is convergence across measurement channels within one cohort family, not two independent replications.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Bears on whether a functional MRI marker - DMN connectivity or regional ASL perfusion - can be used in a memory clinic as a biomarker of the memory decline that defines amnestic MCI and that brings the patient to clinic. In both studies the memory association is precisely the one that fails, so neither marker can substitute for or corroborate memory-based staging; what they index is executive and language function, which is not what the referral question asks. The reserve moderation carries a second, patient-level consequence: because the CBF-fluency coupling is stronger at higher verbal IQ, the same regional perfusion value does not mean the same functional level in a high-premorbid-ability and a low-premorbid-ability MCI patient, so an untransformed regional CBF number should not be read to a patient as a severity index.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 2): Different haemodynamic measures narrow surviving cognition associations to MCI/non-memory coupling. Evaluation: Best self-bounding in the batch (in-insight 'NOT claimed' paragraph, including ADNI entry-criteria range restriction and one-cohort-family convergence); ADNI cohort-family non-independence flagged.

complementary_findings.finding_a: Supplies the selection half and the only non-ADNI, naturalistic, unselected memory-clinic evidence in the pair: three subgrouping rules applied head-to-head to ONE cohort of 792 select patients carrying three different pathologies (amyloid-42 positivity, medial temporal atrophy, white-matter hyperintensity burden). It also supplies the population P-1226 lacks - an unselected clinic including subjective cognitive impairment - and its own explicit statement that it validates no rule against any out-of-sample cohort.
complementary_findings.finding_b: Supplies the outcome half absent from P-1244: the conversion spread INSIDE a single biomarker-defined stratum (elevated florbetapir PET), and the demonstration that the quantity ordering that risk is a cognition-plus-hippocampal-volume index rather than the biomarker used to select the stratum. It supplies the only conversion endpoint, the only survival follow-up (mean 2.76 years) and the only quantified risk range in the pair.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: COMPLEMENTARY FINDING (biomarker-defined MCI subgroups in the memory clinic). P-1244 and P-1226 address the same clinical decision - how a memory clinic defines, and then acts on, a biomarker-labelled MCI subgroup - from opposite ends. ENTRY (P-1244; MemClin, 792 naturalistic Swedish multicentre memory-clinic patients, 142 SCI + 650 MCI, non-ADNI): which pathology a subgroup is enriched for is decided by the neuropsychological subgrouping rule applied, not by the patients - the inclusive rule captured CSF beta-amyloid-42-positive patients, the less inclusive rule captured high medial temporal lobe atrophy, and the data-driven rule captured high white-matter-hyperintensity burden - with no outcome by which any rule can be shown right, and no overlap or concordance statistic quantifying the divergence. EXIT (P-1226; 843 ADNI MCI, 220 with elevated florbetapir PET): once the amyloid rule has selected a group, prognosis within it is highly heterogeneous - IN-SAMPLE, with quartile cut-offs re-derived in the same ADNI data, conversion ran from 94.1 percent within two years at Cog_Vol < 101 to 0 of 42 over follow-up at Cog_Vol >= 340, ordered by a hippocampal-volume-to-ADAS13 ratio rather than by the amyloid status used to select the stratum, against the paper's own premise that only 40-55 percent of amyloid-elevated subjects convert. WHAT THE PAIR SHOWS AND NEITHER PAPER CAN: cognitive criteria and biomarker status do not stack as independent axes - the cognitive rule chooses which pathology the subgroup is enriched for (P-1244), and inside the amyloid stratum a cognition-plus-hippocampal-volume index, not the amyloid label, orders the risk (P-1226) - so 'amyloid-positive MCI' does not name a rule-independent population with a shared prognosis, and cognitive information contributes at both stages (as selection criteria at entry, as half the risk index at exit) while being treated as neutral background at each. SCOPE LIMITS ON THE FACE OF THE RECORD: the 94.1-to-0 spread is in-sample and cut-off-tuned, not externally validated, and the intermediate Cog_Vol band (102-266, ~60 percent risk) is not individually classifiable; P-1244's non-overlap is qualitative, with no concordance statistic; and the two arms operate at different layers (alternative subgroup-definition criteria vs a continuous index inside one fixed MCI definition), so the halves join at the level of the shared clinical decision, not as one quantity measured twice. P-1244 cannot reach the joint conclusion because it measures no outcome; P-1226 cannot because it never varies the selection rule.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: Bears directly on the memory-clinic decision to treat a CSF or PET amyloid result as a 'prodromal AD' label and act on it - what dementia risk to tell the patient, whether to refer for anti-amyloid therapy, and whether to enrol in a prevention trial. The pair says the label depends on which diagnostic rule the clinic happens to apply (P-1244) and, once applied, spans essentially the entire risk range in-sample - from near-certain conversion within two years to none within four, with quartile cut-offs re-derived in the same ADNI data, so the spread is not externally validated (P-1226). For the individual amyloid-positive MCI patient the prognostic conversation is therefore carried by hippocampal volume and the cognitive score, not by the amyloid result that triggered it; and for trial enrichment an amyloid-positive roster is heterogeneous enough that the recruited population changes materially depending on whether a cognition/volume index is applied on top of it.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 1): Same MCI-definition decision viewed through included and excluded patients reveals a substantive prognostic blind spot. Evaluation: Implication bound to the in-sample spread (quartile cut-offs re-derived in the same ADNI data; not externally validated); merge artifacts belonged to the candidate; P-1244 registry miscoding (modality_subtype='review_no_primary_data' on a 792-patient cohort) logged for pipeline audit.
complementary_findings.operator_caveat: Operator G4 required this caveat to appear as an explicit limitation in the manuscript text, not as a quality-flag footnote; the combined_insight / clinical_implication / human_evaluation_note above already carry it.

complementary_findings.finding_a: Supplies the positive discrimination figure (FSST time, AUC 0.825, Youden cut-off 15.11 s, within-MCI fallers vs non-fallers) and, in the same paper, the reason it cannot be read prognostically: falls were ascertained by 12-month recall and the FSST timed afterwards, in a cohort selected for memory impairment.
complementary_findings.finding_b: Supplies the outcome-ascertainment design P-709 lacks - prospectively recorded monthly fall calendars with telephone prompting - and returns a null in every cognitive stratum. It also independently confirms that gait speed does separate MCI and mild AD from preserved cognition cross-sectionally (0.89 and 0.86 vs 1.06 m/s, group effect p = 0.001, observed power 0.929), which localises its null to the falls target rather than to gait as an MCI marker.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: In MCI, the corpus's only positive mobility-based fall-discrimination figure is produced against RETROSPECTIVELY RECALLED falls, and the corpus's only PROSPECTIVELY ascertained test of a mobility marker against falls is null. P-709 reports the Four Square Step Test separating fallers from non-fallers within its MCI group at AUC 0.825 with a 15.11 s cut-off, on fall status obtained by 12-month recall in a sample selected for memory impairment. P-695 ascertained falls with monthly fall calendars and telephone prompting over six months and found its mobility measure did not discriminate fallers in any of the three cognitive strata (PrC p = 0.185, MCI p = 0.232, AD p = 0.528). Taken as a pair, the positive falls signal in this literature sits on the ascertainment method whose measurement error is generated by the very deficit that defines the population being screened - consistent with an ascertainment effect, though the pair also differs in predictor class (a single FSST balance measure vs six-month gait-speed change) and P-695 is underpowered (observed power 0.146), so the contrast cannot be isolated to ascertainment alone - and the ascertainment method that removes that error returns nothing. Neither paper alone can show this: P-709 concedes the retrospection but has no prospective comparator; P-695 has the prospective design but no positive result to set against it.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: This bears directly on falls-prevention triage in memory clinics and neurology outpatient services, where the decision is whom to refer for balance rehabilitation, home-hazard assessment or medication review. On this pair, the 15.11 s FSST threshold may be used to describe a patient's current dynamic balance and to detect change (its measurement properties are the sound part of P-709: SEM 0.63 s, MDC95 1.74 s), but it may not be used as a forward-looking fall-risk threshold for referral, because no corpus evidence links any mobility measure to falls that have not yet happened in this population. The asymmetry matters most in MCI specifically: recall-based fall histories are under-reported by people whose defining impairment is memory, so the same threshold applied to a memory-impaired patient carries an error the general-geriatrics literature that produced it does not.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 1): Retrospective positive fall association versus prospective null directly exposes ascertainment/design effects. Evaluation: Predictor-class confound (single FSST measure vs six-month gait-speed change) and P-695 underpowering (observed power 0.146) bound the claim in-insight ('consistent with ascertainment or predictor class').
complementary_findings.operator_caveat: Operator G4 required this caveat to appear as an explicit limitation in the manuscript text, not as a quality-flag footnote; the combined_insight / clinical_implication / human_evaluation_note above already carry it.

complementary_findings.finding_a: Supplies the cognitive-loading arm, as a clean within-participant dissociation in 30 MCI and 30 controls: the same walking test is null unloaded and separating under a concurrent cognitive demand. It is already a supporter of VF-25 for exactly this dissociation, and here it serves as the reference channel against which the second loading channel is compared.
complementary_findings.finding_b: Supplies the non-dual-task loading arm in 25 MCI and 30 controls: the load is put into the locomotor task itself (an oval path) under single-task conditions, and it recovers macro velocity and cadence separations that the straight-walking condition of the same 55 participants does not produce.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Two independent studies each run a within-participant contrast between an unloaded and a loaded walking condition, and in both the unloaded condition is null on the macro-level walking measure while the loaded condition separates MCI from controls - but they load the walk through different channels. P-687 loads it COGNITIVELY, with a concurrently administered and separately scored secondary task: single-task Timed Up and Go did not separate the groups (17.29 vs 17.60 s, p = 0.643) while dual-task TUG did (29.23 vs 24.92 s, p = 0.012). P-1082 adds no secondary task at all and loads the walk SPATIALLY, by changing the path: under single-task conditions, walking an oval separated MCI from controls on macro velocity (p = .007) and cadence (p = .018), where straight walking produced no significant macro marker at all. What the pair reveals, and neither paper can, is that the sensitising manipulation is substitutable at the macro level - re-shaping the locomotor task itself recovers the group separation that a plain overground walk misses, without requiring a separately scored cognitive task. P-687 has no non-dual-task loading condition and P-1082 has no dual-task condition, so neither study contains the comparison; it exists only across them. Caveats carried: the load-bearing p-values (p=.007/.018) come from an uncorrected family of ~100 tests (50 markers x 2 conditions) and would not survive Bonferroni correction across markers, and the 'curve more informative' claim rests on a marker count (27/50 vs 20/50) with no formal comparison.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: This bears on how a memory clinic or a community screening service should build a walking-based MCI screen when a plain overground walk is not discriminating. The pair says the sensitivity gain can be bought by changing the walking path rather than by layering on a secondary cognitive task, and in this population that difference is not cosmetic: a dual-task protocol requires a standardised secondary task whose own performance varies with the patient's cognition - in P-687 the MCI group's dual-task cognitive accuracy was numerically lower (70.00 percent versus 86.67 percent, chi-square 2.46, p = 0.117) while their walking time was longer - so dual-task cost blends the motor and cognitive channels and its interpretation depends on how the patient traded them off. A curved or oval path keeps the recorded score's content purely locomotor (no separately scored secondary task) while the manipulation itself plausibly loads cognition - which is likely why it sensitises - needs no secondary-task standardisation or scoring, and is deliverable with a floor marking. For services choosing between the two, the decision is which sensitising channel to standardise, not whether loading is needed.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 1): Two within-person loading paradigms converge on task-dependent mobility signal. Evaluation: Multiplicity surfaced (~100 uncorrected tests; p=.007/.018 not Bonferroni-robust across 50 markers); 'purely locomotor' corrected to content-locomotor/load-cognitive per P-1082's own caveat.
complementary_findings.operator_caveat: Operator G4 required this caveat to appear as an explicit limitation in the manuscript text, not as a quality-flag footnote; the combined_insight / clinical_implication / human_evaluation_note above already carry it.

complementary_findings.finding_a: OUTCOME ARM. Prospective 1687-person Taiwanese cohort (365 controls / 338 MCI / 984 AD) with death ascertained from the national death-certificate registry over 4.0-5.1 year mean follow-up. Establishes that the MCI diagnosis alone carries no excess mortality and that the excess sits with baseline neuropsychiatric burden. Has no imaging, no CSF and no molecular biomarker of any kind.
complementary_findings.finding_b: BIOLOGY ARM. Cross-sectional ADNI-3 analysis of 233 MCI plus 305 healthy comparisons with FreeSurfer regional volumes and partial-volume-corrected Flortaucipir SUVR in nine regions including Braak 5-6. Establishes that total NPI burden has an independent posterior-cingulate volumetric predictor, no tau predictor, and no individual-symptom correlate. Has no follow-up, no outcome and no survival endpoint.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: In MCI, the neuropsychiatric-symptom (NPI) burden - not the MCI label - is the dimension that carries prognostic weight, and that same burden has a grey-matter correlate but no tau correlate and no single-symptom correlate. P-755 supplies the outcome half: in a 1687-person Taiwanese three-hospital cohort linked to the national death registry, MCI as a diagnosis carried no excess mortality (22/338 MCI, 6.5 per cent, against 21/365 controls, 5.8 per cent), while inside MCI the baseline NPI-Q burden split separates a null hazard from a significant one (1.04 against 3.00 on the mood-domain split). P-770 supplies the biological half from an independent cohort: in 233 ADNI-3 MCI participants, bilateral posterior cingulate volume is the ONLY independent predictor of total NPI score after age, sex, education and MMSE, the parallel nine-region Flortaucipir tau model predicts NPI not at all, and none of the five most frequent individual symptoms correlates with those same volumes. What the pair establishes and neither paper can reach alone: the prognostically decisive dimension in MCI behaves as a NON-SPECIFIC AGGREGATE BURDEN - it is not indexed by the AD molecular marker used to stage MCI, and it is not reducible to any one symptom - so a tau-negative MCI patient with several mild neuropsychiatric symptoms is not a low-risk patient.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: In a memory clinic, an MCI patient screening positive on NPI/NPI-Q mood items should not be de-prioritised on the strength of a negative tau PET: NPI burden - not the MCI label - carried the mortality hazard (within-MCI mood-split HR 1.04 vs 3.00), and the aggregate NPI total rather than any single symptom item is the quantity to record. Caveats: only 22 MCI deaths underpin the split (lower CI adjacent to 1.0, no multiplicity correction across models x domains), and NPI-Q/NPI instrument equivalence is assumed, not demonstrated.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 2): Mortality and neuroanatomical evidence both show the MCI label can obscure NPI burden. Evaluation: Field swap applied: guidance (aggregate NPI total; do not de-prioritise on a negative tau PET) moved into clinical_implication with the 22-death fragility (lower CI adjacent to 1.0) and the NPI-Q/NPI instrument assumption carried.
complementary_findings.operator_caveat: Operator G4 required this caveat to appear as an explicit limitation in the manuscript text, not as a quality-flag footnote; the combined_insight / clinical_implication / human_evaluation_note above already carry it.

complementary_findings.finding_a: Supplies the detection end. A four-arm community contrast (normal 524 / osteoporosis alone 398 / sarcopenia alone 44 / co-occurring 92) in non-demented Chinese elders using AWGS 2019 sarcopenia plus forearm-DXA osteoporosis, in which the single-condition arms are null and only the joint exposure reaches significance.
complementary_findings.finding_b: Supplies the severity end. A memory-clinic cohort of 497 MCI and 684 AD outpatients at one Japanese national geriatrics centre, Asian (non-EWGSOP2) cut-points, in which sarcopenia and severe-sarcopenia prevalence both rise sharply from MCI to AD - a stratum P-828 does not contain, and a comparison P-828 cannot run because it excluded dementia.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Sarcopenia behaves as a severity-tracking comorbidity of cognitive impairment rather than as a case-finding signal for it, and the two halves of that statement sit in two different papers. At the community / normal-to-MCI boundary (P-828, 1058 non-demented Shanghai elders) neither sarcopenia alone nor osteoporosis alone raises the adjusted odds of screen-defined MCI; only the co-occurrence does, OR 2.29 (95% CI 1.17-4.48). Across the MCI-to-AD boundary inside a memory clinic (P-851, 1181 Japanese outpatients) sarcopenia prevalence roughly doubles with diagnosis (men 17.5% -> 30.2%, women 12.7% -> 23.8%) and severe sarcopenia rises about ten-fold in men and nearly four-fold in women (0.5%/1.0% -> 5.9%/3.7%). Neither cohort contains the other's contrast: P-828 has no dementia stratum and P-851 has no cognitively normal stratum.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: In community screening at the normal-to-MCI boundary, sarcopenia alone is not a usable case-finding signal (adjusted OR non-significant/underpowered at n=44 with 10 events, though raw prevalence is elevated), so case-finding effort should target the co-occurrence signal (OR 2.29) and severity-tracking within established impairment (prevalence roughly doubles MCI-to-AD); the MCI-to-AD gradient should be read with the age/MMSE confound in mind, since P-851 runs no diagnosis-adjusted analysis.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 2): Sarcopenia is null near MCI onset but severity-linked later; useful stage-dependent distinction. Evaluation: 'Null' corrected to non-significant/underpowered (OR pinned just below null, n=44/10 events, raw prevalence elevated); 'ten-fold' corrected to men-only; age/MMSE confound for the MCI-to-AD gradient flagged; meta-commentary implication replaced with guidance.
complementary_findings.operator_caveat: Operator G4 required this caveat to appear as an explicit limitation in the manuscript text, not as a quality-flag footnote; the combined_insight / clinical_implication / human_evaluation_note above already carry it.

complementary_findings.finding_a: Supplies the functional half: seed-based dorsal-striatal resting-state fMRI in 35 MCI-LB versus 28 healthy controls (CEITEC, Masaryk University, Brno, Czech Republic), where every significant effect is an increase and no region of reduced connectivity is reported. It also supplies the explicit statement that the dopaminergic substrate of that increase was never measured.
complementary_findings.finding_b: Supplies the molecular half that P-811 names as missing: automated 123I-FP-CIT specific binding ratios in 44 PSG-confirmed iRBD patients (Genoa, Italy), where the 14 iRBD-MCI patients show reduced nigro-putaminal and nigro-caudate binding versus the 30 iRBD-NC patients. Only the baseline group comparison is used here; the paper's four-predictor conversion model (sensitivity 90%, specificity 100%, accuracy 97.73%) is resubstitution performance and is flagged for authors_overclaim, so this record excludes it from the paired claim.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: In the Lewy-body prodrome, the emergence of MCI is accompanied by presynaptic nigrostriatal LOSS and by INCREASED striato-cortical functional coupling, and each half is held by a different paper. P-817 shows that within polysomnography-confirmed idiopathic REM sleep behaviour disorder it is the MCI subgroup that carries reduced nigro-putaminal and nigro-caudate DAT-SPECT binding relative to the cognitively normal iRBD patients. P-811 shows that in clinically diagnosed MCI with Lewy bodies the ONLY significant striato-cortical connectivity differences against controls run in the direction of more connectivity, and its authors cannot decide whether that increase is compensation or pathology spread. P-811's leading declared limitation is that it has no DAT imaging; P-817 is the corpus row that holds exactly that measurement in the same disease continuum.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: In the Lewy-body prodrome, an elevated striato-cortical functional signal should not be read as reassuring: it accompanies presynaptic nigrostriatal loss (DAT binding reduced in iRBD-MCI vs iRBD-NC) - the measurement P-811 names as missing - so DAT imaging is indicated when cognitive impairment emerges in the prodrome, and the loss-plus-increase pattern is the pair-level finding. Caveat: population adjacency is partial (McKeith-clinical MCI-LB without biomarker confirmation vs PSG-confirmed iRBD, a group that by P-817's own quoted base rate phenoconverts about half to parkinsonism and half to dementia - 5 DLB and 5 PD in this cohort, with all five DLB conversions arising in the iRBD-MCI subgroup), so 'same disease continuum' is an assumption; P-811's three dorsal-striatum clusters (59, 41 and 35 voxels) survive cluster-level FWE correction at p=0.003, 0.020 and 0.039 - the weakest near the 0.05 boundary - corrected within each seed map only with no correction across the three striatal seeds; the ~3.5-year education gap WAS regressed out in the between-group GLM, but depressive symptoms (GDS 4.25 vs 8.6, P 0.002) and daytime sleepiness (ESS 5.46 vs 7.97, P 0.006) differed between groups and were not modelled.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 1): DAT loss and increased connectivity provide complementary nigrostriatal readouts across prodromal Lewy-body disease. Evaluation: Truncated finding completed; population adjacency (McKeith-clinical MCI-LB without biomarker confirmation vs PSG-confirmed iRBD) and the p=0.039-within-seed-map fragility carried; guidance written for the implication.

complementary_findings.finding_a: Cross-sectional arm: three diagnostic algorithms applied to one racially diverse memory-centre sample, giving the case-count spread (44/53/41%), the agreement statistics, and the demographic composition of the actuarial-only surplus. It has no criterion-matched reversion outcome.
complementary_findings.finding_b: Longitudinal arm: two criteria applied to one Swedish population cohort with median ~7-year follow-up, giving criterion-matched reversion rates and post-reversion dementia hazards. It has no consensus-diagnosis comparator and no demographic-equity analysis.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: Neuropsychologically-operationalised MCI criteria (actuarial Jak/Bondi and the modified NP rule) were adopted to cut false positives, and two independent cohorts show the promise fails on both of its axes at once, in opposite directions of case-count. P-955 (Penn, n=354, three methods on the SAME participants) shows the actuarial rule labels MORE people than clinical consensus (53% vs 44%, LCA 41%), shows cross-method agreement the authors call substantial (kappa 0.80 consensus-LCA, 0.68 actuarial-consensus, 0.70 actuarial-LCA, so the actuarial rule agrees least), and its surplus cases are disproportionately Black. P-986 (Swedish GAS/SNAC, 5,804 examined, two criteria on the SAME cohort) shows the stricter NP rule - a modified version (two tests at 1 SD with the complaint retained; removing the complaint raises reversion to 54.7%) - labels FEWER people (987 vs 1,785 by Petersen) and still reverts slightly more over a median 7 years (48.3%, 95% CI 43.2-53.5 vs 43.4%, 95% CI 39.8-47.0; heavily overlapping intervals, so the difference is point-estimate-only). Combined: the false-positive burden the actuarial/NP family targets is not a function of how many people the rule labels - tightening or loosening the psychometric rule redistributes WHO carries the label without buying diagnostic stability.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: For a memory clinic or an MCI trial choosing its case definition: switching to an actuarial/NP neuropsychological rule to reduce false-positive enrolment is not supported by either cohort. In the racially diverse clinic sample the rule enlarged the labelled group by nine percentage points over consensus and its surplus fell disproportionately on Black participants, and in the population cohort the stricter version's smaller case set still reverted at 48.3% over a median seven years. Expect roughly four to five in ten labelled cases to revert whichever rule is used, and expect the choice of rule - not the patient - to determine borderline case status, with a demographic skew in who is affected.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 1): Independent criteria studies show disagreement in case counts and reversion, exposing an operationalisation effect. Evaluation: Kappa 'agrees least' reading corrected (the actuarial-LCA kappa is unprinted, so the minimum is not established by the printed numbers); overlapping CIs bound the reversion difference to point-estimate-only; modified-NP-rule/comparator mismatch surfaced.

complementary_findings.finding_a: Supplies the measurement side: what determines short-term practice-effect magnitude across intact, amnestic-MCI and mild-AD groups, and specifically that the determinant is baseline cognition/function, so the artefact is a systematic gradient rather than random noise. It reports no conversion or reversion outcome.
complementary_findings.finding_b: Supplies the clinical side: an annual-retest memory-clinic cohort in which reversion is graded 6.6-fold by baseline memory-impairment severity, and which uses that first-year reversion to argue for lighter follow-up in the milder stratum. It has no practice-effect adjustment.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: The stage gradient in MCI reversion runs in the same direction as the stage gradient in short-term retest gain, so severity-staged reversion rates are confounded by the very variable used to stage them. P-1004 (US, N=166 intact/aMCI/mild-AD, one-week retest, standardised regression-based change) establishes that practice-effect size is set by baseline COGNITIVE and FUNCTIONAL status rather than by demographics or comorbidity, with more impaired participants gaining less on retest. P-975 (Taipei memory clinic, N=564, annual retesting) reports first-year reversion of 32.8% in EMCI against 5% in LMCI (printed as 54/161 and 16/258, which do not exactly reproduce those rates and should be verified against the source) - a 6.6-fold gradient across a split defined by baseline memory-impairment severity, which is the same axis P-1004 shows governs retest gain. Combined: the milder stratum is simultaneously the stratum with the largest expected retest improvement and the stratum with the highest reversion, so no severity-staged reversion figure separates recovery from retest exposure until stage-specific practice-effect equations are applied. Neither paper can make this point alone: P-1004 has no conversion or reversion endpoint, and P-975 names the dependency without quantifying it. Two caveats bound the confound claim: P-1004's practice-effect gradient is measured at one-week retest while P-975's reversion gradient is annual, and practice effects decay with interval, so the confound could be materially smaller at twelve months; and P-975's EMCI first-year reverters show dementia-free survival indistinguishable from controls while LMCI reverters retain risk, a prognostic dissociation a uniform retest artefact would not obviously produce.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: For the memory-clinic decision P-975 explicitly recommends - using a single one-year retest to identify low-risk early-MCI patients and lighten their follow-up - the combined evidence says that decision is being made in the stratum where expected retest gain is largest, so an uncorrected annual retest is the weakest available basis for discharging or de-escalating an early-MCI patient. Clinics reporting or acting on stage-specific reversion rates should apply stage-specific practice-effect (standardised regression-based) corrections before treating a first-year reverter as recovered, and trials enriching on non-reverters should expect the milder stratum to be the one where the label is least stable.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 1): Practice-effect magnitude and stage-specific reversion align on the same severity axis; strong methodological complement. Evaluation: Count/denominator arithmetic (54/161 vs 32.8%; 16/258 vs 5%) flagged for source verification; interval-decay (one-week vs annual) and P-975's prognostic-dissociation counter-evidence added in-insight.

complementary_findings.finding_a: Psychometric arm at population scale: shows that the consensus 'normal cognition' label in a 16,005-participant multi-ADRC subsample decomposes into strata with different progression rates, so the clinical gate does not select a homogeneous low-risk group. It contains no CSF, PET or MRI in the subtyping.
complementary_findings.finding_b: Structural arm in the same transition: shows that in 97 cognitively healthy people followed 48 months, the field's two default structural markers are null for conversion while a subordinate amygdala subfield set separates converters. It performs no cognitive subtyping of the stable group and reports no discrimination metric.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: In the pre-MCI window, the two filters that jointly define a 'low-risk cognitively normal' participant - the consensus normal-cognition label and normal canonical structural MRI - are each uninformative, and the informative signal in each domain sits in a subordinate feature. P-1084 (NACC, 26,255 non-demented, 16,005 consensus-normal subsample) re-clusters the participants already labelled normal and recovers five strata with ordered progression (High-All < Low-WM = Low-Memory < aMCI < naMCI), with about 22% falling in Low-WM, 36% in Low-Memory and a further 25% clustering into aMCI/naMCI profiles - i.e. the normal label conceals, not excludes, elevated risk. P-1066 (ADNI-3, 97 cognitively healthy, 22 converting to MCI within 48 months) finds the baseline structural separator of converters is right-amygdala subfield volume (basolateral complex, AAA, CATA), while hippocampal volume and whole cortical thickness show no significant group difference in the same FDR-corrected analysis. Combined: a preclinical screening protocol that gates on consensus-normal cognition plus normal hippocampal/cortical volumetry is stacking two gates that each fail in this window, so it does not enrich for low risk; neither paper shows this alone because P-1084 has no imaging in its subtyping and P-1066 has no cognitive subtyping of its stable group.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: For preclinical AD trial enrichment and for prevention-clinic screening of cognitively normal older adults: a protocol that admits participants on a consensus normal-cognition label and excludes on normal hippocampal volume or cortical thickness is not selecting a low-risk group. In the NACC consensus-normal subsample the majority sat in clusters with elevated progression, and in ADNI-3 the healthy participants who converted within four years were structurally indistinguishable from those who did not on exactly those two measures. Enrichment at this stage needs either the psychometric substructure (working-memory and memory subclusters) or subordinate medial-temporal morphometry beyond whole-hippocampus volume; screening on the two conventional gates should not be counted as risk stratification when powering a prevention trial.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 1): Cognitive-label failure and canonical structural-MRI failure jointly show two conventional preclinical gates can fail together. Evaluation: Power bound noted: P-1066's null rests on 22 converters and would very likely miss a hippocampal effect of the size typically seen at this stage; the pair is also asymmetric in scale (16,005 vs 97) and the ADRC/ADNI samples are adjacent recruitment ecosystems, not independent populations.

complementary_findings.finding_a: Supplies the excluded-arm half: the same Winblad-vs-Jak/Bondi contrast applied as an MCI EXCLUSION rule inside one memory-clinic database, quantifying how much dementia incidence differs between the two residual SCD samples (age-adjusted IRR 3.7, 95% CI 1.5-9.3).
complementary_findings.finding_b: Supplies the admitted-arm half: the same two criteria applied as MCI INCLUSION rules in an independent population cohort over 12 years, showing comparable dementia risk and a difference confined to label stability (63.2% vs 43.2%).
complementary_findings.combined_insight: The prognostic consequence of choosing an MCI operationalisation lands almost entirely on the patients the criterion EXCLUDES, not on the patients it admits. WHAT B (P-1136, the admitted-arm paper) SHOWS: P-1136 applies Conventional (Petersen/Winblad) and Neuropsychological (Jak/Bondi) criteria to the same population-based Italian cohort (InveCe.Ab, n=1,021) and finds that the two criteria confer comparable 12-year dementia risk for the people they label MCI, differing only in how stable that label is over time (diagnostic consistency 63.2% vs 43.2%). WHAT A (P-1094, the excluded-arm paper) ADDS: P-1094 applies the SAME two named criteria sets to the same UK memory-clinic database (Essex, 1999-2023) as EXCLUSION rules, and compares the residual non-MCI (subjective cognitive decline) samples they leave behind: SCDJak/Bondi (n=185) versus SCDWinblad (n=86), age-adjusted dementia incidence rate ratio 3.7 (95% CI 1.5-9.3). WHAT THE COMBINATION REVEALS THAT NEITHER SHOWS ALONE: criteria choice is close to prognostically neutral inside the MCI label and 3.7-fold consequential outside it, so the standard reassurance that 'the criteria predict dementia equally well' is measured on the one arm where the choice does not matter. Each paper can only see one arm: P-1136 never analyses its non-MCI residual, and P-1094 never compares MCI arms. Caveats: P-1136's 'comparable risk of dementia over time' is reported without an equivalence margin, so it is an absence of a detected difference rather than demonstrated equivalence; P-1094's two SCD samples (n=86 and n=185) are small, come from a single memory-clinic database spanning a 24-year retrospective window (1999-2023) in which referral and diagnostic practice will have drifted, and are drawn from the same 2,233-patient database rather than being independent samples, and its IRR of 3.7 carries a wide CI (1.5-9.3). CLINICAL IMPLICATION: a memory service picking an MCI rule is not choosing between two equivalent prognostic instruments; it is choosing which patients get discharged or reassured as 'not MCI', and under one rule that reassured group carries nearly four times the dementia incidence of the other. Correspondingly, SCD cohorts and SCD trials that specify only 'MCI excluded' without naming the rule are not comparable to each other, and this incomparability is invisible in the MCI-arm prognostic literature that is usually cited to justify criteria choice.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: For a memory service picking an MCI rule, the choice is not between two equivalent prognostic instruments: it is choosing which patients get discharged or reassured as 'not MCI', and under the stricter rule that reassured group carries nearly four times the dementia incidence of the looser rule's residual (age-adjusted IRR 3.7, 95% CI 1.5-9.3 - a wide interval from small samples of 86 and 185 in one clinic over 1999-2023, with the 'comparable risk' equivalence in the MCI arm reported without a margin). SCD cohorts and trials that specify only 'MCI excluded' without naming the rule are therefore not comparable, and this incomparability is invisible in the MCI-arm prognostic literature usually cited to justify criteria choice.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 1): Same criteria applied to inclusion versus exclusion reveal that prognostic consequences can fall on the excluded group. Evaluation: A/B arm labels corrected to match the record's paper_a (P-1094) / paper_b (P-1136); marginless-equivalence ('comparable risk'), 24-year secular-drift and nested-SCD-samples caveats surfaced; guidance written for the implication.

complementary_findings.finding_a: Varies the rater while holding the instrument (ECog-12) and the cognitive stage fixed, giving the informant-versus-self corroboration multiplier at every stage of the AD spectrum, including the point where self-report loses all forward signal (dementia-stage HR 0.93).
complementary_findings.finding_b: Varies objective cognitive status while holding the rater fixed (self-reported NCGG-ADL), giving the impairment-versus-no-impairment corroboration multiplier and establishing that uncorroborated self-reported IADL limitation is not significantly prognostic on its own.
complementary_findings.combined_insight: A report of everyday functional decline is prognostic for dementia in proportion to how it is CORROBORATED, and the two available forms of corroboration - a second rater, and objective cognitive impairment - each multiply the hazard by roughly two- to three-fold on top of the uncorroborated self-report. WHAT A SHOWS: P-1109 holds the instrument and the cognitive stage fixed and varies the RATER. In approx 1,320 ADNI participants, the identical 12-item Everyday Cognition scale rated by the study partner rather than by the participant raises the hazard of CDR-SB worsening from 3.34 to 9.61 in the cognitively unimpaired, 1.44 to 2.82 in MCI and 0.93 to 1.82 in dementia, and the hazard of diagnostic conversion from 3.01 to 6.24 (CU->MCI) and 1.61 to 3.07 (MCI->dementia). WHAT B ADDS: P-1132 holds the rater fixed (self-report) and varies the OBJECTIVE COGNITIVE STATUS in an independent Japanese population cohort of 2,118 adults aged >=65: against unimpaired-and-unlimited, self-reported IADL limitation alone gives HR 1.53 (0.90-2.61, interval crossing 1), MCI without IADL limitation gives 1.87 (1.28-2.74), and the two together give 2.88 (1.65-5.03). WHAT THE COMBINATION REVEALS THAT NEITHER SHOWS ALONE: crossing the two designs completes a cell neither study fills. The uncorroborated self-report of everyday functional change in a cognitively unimpaired person is the floor of the whole system - non-significant in P-1132 and, at the dementia stage where the patient can no longer corroborate their own decline, actively signal-free in P-1109 (HR 0.93). Adding either an independent rater (P-1109) or objective cognitive impairment (P-1132) restores a hazard roughly 1.9 to 2.9 times larger, from two different countries, two different instruments and two different corroboration mechanisms. CLINICAL IMPLICATION: in community and primary-care dementia-risk triage, a patient's own report of everyday functional difficulty is not by itself an actionable risk signal and should not be used either to trigger a referral or to reassure. It becomes actionable when an informant confirms it, or when a brief objective cognitive assessment is abnormal - and the two studies together say that either route is sufficient, so services without routine informant access can substitute objective testing and vice versa.
complementary_findings.clinical_implication: In community and primary-care dementia-risk triage, a patient's own report of everyday functional difficulty is not by itself an actionable risk signal and should not be used either to trigger a referral or to reassure; it becomes actionable when an informant confirms it or a brief objective cognitive assessment is abnormal, and the two studies together indicate either route suffices, so services without routine informant access can substitute objective testing and vice versa. Caveat: the two 'corroboration multipliers' are not the same quantity (rater accuracy on one exposure vs partly the added risk of impairment in a joint exposure), and ADNI's informant availability is a study-design guarantee absent in primary care.
complementary_findings.human_evaluation_note: G4 ACCEPT (operator, Tier 1): Informant corroboration and objective cognition independently restore prognostic signal around self-reported function. Evaluation: Cleanest orthogonal-manipulation pair (rater-varied/status-fixed x status-varied/rater-fixed); 'the two corroboration multipliers are not the same quantity' caveat carried in the implication.
